title: Devin Bush, Colston Loveland on 'buying in' to Bears' culture | Press Conference
text: Deon, how was your first training camp here in Chicago? >> Say that one more time. >> How was your first training camp experience here at Chicago? >> It was good. Um, man, it was a competitive um camp. Uh, probably one of the competitive camps I had so far uh my career. Uh, it was real good work from both sides of the ball, even special teams. So, just learning a lot about the schemes and the team and everything like that. >> Talk about the way that you guys players have really been the term you use is devoted to to kind of the culture to taking everything they're coaching and working on it as players. M where does that come from as as a new guy kind of how did you catch on with that and sense what your teammates are are believing in as well? >> Yeah, I mean that's the big biggest thing about in this league is just buying in especially when you come into a new team, a new organization, a new group of guys uh you want to show those guys that you willing to you know follow before you lead and a guy you could they can lean on. So I mean u you know coming in new and and and falling into line and learning what the coaches are are teaching and applying that on the field is is huge. What's your interpretation of kind of what where the culture is right now and and what you what you jumped into from a team that had absolutely success last year? >> Uh so what you asking me like >> what how do you kind of interpret the culture that's in place right now that you're a part of here? >> Um obviously it's a winning culture. Um you know it's a culture that you know really I don't want to give too much information out for week one but um uh we hard knows. Um you know we going to play physical, we going to play fast, we going to play poised. Um but at at the same time, you know, we still got some ways to go before week one. Um and you know, early on in in this in this process, you know, we still developing and still, you know, hardening, you know, what that looks like, you know, realistically once we get through, you know, week one and week two and week three. >> Deon, one one training campaign, but what was it like covering and going against Coulson Lovelin for the summer? >> Great work. Um really really really good player. um development as a good player is going to be a good player in this league for for a long time for however long he wants to play. Um [clears throat] development for both of us. Um I'm giving him good looks. He giving me great looks. Uh we go do these joint practices and you know you come in off of you know going against Coulson you know weeks in a row and you get to see you know new players and you get to compare and you know bring new skills that you learn, new things that you you know develop going against a guy like Coulson and stuff like that. So it was good. >> What kind of challenges does it present? Man, he's he's one of those guys, man. He just he has a way of just catching that ball, dog. Like, he just I don't know. He's he's really good at at tracking the ball. He's really good at stemming his routes and getting to it getting to his points and um you like I said, bringing that ball in, man. He's he has a huge catch radius. You know, obviously his athleticism is is a bonus and you know, how how he's structured, how he's built, uh he's really tough to a real tough cover. what uh Dennis Allen asked you to do with his system. Is that similar to what you've been asked in the past or there some unique [clears throat] uh things that he >> It's a little little little hitches here and there. Uh but for the most part, I mean uh it's it's still football. Um you know, I got to find a way to apply my skill set to his scheme. Uh obviously that's with my speed and, you know, tracking the ball and making plays on the ball and and making you know, TFLs and sacks and stuff like that. You know, all that stuff is going to come. But, uh, I think it has a lot to do with me meshing with the guys and being able to play within the the scheme at the same time express my skill set as much as possible. Uh, so that was kind of like the whole journey throughout this whole camp and it's going to be something, you know, I'm continue to get better with week by week. >> As you go, >> how does Caleb Williams test you guys just in practice? >> His arm talent. Um, you know, the way he sees the field, way he sees the game, uh, his ability to, u extend plays, uh, is is huge. Um, and just the way he just what's the way he he carries himself, you know, he carries the offense. Uh, he's always looking ways to attack the defense, stretch the field, you know, make a play here and there. So, I mean, his his his IQ and his playmaking ability, you know, really gets us ready. >> From I think the last time we talked to you, you talked about how difficult he is to chase down. Um, >> from the first part of training camp to now, like what are the challenges in defending this team when they go in scramble drill mode and just like what he how proficient he is in that area? Yeah, it starts with him. Um, you know, once he once he gets rolling, you know, starts starts moving around that back field. I mean, any plays any play is possible, you know, whether he he chucks it 60 yards or he he dumps it off five yards. Uh, the guys he's dumping it off to, you know, he's hitting Swift in the flat or Manung guy in the flat, he's hitting Coulson or Luther or Rome, you know, who those guys are not guys you want to see with open field and the ball in their hands. So, I mean, guys like that and, you know, a bonus with Caleb is is tough tough to defend. >> Is he one of those quarterbacks where it's like no play is considered like a dead, >> right? Yeah, absolutely. He's definitely one of those quarterbacks. He's it's never really a broken play with him because it can just turn into a whole new play. >> With your chemistry with CJ, uh is it kind of equal how you guys communicate with each other? Does he kind of take the lead? How does that work between you two? >> Uh it's it's it's kind of like a like a ping pong game, uh you could say. Um you know, he's he's alerting things. I'm alerting things. you know, we talk about it after the play or during the play um of what how we see the game, what we see on on certain plays and you know, um we kind of just bounce off each other and just play off each other. Honestly, >> is it difficult to build chemistry and knowing that, you know, he's trying to work back to his full self? >> Yeah. >> Like does that affect the chemistry or >> not really anytime we we get a chance to get out in the field together is is opportunity to work on that. So, I mean, as much as we could uh he's as he's still progressing, you know, we more and more reps is only going to make us more and more better. What have you seen from DeAndre Swift out there on the field? >> Uh the same Swift he's always been. Uh man, I mean his his last name describes it all for real. For real. Uh really good between the tackles. Um really good in space. Uh play behind his pads, can make a guy miss open field. Uh good enough to run past you or through you. So uh he's he's one of those all-around backs for real. >> How would you assess this camp for yourself and for the team? >> Uh I thought we definitely got better. Um, I feel like I got better individually and most importantly as a team we got better. Um, kind of found our identity. Um, finishing, you know, uh, physical in the run game, in the pass game. Um, and just I felt like lasting longer. Um, you know, being able to practice at a long period of time, the way we practice, the live periods, I think that all helped us build a callus. [snorts] [clears throat] Um, obviously still we still got the rest of this week um to stack those days on top, but I feel like it was a good camp. A lot of lot of ways we can all improve for sure, especially heading into the season, but good start. >> Ben said that there was never a day he walked off the practice field where he felt like, you know, for especially for the offense, like man, that was really rough, like a step back, something like that. How different does that feel for you compared to last year? >> Yeah, a a lot different [snorts] for sure. um just as far as the operation, the details, the missed assignments, those I'm sure if you put them all up on a chart this year compared to last year would be a big difference. Um so that just helps the practice run a little smoother and then when you watch the tape it's like all right, we can actually see these plays and we can actually get plays off. Um so yeah, I think it was big. I think uh yeah, I think I think we we we did we did a good job this camp and second year in the offense, everyone as a whole has kind of grasped that and really ran with that. Caleb's doing a great job commanding the offense. Um yeah, ready to go. >> In light of that, how has Caleb's voice maybe gotten louder or his his intentional um efforts [clears throat] every day to get better? How has that impacted the rest of the group? >> Uh yeah, huge impact. Obviously, him being the lead of our team, the quarterback, everyone looks up to him. Um, and him just, you know, with anything, you build confidence over time. Um, and him being more confident, I think that spreads throughout the team for sure. And, you know, you could tell he's he's ready to go. >> Did you see how did you see the teams in Oh, go ahead. >> Does he seem Paul was saying he's full of joy? He looks a little bit and Ben described him as goofy in a loving way. Do you see that joy kind of come out in a little less serious than he was last year? >> Yeah, for sure. Yeah. letting his personality show a little more. Um, and that's good to see, you know, him just being himself out there. That makes guys want to, you know, hook on to him and really uh follow him and and do what he does and talk to him and I think he's doing a great job. Yeah. >> Um, when you guys went up against the Bengals and then against the Titans, I know nobody's game planning for these things. >> How did you see them try to deal with you in terms of who they put on you and how frustrated that might have made them? >> Yeah, I don't think it was anything too crazy. Um, like you said, we're not really game planning. So, it's a it's a scrimmage. It's a joint practice. So, kind of just doing whatever, but it didn't feel like, you know, a couple people saying like, "What's up?" And, you know, you're you're a good player. Maybe that, but nothing as far as in the scheme of the moment getting bracketed or doing something like that. So, >> you might had uh more firsthand experience going up against Dylan Feedman than really anybody else in this offense this camp. Where have you seen him grow from where he was uh say at the end of July to now? >> Yeah, a lot. Um he's always been on his stuff as far as playbook. I mean, he's got a great routine. I see him in there in the weight room before practice getting right. He does the same thing every single day. So, it's obviously not a question he's going to be he's going to be really good, but out there on the field as well. I mean, it shows up. Um I think I got a good I got him a good amount of times early on and then seeing him, but he was in position, you know, it was just like lay hands, whatever. and then kind of at the end of the end of camp him start making plays on the balls. It was cool to see. Um he's a great player, super fast, physical. Um he's grown so much throughout this camp. I'm excited to see him go out there on Sundays. Do >> you feel like there's been enough focus on install um you know just you know a week away from camp I mean from regular season give or take. >> Say that one more time. Sorry. >> Do you feel like there's been enough focus on the install the playbook and focus? Yeah, I think yeah, I I think so, but uh using this week as well to do that. And I think you can never be uh set as far as the playbook goes, especially throughout the season. It's going to be changing, you know. So, I think uh it's all it's all about the little things, the details, cuz that's the stuff where we get into the late weeks, late weeks of the season, we'll, you know, might start messing up some things. We're not in the exact spot, and we're kind of just overlooking stuff. So, I think it's important that we go through the whole playbook and we go over installs. Even though it sounds boring or we've done it before, I think it's good for everyone to to hear it. >> The biggest difference for you from year one to year two? >> I would say uh a lot of things. My body, uh my [sighs] my mindset as far as the playbook goes, uh relationship with teammates, coaches, I think everything's a little different. Um just more grown up, I'd say. Uh so, yeah, really looking forward to this year. It's going to be fun. Is there [snorts] any difference in the way that you prep? Like how you take notes, what you take note of? >> Um, this year to last year, you're saying? >> Sorry. >> Not necessarily. No. Um, really just writing down everything I can write down basically, but still being able to listen and, you know, hear what important notes I need to take. But really nothing and nothing's not important enough to write down, you know. So I kind of write everything

title: Ryan Poles: 'I feel really good' about talent on 53-man roster | Press Conference
text: I'll start off by thanking all the players um for their hard work, buy in uh this training camp, but those are really successful training camp, a lot of really good work. Um you can see the competition, joint practices here. Um and you could also see the team get closer together, which is was something Ben and I talked about from the beginning. When you have new players every year, it's a new team. Um spending time with each other, building those bonds, I think goes a long ways. U I want to thank all of our staff as well. Um whenever you have two away joint practices, that's a big undertaking. Um especially Kyle Kelly, Darby, and video um moving us from um Cincinnati to Nashville. You know, we had a really quick turnaround there um from that night game. They brought our servers. We were able to to really get after the film and prepare for the for the cut down day. Um and that was a huge help. So, I just want to make sure I said thank you to them. Um, obviously getting to 53 is always difficult. Um, as you get a more talented roster, it gets really difficult to make those tough decisions. Um, and it's really hard to have those kind of exit meetings as well. Guys you care about, guys that you saw fight um, and and not make it at the end of the day. We try to handle that process as as best we possibly can. I feel really good about the roster. Um, I love the depth. I love the talent. Um, this is probably the more versatile roster we've had. guys being able to play different positions which I think is going to really serve us well as we get into the season. Um couple things just uh transaction. So traded Dexter uh to Atlanta um for Clark Phillips in a fifth. Um that deal was more uh about timing than anything. Timing fit. Um you know we had some young guys really pushing um that came in this year with uh Jordan and and Loving. They did a really good job and um we felt like it was a good fit as we we moved forward. Um Jack Sanborn and and James Lynch will be back on the roster today. Um that move allowed us to put Kobe and Hayden Large uh down and remain flexible as we go through the season. Hopefully th those guys can make it back at some point on the back end of the season. So um that should work out well. reserve uh PUP. We got Shamar and Noah. They're they're close. We're doing a really good job with our performance team. Getting those guys ramped up in shape, ready to go so that when they play, they're they're ready to make an impact. Um and talked to those guys this morning. They're they're fired up to start that clock and get going. And uh and then Kyler is on that list as well. We'll see when he comes back. I don't have a timet. Um we'll see how that goes. And uh I do want to give a shout out to um our really our return to play protocol folks really Andre Tucker, Brent Salzar, Pierre um they've done an unbelievable job. I don't think I've had a a moment to talk since Azy's come back, but there's been plenty of guys that have come back this year that their hard work along with our players hard work has allowed them to come back and and become football players again and and be able to help our team and help our depth. um and and they've done a fabulous job and and that group um it's special. They care a lot. Um so to see success like that has been been really good. So I'll open up to questions from there. >> With Kyler, are you convinced he's going to play for you? >> I don't know. Um I would hope so. I still have hope there. Um he's going to have to continue to to work hard and and get back to playing football. when it it feels like there's a disconnect somehow. I mean, when I ask you, you know, whether a player is going to play for you at all, you say, "I don't know." What what specificity can you give us about what's going on here? >> Yeah, I really can't. Um, I think when people come back from injuries, there's different things that happen. Um, sometimes they they return fast, sometimes it's slow. So, it's really a timing thing and and a healing thing and confidence thing. Um, so I really don't I wish I did. Um, but we'll see. >> Is Kyler Is Kyler working with Is Kyler, >> sorry, is Kyler working with your staff here or is he working with with outside help? >> Yeah, he's he's working with our staff here. Um, you know, some of these guys, they also have, you know, other people that they work with, too. Um, yeah. >> Is there a difference between what he's reporting to you guys about his pain and discomfort versus how you all have assessed his injury? Um, I think listen, anytime you have an injury, and again, I'm not going to get all into the details of this. I really I wish I had more for you all, but anytime you have an injury and you're coming back from something, there's discomfort that you have to push through. Um, and that's what it comes down to. So, we haven't been able to get over that hump and we're not progressing as as as fast as we would like. So, that's really all I have to say about that. >> All right. with the Dexter deal. What was the thought process of obviously get weighing the return that you were getting with subtracting a starter that's been around for a while? >> Yeah, like I said, I think it really has to do with uh the room. Uh that room was highly competitive. Um those young guys started making a push when we got through camp and along with with obviously Grady Street and and Neville and we felt like the the timing made sense for us. So really it was it was about the shaping of the room and and really how well those young guys were doing too. So we feel really good and and confident in our talent level and the depth in that position. >> The vision for how Phillips fits in. >> Yeah. So uh definitely going to add depth to our our corner room. Um we like from the tape that we watched his man cover skills. Um short area quickness is really good. Speed's really good. Sticking coverage. Um so we're looking forward to getting him on boarded and and get going. safety and nickel have been kind of a a carousel uh through camp. What do you envision as a starting options at each spot? >> Yeah, I think there's a couple starting options. Uh I'm not going to really get into the depth chart. Um I think there's some strategy that goes along with that as we're going getting into Carolina now. Um but I think there's there's guys that are definitely capable of starting. Um you saw them during the preseason u whe whether it was Malik um playing nickel Xavier Cam u along with Dylan so it's a good room >> with with Clark Phillips is he outside >> were you going to try him in slot >> um we'll see you obviously just got here most of his tape in Atlanta was outside in college he was inside I like what that tape looked like too so I think he's capable of both um but since he's been in the league he's been outside so um we'll see where we start him off and go from there. >> With with Azie, how do you what do you guys need to see to know he'll be game ready? >> Yeah. Uh practice. I think the big advantage of him um coming back when he did, which I still think is amazing, um is is really the padded practices, uh team periods, um really testing his, you know, anchor mobility, all that stuff. So, obviously in helmets or not even a helmet, it looks it looks fabulous or he wouldn't be where he is. Um, but it's playing football. There's definitely rust to knock off. I don't know how long that'll take before he's he's, you know, involved with the game plan and starting or um, a rotational guy or active. Um, it's too early to tell right now. But the beautiful thing is again when he got back, one of our big concerns is how many padded practices could he get before because once we get going here, those start to to drop off. Um, and we got plenty of like short weeks that we got to deal with this year, too. So, we'll get through those padded practices and see how he holds up. Right. Wouldn't you see enough of from Karan Amagaji? >> Yeah. Um, again, I would go back to the room and the competition. Um, had good conversation with him at the end. Uh, really just wasn't a a level of consistency that we were looking for. >> How do you feel about the way that left tackle depth looks while you're waiting for Azie? And very similar to the same feeling you had going into last year. >> Yeah, I think we feel a little bit better. Just Braxton's way healthier than he was last year. Um I don't know if he was completely himself last year. So um he's in a better place. Uh Theo has a bunch of games under his belt too. Um and then obviously when Aussiey's ready, he's he's started a bunch of big games himself. So we feel good about it. >> You had had confidence in that defensive line in the pass rush going into this camp. As you come away from it now, obviously being willing to move on with a guy like Dexter because of what you see coming on there. Like what's your confidence and belief in that group as you look to this season? Yeah, I I have a ton of confidence in those guys. Um I think they did a good job this preseason. Um I still think it's a unit that's going to have to work together. Um whether it's it's our blitz packages or the twists and games that we play. Um those guys bring it. They have really good motors. Um and they have the skill set to to get into the back field and and get some pressure on the quarterback. Um and again, the defense is going to have to play as as one unit, and I think that's important. >> Do you think Booker will be ready for week one? >> Uh I'm not sure yet. We'll get through this week. Um, again, this week zero is it's always good to have. We'll get through these next three days and be able to assess and see if he's ready to go. >> Ryan, more of a more of a big picture question for you. I'm just wondering like everyone in this league understands that not every acquisition is going to work out whether draft free agency. Do you feel like as you've >> progressed in this job that you've gotten more comfortable with, you know, acknowledging when those situations just are working and moving on quicker than maybe in the past? I think I've been pretty quick to, you know, if there's if there's something that doesn't work out, um I think we're pretty good at being honest about that and moving on. I don't think we're an organization or I'm a GM that is going to hold on just because it was u a draft pick or a trade that you made and now I got to make it work and we're just going to keep that player here when it's not working like that. It'll hurt the team. I think I've mentioned before um the locker room always knows. Um, so we hold true to that and um, we want to put the best group together regardless of how they're acquired. Now, is there a time uh, frame in terms of developing that we believe in? If we saw something, we're going to try to exhaust that. Um, but again, it's about the best 53. So, um, at some point, you got to move on and, uh, and help your roster out. >> You thought you thought anything connected maybe with the some of those higher picks that haven't worked out. What have you maybe learned from the the process of having to move out from a bunch of those guys? >> Yeah, we've uh I think I talked about that too. Uh we do after action on all these guys, whether they they hit and they're starters or the backups or they don't. Um and then we research on why did it not work out? Uh is it body type? Is it makeup that we missed? Um is it the system that we're in? There's a lot of different pieces that you got to go through. Um, and I think you've you've all seen every year just gets better and better and better. Um, I actually think we've been really good at our top picks. I think you also have to research what's the expectation um at one at 2, A3, A4, A5, A6, at seven. Um, and then I mean even if you look across the board, um, our UFAs that we've hit, our late round picks, um, Kyle, uh, UFAS, um, Tyson, Theo, um, Jade Day. Um, so I think we've done a really good job. Um, but we do research that and we look into it and I think you got to be honest with yourself of what works, what doesn't work, and just keep trying to tighten the screws on your process. So I think we've done a good job. You obviously you obviously took the North last year outside of presumed player development. Is there an area or a particular acquisitions that give you confidence that you've done enough to make sure you never give it back? >> Uh I don't think I'm ever comfortable with it with anything. Um we're always like I just said, we're always trying to get our get our process to be as perfect as it possibly can be. um and really focus on that more than the outcome. That's the goal. But if we can continue to develop players, we can continue to bring in the right players in and this amazing co coaching staff that we have them keep coaching these guys up. We'll put oursel in position to do that year in and year out. for you as as a as an evaluating staff, what have you learned about the way the process you go by seeing through this talent and how this coaching staff has enhanced developing these guys, what they can do for maximizing these guys potential? >> Yeah, I think there's alignment with the vision of who the player is, how they can help us, and then it's the follow through. Um, we have a pretty in-depth process where we really attack the coaches are attacking the tactical side of it and then our support staff is hitting, you know, we call it habits and headsp space to make sure these guys are in a good spot. Uh, they know how to prepare, they know how to go through the season. Our rookies go through it. The last two classes have gone through this process. Um, and then the physical part from the performance team to make sure that they're developing physically, getting stronger, faster, and really tying in, uh, some of the tactical things that they have to improve to improve on with the physical to make sure everything's aligned and moving forward. So, um, I think that alignment, uh, communication and and the buyin has been huge for us. >> Can you talk about >> Can you talk about the roster balance? Why you went with like five receivers versus four tight ends? just kind of the overall big picture of how you constructed this 53. >> Yeah, we're gonna be here for a long time if I go through that. That's really what the last I mean you're doing it weekly. Um but the last three four days going into cutdowns, that's that's what you're doing. Um obviously it's there's a talent level threshold. Um and you might be saying, okay, is it going to be a fourth tight end or a sixth receiver or a 10th lineman? um six corner. Um so you're you're really kind of comparing where guys are at. Um there's a short-term and long-term game that you're also playing to make sure that you're set up, you know, into the future as well, but obviously, you know, you're doing everything to win now. Um that's a long process that that we're going through to make sure it all works. Um you're also trying to gauge who's who who can make it to the practice squad, who can't make it to the practice squad. I think if you continue to do a good job, you know, at some point other teams are going to see that you have talent that they like. Um that maybe that 11th lineman you can't keep and you got to expose them to waiverss and and they go elsewhere. So, um pretty in-depth process. Um again, making sure we're aligned with our coaching staff. Um and really the other thing too is like you got to play the active game. Who's going to be up? Who's going to be down? That goes into it as well. >> What do you think about watching Ben run training camp his second year and how this group has come together? Yeah, I just, you know, anytime you have a new coaching staff, um, like it was last year, you're sitting there watching the guys trying to figure out, are they going to buy into this this new way, these guys were locked in from the beginning. So, um, I thought Ben did a great job with the schedule. He's got a great feel for where the team is at mentally. uh when he's got to challenge, when he's got to make it fun, um when we got to take time to spend, you know, with each other like that the joint practices we talked about. We had position groups going out to dinner together that was organized, uh food trucks at the hotel in Cincinnati. Um he's got a great feel for the guys now and um it's really impressive to watch. Jason Dan >> Ryan, what have you thought of DeAndre Swift's >> changes that he's made, adjustments that he's made over the past year or so and with him being in the last year of his contract, what's your outlook for him long term? >> Yeah, it's definitely something we need to look at. Um, and we will look at I think he's done a great job. I love his approach this offseason. U, he looks amazing. Second year in the system, too. I think the combinations of having EB and Studsville uh has been awesome for him. Um, so I like where he's at right now. Um, this is where this job gets tough is is really trying to figure out how you want to allocate everything, not only for now, but into the future. Um, so we'll have those conversations and and see where we want to go with it. But I love Swifty. I love the way that he's working. >> You mentioned Jamar off the jump. What's your short-term vision and timetable for for where he's at as the regular season begins? >> Yeah. Um, like I said, just had a conversation with with him and our performance team. He's trending in a really positive direction. Uh, he's already doing position work off to the side. We'll simulate um some individual and and practice type things um to get him prepared mentally, physically, and and his endurance needs to continue to improve. Uh but he's working his butt off. Uh, I would imagine him being back at some point here, um, when he gets through this this little last phase of his rehab. And then from there, like we talked about, um, you know, these guys get will get weeks three and four to start practicing before they're actually active to go. Um, knocking that rust off and and becoming a football player. um starting to get that short area quickness and and and really being able to react and have the instincts come back, especially in, you know, playing defensive line that you're getting hit from every different direction. So, uh just not going to rust off, getting the instincts going. When that happens, it'll it'll be great. We'll get him back out there, but I'm not exactly sure when that all is going to come together. >> Right. With camp now over, how do you feel about what you saw from Caleb? And then second, how do you feel about the the collection of talent that you built around him this past couple years? >> Yeah, I I love where he's at. Um I know Ben's talk to you guys probably more in detail. Um but what I see is I see joy. Um I think the the first year, you know, there's he was white knuckling, you know, the whole time trying to figure it out. Um try to doing it right. Um and he continues to do that, wanting to do it right. But I think you see that that joy back in his game uh where he's playing free. I think he um sees and identifies where he comes up short faster than what he did before. Um and I think that's where him and Ben will are continuing to work really well together. Um trying to get better every every single day. Um in terms of the talent, I feel really good. Um there's playmakers all around. title: DL Andrew Billings Press Conference 9.1.26| AZ Cardinals
text: Mike said he was going to put you guys through a tough one today. Was it a tough one today? >> It was it was it was pretty tough, but we got through it. >> [sighs] >> How do you How do you kind of see this this defense panning out now that we're to the regular season and you guys have a better idea who's going to be in the room? >> Uh panning out is like as far as I >> How you guys coming together and >> Yeah, I don't know. It's just coming together pretty good. Playbook's coming together, which is probably most important. Uh I think I think it'll be uh good to see week one. There's going to be a couple of hiccups as always, but uh I think overall we will get on the same page as a defense and once that happens, nothing nothing's going to stop us. >> The pairing of you and Roy as those nose tackles, how do you guys feel like you guys compliment one another? >> Well, you got Roy. He's a quick one. He's going to You you're not going to know where he is at. Me, you come at me if you want to. I'm just I'm just going to run through you. And so I think uh it's a lot of different things they're going to have to deal with. Um I think uh most of all is just we're going to be fresh legs and we both want to be uh knowledgeable of what we what we need to get done. >> You mentioned Roy. What's it like to have a a teammate like that, a guy that's, you know, good practice player, good locker room guy, always seems to have a positive attitude, not afraid to, you know, take on two guys to open up something for somebody else? >> No, it's a very important. I mean, that's uh you know, you're not going to you're not going to hear about it much, but that's what makes the defense work. So, I mean, having a dude like that, without him, other dudes wouldn't be who they are. So, man, that's the honest truth. >> What have you seen out of a guy like Walter? >> Man, [snorts] he's just uh he's sneakily a freak of nature. I don't know I can't describe I never seen nobody like him before, man. It's a very athletic for his size. I mean, good bend. He he he's knowledgeable of football, which helps him even more cuz he's not just doing what he wants to do. He's doing things in the framework of the defense, but he's doing them at such a crazy speed and such a crazy angle that, you know, I don't I don't know who can block him. Honestly. >> Why is he so big because he's so good? >> Uh because he you know, you look at dudes like you know, Aaron Donald and stuff. You see how they're built. It's like, oh yeah, yeah, I get it. You see Walt, he's just like, uh I don't know what you can do. And then he puts the pads on. It's like, whoa. You know, it's like it's it's kind of crazy, honestly. >> Do you hear I mean obviously you probably aren't going to put yourself necessarily in that category, but I mean even at your size, like you're to get to this level, you have an athleticism that most people most normal human beings aren't going to have. Do you Do you consider yourself Do you think of yourself in that way? >> Of course. Probably probably way too much. I'm I'm probably got a big head on that one. Sure, I think I can I think I'm I can just do everything, but uh realistically, yeah, no, I I've some yeah, you work at it. Grew up big, so you know, I just I hold it well and work with it well. >> Do you sense when you're going up against some offense tackles maybe during the joint practice where they're just like, man, this guy is >> Yeah, they they they stare at you and when they're in the huddle they just start looking and then you line up and they're like, oh tap in the center. What we got here? Stuff like that, you know. >> So, would you put yourself in the same boat as Walt? >> Uh >> nah, not really. Uh I don't think dudes expect what what Walt has. I mean, people expect me to run through their face. That's why they they jump set me or double team me. Uh Walt Walt just brings something different. Yeah, I think as season goes along he's going to get doubled more than anybody's It is what it is, but they'll figure it out as they probably always do. >> So much of the talk throughout this off season has been about the defensive front and expecting and wanting more from that unit. You sitting in those position rooms, is there a chip on the shoulder of the guys in there? Or like what are some of the conversations? Do you guys feel kind of that attention or that pressure? >> Uh I mean, yeah, I mean that's but that's I mean that's NFL. We can walk in the room every year with that pressure on us. As defensive line we are the front of the defense. Whatever we do the defense is going to go. We We're not doing good the defense ain't going to do good. I mean rush coverage we're all part of that run game. We're really front line of that. So it's always that pressure. As far as what happened last year I think we cleared that. Moving on to the next. This is a new year. New new room new team so it's time to just just get better every day. >> What do you What do you like out of Darius Robinson and and what kind of relationship do you have with him? >> A good relationship with D-Rob. I mean what I like about him is just his get off. His strength. He's a He's a tall longer guy and usually they're they're not the strongest on the team but he's pretty damn strong. I worked out with him uh yesterday he he he really can bring it. I like that he has good pad level for tall guys as well. >> You talked about your last season and whatever and it's over. Do you have the same type of mentality with the preseason and like you know whatever happened in the preseason score wise you already what you guys give up with it and said that you know the preseason is kind of for the regular season. >> Oh yeah 100%. Preseason is way different regular season. I mean preseason is important dudes are trying to you know earn spots on whatever team they end up going to or here. Uh but you know when the season comes there's no uh this record counts. You know what I mean? It counts. And usually by week eight you kind of know where you stand. So you got to get rolling fast. >> Do you feel like the first practice is after cut down day is kind of a a shock or it looks kind of empty compared to what it was during camp? Like what's it like for a player not to have 37 other guys? >> Uh here it it probably sucks. Um I know I know the coaches feel it too. You know you you're out here grinding with these dudes you kind of build a relationship break bread and all that but uh you know when you come back in the room it's going to be empty. You know it's only 53 dudes are going to make it. So uh it's part of the process um but you do hope those guys find somewhere else and typically you know if they perform during the preseason they do and that's what makes it so important. >> You talked about wiping the slate clean from last year. As an outside addition is that something you consciously wanted to bring to this team or do you feel like that kind of just naturally happens year after year? >> Uh for me, I think I think it naturally happens year after year. I mean, it's uh it's actually probably harder to do once you make it to the playoffs or the Super Bowl to wipe that slate clean. That that sticks to you more so than a losing season. So, uh it I think it naturally happens, but it's something you do have to work at. It's not just You don't just wake up and like computer just wipe it, but yeah. >> Do you Do you like playing the role of mentor when that is asked of you? Do you like giving advice? Do you Do you feel that or do you would you rather just be I'm just one of the guys. If you need help, that's great, but just because I'm a veteran, I don't You don't necessarily need to come to me. How do you How do you kind of approach that? >> [snorts] >> I mean, it's it's a little bit of mixture of both. I'm not a loud guys. I'm not going to, you know, come up to you, but uh if you come up to me, I'll talk. I mean, if I got a question, I'll ask, too. So, it's not a nothing I'm trying to hide from or walk away from these guys or not help them. I I I just want dudes to succeed and have a great career.

title: RB Bam Knight Press Conference 9.1.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: I know you talked to before about having, you know, interaction and and some time with Mike earlier. I know earlier today he was like, "That's a long time ago." Like how how what was it like when you first showed up? Did it feel like there was just somebody that you were with for a brief amount of time or do you do you feel like you have a connection? >> I feel like I have a connection with him cuz in New York, obviously, as an undrafted free agent, I had opportunity to play a little bit like kind of halfway through the season and I excelled good in his system. So, at the time he got the job, I was still technically a free agent this past off season, so couldn't really reach out to him until I had confirmation whether or not I was coming back, but once I did, like I knew I was in a good center with him, coach Hack, and then Goby as special teams coach. Like I was with all those guys with the Jets, so I knew I was in good hands with them. >> What have been some of the biggest differences you noticed out of those guys coming back? >> Uh I would say, I mean, obviously, it's different roles for everybody now. So, like it's definitely more you could tell their demeanor as far as them trying to flip this organization. And I think it's going in the right direction. Everybody's buying in, so that's been a positive. >> With with all the running backs that were in your room when you did come back, and obviously that was before the draft and all that stuff, but like did it feel any more comfortable than you had to go what you went through last year or >> with all the people, was it still >> I would say this year it felt like it was definitely deeper a deeper as far as from the running back perspective. I feel like last year it was a little bit more, you know, versatile guys, guys that could do special teams and that, but I just feel like just from a running back standpoint this year, it was crazy amount of talent. Like you saw Corey Cannon, he got traded, they traded for him, Evan Hall, he flashed, even like Trey, like him in training camp, like he when he flashed when he was at practice. So, everybody has a good idea and can be successful in this scheme. It's just a matter of kind of bringing all that together. And so, I do think we have a great room and we did pre-uh training camp. >> Did it make it harder for you then on a personal level? I want to say no cuz I feel like I guess somewhat had an advantage cuz I am familiar with their system, offensive system. So, I feel like a lot of the run game and stuff was clicking a lot for me earlier on. But like I said, we did have a lot of good backs in the room. So, I don't feel like it put me at too much of an advantage, but I do feel like just having some familiarity with the system kind of did help me catch on a lot quicker than maybe some of the other guys. >> I know there's never a point where you could get too comfortable, especially during this training camp time of year. But was there a moment where you were like, all right, I I do believe I have a spot on this 53 and I might be a part of this? >> Uh I want to say no. And that's that's the honest answer cuz like one thing I've learned in this league, like I've been cut three times, like nothing is ever certain. Unless you're a first, second round pick, like nothing is ever certain. Even sometimes then, like you see guys get released. So, I try not to, you know, obviously I didn't play too much during the preseason. So, that I had a general idea, but like I didn't want to get comfortable and start saying, "Yeah, I'm on the team." Cuz like I said, anything could happen. They could have claimed somebody or something like that. Like you never know. >> Working through those thoughts in your head right there in the back of your head, usually the sign, a good sign, but I've been cut three times before and I don't know if I'm on this team. Like how >> Uh I mean, honestly, it just comes with experience. Like I've been through every situation. So, like you kind of learn to deal with it versus guys who've never been through that. Like I'd say like some guys who's going through it for the first time now with first cuts that just happened. Like they're probably experiencing, like they don't know how to feel right now. But I've been through that. So, like I know how to deal with it. I know how to come back stronger. I know how to just keep doing my thing throughout that. >> You talk about, you know, the the talent in that room and you know, people flashing. What what you see with with Jeremiah Love did, you know, so soon, you know, when when he first got his actual look over to you by when you see the skills that that he has. >> It's it definitely caught me off guard. I'm like, this guy looks good. Cuz like I just feel like even with his college tape, like it doesn't do it justice. Just seeing like how he move in between the tackles, even in individual drills. I'm like, dang. Like it's it's definitely stands out. And you know, I think the media and kind of pre-draft evaluation was was right. Like he's that type of player. He could be a guy that can change the franchise for sure. >> I know that Mike isn't going to sit here and say we did really well in the off season in the preseason with offense because it's preseason. >> Mhm. >> But at the same time you've been around this enough times. Like what is your gut feeling of what this offense can do when it counts? >> I mean honestly, like people saw it in preseason. Like the fact that you had guys, you know, essentially at the bottom of the roster out there playing and still creating explosive consistently every week of the preseason. That shows. And then the ones, twos, like it's that much more. Like the offense honestly can be top in the league. Like it's just a matter of us to keep buying in throughout the whole season and just keep getting better and better, getting everything down. And there's just so many variations to the offense. So it'll be hard for somebody to catch on to our scheme and how we do it. >> Do you let yourself take a moment when you made the roster to celebrate it all or you just going right back to work? >> No. I mean I like I said before, like I kind of had an idea but like kind of was in the grayish area. Like my mom, my brother, my best friend, they called me said congrats. I was like I kind of had just forgot about it. I was just kind of like all right. So it's just kind of getting ready for week one, whatever that role may be for me. So just take one day at a time, honestly. >> So much of this time of year is focusing on yourself and then starting next week obviously it's going to be focused on an opponent. Is there a switch you kind of have to flip when you're watching so much tape of yourself versus now you're going to be watching a different team? I would say no. I think you get Well, maybe like for like rookies or something but as you get older you kind of just adjust to that. Just kind of learn how to balance things out. Like you can evaluate yourself and kind of put yourself in those positions as you're watching film on another team. Like see how this guy created explosive, put yourself there and just envision it, if that makes sense. Yeah. >> You You were obviously running teams all last year and had the unfortunate injury and he's still trying to come back. What What's it been like for him? How How is his spirits? We haven't had a chance to talk to him. So how is he handling kind of what he's going through? >> Yeah, I mean I'm sure you guys know like what type of man he is. Like he's around the team. He's also busting his butt to get back on the field obviously, but just being in the running back room still engaged on the field when he can be, just making sure the guys are going through it, even going through the system himself. So like just having an older vet guy like that still bought in and still trying to teach everybody, even like me. Like this is my fifth year, he's still teaching me stuff. Still making sure Jeremiah good, trying to help him out, give him little keys and hacks to kind of help him. So you know, just having a leader like that in the running back room. Not even just the running back room, for the team. That's essential. I feel like that's an essential part of this team.

title: DL Waltewer Nolen III Press Conference 8.31.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: So after all these weeks we talked to you I think pretty early in camp just kind of where do you see yourself? Do you feel totally healthy, totally ready to go? Is there any part of you that feels like you still got to ramp up a little bit more? Like >> I'm just looking forward to week one. That's it. >> After last year's injuries, is there an extra appreciation for being able to be out there and be full health? >> Oh yeah, I mean I'm taking every day as a blessing, you know, last year was a real wake-up call for me that you know the sport can be taken away at any time. So I just been taking it day by day. >> Yo, they said that you've been kind of walking around like with this with this presence. Do you feel like that confidence kind of going into week one or or just kind of based off how last year went and kind of going into this year? >> Uh no, I'm just confident in like I said I'm confident in the Lord and I'm confident in in the work that I've been putting in. So um I guess I guess I've been walking around like that but um like I said I'm just excited for the season. >> I know there's been a lot of conversation about Aaron Donald coming back and that whole idea of having a dominant inside guy. Everybody's hoping that that's what you're going to be. I'm sure that's what you're hoping you're going to be. What does that mean for a team if you can be kind of a dominant inside presence on defense cuz everybody always talks about the edge guys but >> Um wholeheartedly I feel like it start with us and especially talking about my position um I feel like I'm the heartbeat of the defense and a lot of times I feel like um when I'm on the [snorts] field things move a little bit differently. So um once I'm out there I feel like we're going to we're going to kick ass. >> Both Michael Florin and PK have talked about how they think that you can get to another level of with your game. What what can you do to make that happen? Like what are you working on to actually be able to get to that level? >> Uh really just uh staying consistent every day. Um just trying to pick up on the little things early so you know um a lot of things that that the vets learn I'm picking up on it now, so I know it already. So, I'm just taking day to deposit every day, just putting something in my basket. >> What did Mike LaFleur say a couple weeks ago that when he was with the Rams last year, he could tell a difference in this defense when you were on the field and when you weren't on the field? I don't know, has he had that conversation with you? Does that surprise you at all that at that point he's an opposition coach, but talking about what a difference you make on the defense? >> Uh no, we really haven't really just talked about that for real. Um I don't really try to talk about nothing in the past for real. I try to just look forward to the future, but um I mean, if he's saying it, so I'm I'm just going to keep going, so. >> I think a lot of us thought when you left the field against Atlanta, we had processed might be a lot longer. Was there like a sigh of relief in the off season when you realized you were going to be able to come back faster and the injury wasn't what it kind of looked like initially? >> Yeah, I was uh I was definitely more so excited knowing that um my recovery timeline was shorter than a lot of other people, but um I just knew I had to put in a lot of work to get where I'm at now, so. >> You told us you dropped a little weight, you got a chef. How have you felt like that physical transformation has helped you throughout this training camp and getting to the season healthy? >> Uh honestly, I've just been feeling better every day, so I'm just going to continue to keep going with that. >> You been saying thing? Eat more? >> Yeah, I don't I'mma keep that to myself. >> [laughter] >> Well, whenever we ask other people about you, the one of the first things that always comes up is he loves the game, he loves the game of football. Where did that Where did that love of football start [snorts] or when did it start? >> Um if you ask my parents, they'll probably say um as soon as I came out the womb, but um I don't know, I kind of always had a knack for football like ever since I was little and um it just stuck with me and um luckily I'm I'm here where I'm at now. >> You called last year with call. How are you a different person at this point right now than where at this point last year? >> Uh just I like to say that last year the the word for my season was patience, you know, um I couldn't get on the field when I wanted to and then when I got out there I got hurt. So, I learned how to be patient with myself and just a lot of that going to just slow down the game for me, so. >> You're never going to sit here and say getting hurt was a good thing, but once you got hurt, can you see the the good side learning the patience of that? Can you see that part of it? >> Uh yeah, I definitely see the it's it's pros and cons to being hurt. I mean, I feel like it's all about how you attack your rehab, so um I already had the thought in my head I wanted to be the best coming back from rehab, so just putting in the work every day and that led to now. >> Who were some people that you leaned on and maybe what was the big message from them? >> I really just, you know, talking to guys like Khaseem, like I said, like just talking to older vets around the league you know, getting their input on different things I should be doing to help take care of my body. >> What what clicked for you so much in the Dallas game last year? >> Um that was that was just me playing football. I ain't going to lie, man. I'm just trying to build off that, so just continue to put those days in. >> What's it like to see your former college teammate Jaylen Williams make the make the team? You called him out there I think a dancing gallery in our earlier in camp. What's you know, having seen him go through camp, what stands out about his game? >> Uh just watching how athletic he is, you know, at that position and especially you can come in and being a rookie you you already look kind of more mature for the position and I'm just excited to see where it takes him. >> Thanks, Wall. >> Thanks, guys. Appreciate y'all.

title: OL Hjalte Froholdt Press Conference 8.31.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Yeah, we haven't had a chance to talk to you since the contract. Were you expecting it? Did it kind of come out of left field? Like what are your thoughts on it? >> Uh yeah, man. Super excited. You know, we uh >> [snorts] >> We had some good communication, got it done uh you know, before the season started. So, uh I think all parts are happy with it. So, I'm I'm stoked, man. I'm stoked to be able to be here for a couple more years and at least solidify that. Um it's good to have some security heading into the season as well, but overall, I'm just happy to be a Cardinal and be here. I mean, it's where we call home. Um It's where we live. It's where our girls are growing up and our new boy's coming up here in here in January. So, super stoked about it. Really happy to to stick around. >> And congrats on the contract and congrats on the new addition. >> Thank you. >> Why uh why did you ultimately want to decide on sticking around with the Arizona? >> Um I don't know. I mean, I've I moved here cuz I like the area actually before I even end up signing with the Cardinals. Uh I know over the past couple years here, man, like I know we got a new staff this year, but it just the boys in that locker room and and that old line room, you know, it's we've grown really tight. So, um I love the area. I love being out here. I love playing for the Cards. Um all the support I've gotten from the fans is amazing. So, uh yeah, I've had nothing but positive experiences. Um and now we're hoping to add a couple more with some wins. So, that's the goal. >> Did you allow yourself to celebrate at all? >> Uh yeah, we got some Mexican Q. Uh it's a little barbecue Mexican spot down from down from downtown Gilbert. My wife was like, "Do you want something crazy? Do you want to go to steakhouse?" I'm like, "Dude, Mexican sounds great." So, they have a they have a killer uh brisket burrito and uh some their mac and cheese is really good. So, we crushed that and then uh yeah, back to work. >> Does it allow you to like up your rock game? Where does that stand? >> Uh we'll see. So, uh hopefully I I know if I should be carrying any rocks right now, but uh I'm still trying to push it out there to see if anybody would contact and knows anything about it. Uh let's just say nothing has took yet. >> [laughter] >> No one's reached out. So, it's another PSA to anybody who has rocks to sell that I'm I might be in the market. So. >> You know, I don't I don't know if you had a chance to go against the doll at any point. I know you you faced Walter in practice and stuff. What What is it like, especially as a center, what's it like when the other team has a guy that can really wreck the game inside? Obviously, that you guys are hoping Walter becomes that kind of player. I mean, it's huge. So, I think there's just always been I feel like the league has changed a little bit over I'm sweating still. Sorry. Uh league has changed a little bit over the years. There's always been edge rushers, edge rushers, and then now it's like you see a lot of these like freak athletes come inside and have a lot of moves and create a lot of pressure and push the pocket so you can't just step up. Uh there's a lot of other ways to attack, you know, rushing the quarterback. So, I mean, when you have a guy like that on the interior, and especially the one that we have in Walt, you know, he he is a presence. He's both got a lot of moves and he has a lot of power as well. So, it's kind of hard to predict. And I think that's where is when you start having a plethora of stuff to work with. It's like, well, what do I want to shut down? So, that becomes the issue sometimes. So, been stoked to see what Walt's gone through this like this camp. He's matured so much. He starts to act like a vet. He walks around like he's relaxed. It's I think he's just stoked to be back in playing ball. Uh it's been a tough first year for him in and out. So, it's good to see him out there, man, and just I mean, he loves ball. He just loves playing hard. He celebrates a little bit, but he just kind of does it. He's just kind of in there, gets his head, and he just kind of runs away like it's, you know, I've been here before. So, it's good to see him, man. So, I'm stoked to see him kind of get out there and and uh wreck some havoc. >> I know it's only preseason, and and you guys with the starters only played one drive, but this offense has been very successful in these four games. What do you think it is about Mike's offense that um you know has has enabled all four quarterbacks to find success? >> [clears throat] >> Uh I mean attribute to the offense. I'm not a play caller, so I just do what I'm told. and I think not to dumb it down too much, but I think guys are just doing a really good job at doing what their job is. And I know it sounds maybe cliche, but it's just I think guys have taken on like taken it to heart be like, "Okay, what can we do to maximize run game? What can we do to maximize pass game? What can we do to maximize the play action pass game?" All this stuff. And guys are just really biting into it. So, it's been really good to see. I'm really proud of the whole O line. All the young guys are like, you know, bought in. Um so, it it's that's that's really awesome. And you can even see I feel out with the first group that we're out there, you know, it's not we're not perfect every play, but there's a ton of effort. There's a ton of, you know, like you're you're practicing intently, and you can see that week it's not oh, I'm just going to run left and hope for the best. It's like, "Where do I place my hands? Where do I want my hips? Where's the weight going to be? Where's my hat placement?" All these small things that you might not see on TV, but we're in there in the in the in the film room afterwards you're like, "You did great way pushing your hips up the field here so the cut so he couldn't retrace across your face so the cut back was, you know, arm tackle." That's a small thing, but it's, you know, it's like it's the small things that really make these big runs and and big passes happen. So, um like I mean I think the whole offense is doing great, but I mean I can just mostly speak for my room, obviously. And they I think they're doing a tremendous job. >> With those kinds of details, is there a benefit of Justin Frye being in his second year now with the continuity in that room? >> Uh yeah, of course. I mean I think for him second year also learning how you know, just second year for him being in NFL, you know, how to you know, it's different coaching older men >> than young boys, I guess you'd say. Uh So, there's a little bit different approach to it, but he's found his way of doing it and I think we've all bought into it and you know, it's kind of like, well, if you don't do it the way that we, you know, we kind of stick out a little bit. So, it's like, okay, well, I got to fix it. So, there's a high standard and we want it to be high and I think we're going to have a we're going to have a really good, you know, state of play. >> There was a moment in the joint practice where Marvin caught a touchdown. Kind of guys ran onto the field in the end zone. Feel like there's more of a camaraderie between these guys. You guys have always been a tight knit group as an offensive line, but you feel it team wide now? >> Yeah, I mean, that practice was awesome, you know, you just really saw the team come together. Defense did really good on their two-minute drive. Showed up with a ton of physicality and made some great plays and then we went out there and yeah, Marvin caught that ball and and then on Reese said, "Screw it, let's go for two." And then, you know, Trey caught that little ball there and took to go for two to kind of like win the day or whatever. I don't know what you want to say, but Yeah, a lot of hype, man. Everybody would just wants to to see each other achieve. So, I think that's it's a really good spot, you know, it's it doesn't matter who scores the touchdown or what happens. It's just matter that we win and score a touchdown. So, I think that's there's a lot of selflessness going on there. So, it's also just great to see Marvin out there doing crazy Marvin things. So, that's that's what he's best at. So, yeah, I'm super excited to see what he can he can keep doing for us. >> With two weeks until week one or about two weeks, how would you kind of evaluate how McCord has picked up the offense and what the whole process has been learning it from when he took over during the camp and what he has done? >> I mean, smoothness or smooth smoothness. That's awful. Effortless, I think I was about to say. I think he just, you know, jumped right in. I mean, it wasn't really a big hiccup. Like maybe first day cuz there was new words and learned the cadence is a little bit different and stuff like that, but other than that, I mean, it's like, you know, he's painting a picture in that huddle and he's doing a great job at it. So, wasn't really any um any hiccup there. I think he did a great job coming in and just, you know, and just just getting after it. And it's good to see him, you know, getting also that really good relationship with all the receivers, having proper time to practice with them and all that stuff before heading into the season. Kind of got tossed into the fire a little bit last year, so you know, he's been a really good leader in that room and that huddle for us and then and the entire old unit for the team, so uh it's good to have Jacoby back and yeah, man, he's balling out. >> The first time coaches said that for a rookie especially with Jayden, the game has not felt too fast to him. Where have you seen that in his game? >> Uh yeah, man, super impressed with Jayden. There's a lot of guys that was like, "Hey, that guy got some juice to him, you know?" Uh generally with rookies being so loaded, you kind of see a little headless chicken sometimes walk around out there, but you know, he kind of just just does it and then he doesn't really get too flustered and it's like, "Wow, that's really good." So, he takes the coaching. It's not that it's always perfect, but it's like those small things where like, "Ooh, okay, that was that was pretty good. That was not something I'd expected you to do." Um so, some of the stuff he's taking to heart on some of the same thing we talked about with the small technique. Uh him like throwing his hands or doing these things and making sure his hand placement's correct and not just, you know, there's kind of these phases of being a rookie is like first I got to know the playbook. First I got I'm just I'm in the NFL and things are going really fast and then you got to understand the playbook and you don't really get a chance to truly focus on your technique cuz you're just worried about being in the right spot. And then once it's kind of slowed down, he's like, "I know everything I need to do." Then you can start really focusing on that technique part. It's easier to at least, you know, put more effort into that and you can see that really taking off with him, so I think he's played extremely well in all the preseason games and you know, I'm stoked to see what he can do in the future. >> What is it like to block for this position this this skill group? >> Yeah, I mean, we have a ton of ton of players, you know, I don't there's I don't really know if there's anybody that's the focus, you know, cuz everybody can make plays, everybody can go up and you know um make that play we need to. So, it's really awesome. Backs are running really well and yeah, I mean Mike, Trey, Amari, or KB they're open. So, it's kind of it's pretty cool. >> With with the regular season around the corner, are you the type of guy that is going to start evaluating film now of what the Chargers were able to do or are you just going to approach like an every week type of thing and just focus on the next week? >> I mean, starting to slowly go into it a little bit. Um it's it's always I can start watching a little bit. Obviously, they have some new players there. D'Anthony's there obviously, so I've played a little bit against him the past couple years, but um you can kind of get a feel for you know, the defense and the structure. but at the same time, we don't have the true game plan. So, we're not really going to see that until next week, I think. So, we can do some preliminary stuff like, "Hey, what are we expecting? What fronts are they doing? What are we kind of thinking about running? How to run it, etc. Um but generally, personally, I I I I don't want to over prep, I guess. I know it sounds bad, I guess, but you know, I have I have my process that I do every week. So, um focus is on still on in camp right now and what can I do better and how can I just make sure my technique is correct and then I personally feel like that's going to carry over. So, as long as I know what I'm doing is correct, I'm very intentional with my own technique and what I need to do. They do a lot of some of the stuff that we've seen with our defense a little bit multiple and run in different type like, you know, run in different types of ways and stuff. So, um but you know, a little bit of prep to kind of get a a little bit of a head start obviously is always smart. Uh but you also don't want to oversaturate, I think. So, it's um it's been good so far. >> When you think about what makes up a successful running attack, is it equal running [snorts] running backs, offensive line, strategy/scheme, and coaching or does one of those four kind of outweigh the other? >> I mean, I think everything's a part of it, you know, the game can't really pass the ball or if the guys aren't creating separation and uh the same thing. I mean I mean uh like Mike's huge on you know, making sure the receivers are involved. Uh and you can see some of these plays that are you know, good run plays that we block really well for but then you have a safety in the hole and then it's going to go for six. But then if you get a some type of crack replace or push crack or something from receiver and then you bounce and all of a sudden it's a 15 20-yard gain or something like that. So, I think everybody's involved in a run game. Uh the pass game is a part of the run game. Everything's a part of it. I mean, everything works in synergy, I think. Like if if one thing is lacking generally, it it affects everything else. Um so, I think it's it's definitely a whole team thing. I mean, just the way that Jacoby carries out his fake is really important. So, I think all the small details is huge. It's not just the five old lineman up front. It's the five old lineman and the way the running back runs and then the tight end coming in as well and then the receivers how they're blocking the secondary. So, it's a whole team effort. Uh and it's been it's been huge to see how everybody's taken it to heart. >> No, thank you. Thanks for the >> I appreciate you guys. Thank you.

title: What's Really Going on with the Ravens' Kicker Situation...
text: Funny thing is, we're coming up on 25 minutes and we've yet to address the elephant in the room. At least the elephant for a good chunk of this fan base and that's the fact that a kicker signing took place earlier today as you reported. And one of the 15 players that you see on this practice squad list is Jake Moody, who was recently released. He lost out on the battle in the kicking competition in Washington. And so he is now a part of this practice squad and presumably there to compete while Jesse Mter didn't necessarily describe it as that. He referred to it as compete on the practice squad. So he was careful with his words just the way he was on Friday night, Jeff. But I'm sure you were thinking on Friday night that that was a bit different tune >> in terms of it was a bit non-committal after that preseason finale. I felt like from Jesse as it related to Tyler Loop who went five of eight in the preseason including two misses in that preseason finale against the Commanders. >> Yeah, I mean you certainly could have done more to bring in uh just in time to talk about Tyler Loop Cole, but you certainly could they certainly could have done more to turn up the heat on Tyler Loop. I think at the very least I tweeted about this I think when he made his second kick. At the very least, you had to expect them to bring in uh somebody in the practice squad. You need to get somebody ready to go, somebody who's familiar with their operation, who's kicked out of Orion Eckley holds, who is used to working with the battery. So, if you just decide to pull a plug on Tyler Loop, then you have somebody already there that there's a familiarity with. He's already started working with Randy Brown. He was at practice today. So, but again, Jake Moody is a guy that struggled an awful lot in his career, and he had some good moments where it looks like he sort of resurrected his career last year uh at times, but he didn't kick the ball particularly well this summer for the Commanders. I know fans are thinking, "We didn't do enough here." I I get that. I think the Ravens follow Randy Brown here, who has a familiarity with all these kickers around the league. His son's a a special teams kicking coach in Philadelphia. Ry's been doing it a long time. He's close with all the agents for these guys. So, this is the guy they chose. And, you know, I think you evaluate over the next two weeks and you wait to see how Tyler Loop responds. If he continues to struggle in practice, I think you need to think long and hard about activating a different kicker in Indianapolis in week one. If he kicks the ball well and and and practices well, I think he's still gonna get the shot out of this. But let's face it, he's a miss or two in a regular season game away from being out of the organization. That's just how it works. You only get so many shots at this. And we talked all about the scar tissue from his miss last year and how that sort of lessens the margin of error. Guys, I I mean when I say this, like if he makes that kick in Pittsburgh last year and whatever happens in the playoffs, if they don't lose on the account of a kicker, I don't think anybody really would be that concerned with a five for eight, five for eight preseason performance, especially when, you know, one of his misses was from what 59 yards. So, um, but he doesn't have that luxury and that's the position he's in. You can't say it's unfair. He's put himself in that position by not being consistent enough and not making kicks. And um you know, you can make every kick in the practice. Nobody cares. Nobody wants to hear that anymore. When you get a chance in stadium situations to go up and put the ball through the uprights, you need to do it a lot more consistently than he did this preseason. So, um we'll see how much Moody pushes them. I I don't think the Ravens want to make the change, but the door is open right now. this represented a change. I don't want to say an about face because they're still bringing in a kicker who's, you know, not a not been a a great kicker in his crew. You're still bringing that guy in in the practice part. It's not like you brought in Matt Prader or um you added uh Daniel Carlson when he was available or you put in a waiver claim on the Lions kid uh excuse me, the Colts kid. this is a guy you brought in that was kind of struggling in the summer and and so that needs to be said. Um but it still represents something that they have not done and that's bring in another kicker and start preparing contingency plans and that's a development in this situation that's worth monitoring because right now guys I don't know if there's a bigger concern with this team than the kicker heading into week one and nobody likes that. I mean, you go from Stover, you obviously have that blimp that was Billy Kundiff uh who was actually pretty consistent until the uh till that game in New England. Uh but then you go right into into Tucker. So, it's it's been it's been been a really tough adjustment because this is a lot of teams deal with this and the Ravens have been just fortunate to have two very good kickers in their history that have spanned a a high number of years. I think the more frustrating thing for me is just to not bring in competition during training camp. Like there it's healthy to have competition at at most positions. There was a number of guys that were like UFFL standouts and maybe it doesn't do anything and maybe it's just symbolic, but uh you know at least it looks like there's an effort there to push Tyler Luke. They just didn't do that. I I found that particularly frustrating. Um but you know there how much could really change over the next two weeks that would make a difference? Like is Jake Moody going to get opportunities to really push him or is it just going to uh is it just going to go to uh is it just going to go to a situation where he has to lose a game to then consider making a change? >> Barbecue Orange 321 says, "Love this show.
