title: Tommy Tremble: 'It's becoming a tight end-heavy league now' | Carolina Panthers
text: Tommy, you already asking if you guys can run five personnel? >> Oh yeah, we're talking about 05 personnel and so we're excited man. We're excited for this year. It's going to be fun. >> You guys have so many different styles of tight ends. Obviously 13's become like a pretty big craze around the league. How much does this kind of set you guys up to mix and match different guys? I know you're not obviously the play caller but like watching it kind of come together like how much versatility you feel like you have? >> Yeah, I think it's it's awesome that each guy brings something different to the table. You know, in our room it's it's really good when you have someone a lot of people that can do a lot of different things and so we're excited for this year just cuz like you said it's becoming a tight end heavy league now and so having us being able to do so many jobs it's it's really fun and it's exciting for this offense. >> What's the biggest thing you focused on this off season for improvements in your game? >> I think really just becoming an overall both in the run game and the pass game being reliable, being um really someone that whatever they need me to do I can do and that's what I've tried my best at. You know, I'm a professional at the end of the day. I do my job to the best of my ability. >> Tommy, after last season a lot of you guys talked about there's a new standard. Wondering how you saw that standard kind of play out in the preseason and training camp. >> Mhm. I think showing that the offense has kind of opened up a little bit. A lot of different guys are getting the ball and really showing that no that having Brad at the helm and seeing the way he's running this offense has been a lot of fun being I feel like almost a complete offense now and so that's been really fun during this training camp and going into the season. >> When you say complete offense, can you kind of expand on that? What what do you What is your vision for a Panther's complete offense? >> I think just everyone going out there and being able to do their thing. You know, throughout this preseason everyone's been getting a share of the rock and being able to do that Uh, this year has been really fun and exciting for every group and Evan's been able to go out there and just make plays. So, it's it's really fun. >> Felipe is kind of I mean, has evolved a lot since 2024. What What have you noticed about his game and how he's improved this summer? >> Uh, Felipe, man, he's a dog, man. I I love Felipe. Like, the way he's came in to work and just be the best he can be, it's so fun seeing, especially when he first got here in 2024. Um, his development as a tight end, as a player, as a teammate is like it's out of this world, man. He's a really good football player and I'm excited for him this year, man. He's going to go out there and make plays. That's what he does. And so, I'm really excited for him this year. >> Having been through roster cuts for a few years now, were were you surprised at all that they kept five tight ends? >> Um, not at all. I mean, everyone, like I said before, has um, a different aspect to their game and so, it wasn't really surprising to us. Um, if anything, it shows what they think about us and so, that's uh, something after that uh, deadline hit to see them keep five of us it it was really uh, it was kind of reassuring for us. >> Did Did you guys have a lot of deep conversations about the Houston joint practices or is there something you take away from those practices that you think you guys can really learn from? >> Um, I think it's really just uh, I guess everyone being on the same page and um, being comfortable where they are. You know, joint practices, that's the good thing about them. You get to test uh, what you like without showing really all your plays to the rest of the league and so, I think um, in from these past joint practices, we just realized we got to really focus on the details and make sure that we're just able to do our jobs. If we're able to do our jobs, we're able to succeed. >> You're the elder statesman, I guess, in that tight end room. >> Mhm. >> For a guy like JT, where there's questions surrounding he's going to stay, then they bring in Waller, who may have the same skill set. What type of I guess, wisdom are you imparting on him as he may go through some um, uncertainty? >> I think JT's a professional, man. He hands him He handles himself really well. Not only on the field, but in the building as well. And I think there's no real story for that. It's just he's coming to work just like every one of us, coming to work every single day, ready to get better, and that's what we've all been doing. >> Tommy, as one of the guys who've been around here for a while, what's it been like watching the improvement on defense with your defense over the last couple of years? >> Yeah, it's fun. I mean, guys are flying around, guys are making plays. I'm excited for our defense this year, and so really seeing it every year get better and better and better. It's been a lot of fun and gives a big confidence boost for the offense. >> What's it like, I mean, when you add a Jaelan Phillips, Dylan Lloyd, Bobby today, but when you bring in those kind of big impact guys? >> It's fun, man, cuz it's fun to see playmakers make plays. And so it's one of those things you go through practice, you go through camp, and you're like, I'm glad they're on my team. So it's it's really fun to see that. >> I mean, this was a longer than usual camp, and it was Did it feel that way? Did that extra week kind of start wearing it on you? >> Um sort of, sort of not. For me, I haven't done camp in the last 2 years cuz of injury, and so to me, it felt long regardless. But at the end of the day, a lot of guys came out healthy, a lot of guys came out ready to play, and so I think you don't really think about it too much when you're just trying to get your job done. >> Hey, Oz. Thanks, Tommy. >> Appreciate y'all. >> [music] [music]

title: Bobby Okereke's first press conference as a Panther | Carolina Panthers
text: Fireway? Okay. Well, Bobby, uh welcome. >> Yes, sir. >> Um when you guys were figuring out, you and your agent were figuring out where you wanted to land, why why do you think it took so long to reach that decision? And how long back did you have these conversations with Dan in the front office? >> Yeah. Uh just being a 8-year vet at this point, wanted to make sure I was going to a a really good fit. Um position-wise, opportunity-wise. Um and yeah, we've been having these conversations uh with multiple teams since basically March, April. Um but yeah, just kind of knowing the uh belief and trust I have in myself to prepare myself for a season, uh I just wanted to make sure I was going to the right opportunity and it felt felt great and obviously it did here. >> Was the waiting process hard for you? >> Uh it was interesting, for sure. Um I was definitely itching to play football, for sure. Um but it was good, you know, I'm a I'm a 8-year pro. I love working out, I love taking care of my body. Uh I feel fresh, I feel fast out there today, so uh I just kept myself mentally strong and ready to go. >> When you say right opportunity, how much does Devin Lloyd factor into that and how much does having a general manager like Dan Morgan, who is a former NFL linebacker, how much do those factors kind of um impact that decision? >> Yeah, both of those huge factors. Uh playing next to Devin Lloyd today, just his communication, his command of the huddle, uh it's great. Uh obviously Dan Morgan just being a stud linebacker himself in the tradition of linebackers here. And uh reuniting with Pete Hansen, uh you know, from my days with Stanford, just uh it all culminated in a great fit. >> Uh what was it like to take a practice field this close to week one and how did you kind of stay like mentally ready for football during when everybody else is playing and you weren't? >> Yep. Yeah, it's uh it was a process, for sure. Um definitely stayed disciplined with it. I was watching film on my own. Uh I was training back in Jersey with a helmet on, you know, running hills, running on the track, in the weight room. Uh just disciplining myself cuz, you know, you're not in a program with 90 other guys going through lifts and all that. So, uh a lot of discipline and a lot of resilience. >> How are we liking Charlotte so far? >> Uh say it again. >> Love it. Yeah. >> What have you liked so far? The weather has been good? >> Uh the weather's nice. >> [laughter] >> Nice and warm. >> For for those Panthers fans who maybe never really watched you play, >> what are the Panthers getting? >> Yes, sir. Uh a season veteran, uh fast, sideline to sideline guy, high football IQ, and a playmaker. Uh I've had a lot of forced fumbles, a lot of picks in my career. Uh and excited to bring that here to Charlotte. >> You got a lot of youth in the room as well. How do you instill that, you know, what you've learned over the years to younger guys like Jackson guys like that? >> Yeah. Uh I mean, it's a it's a dual process, you know, they're teaching me the playbook and I'm teaching them uh just stuff I've learned along the way, tricks of the trade, playing next to Darius Leonard, uh playing next to studs, playing with Wink Martindale, with Matt Eberflus. Uh I've had a lot of great coaches and a lot of great players next to me. So, uh just told everybody here I'm here to serve. So, I'm excited. >> And Morgan just said he basically said you're you're going to start. Was that one of the things that you that was important to you for you to come into a situation where you are starting and then what does the next week or so look like for you as you prepare in a new system to take the field as a starter week one? >> Yeah. Uh just wanted an opportunity to compete for a playing time, for sure. Um and yeah, just with my experience, I've played Sam, I played Mike, I played Will. Uh I just wanted to bring that to a team where I'll be utilized in a great defense, obviously here. So, extremely excited. >> Bobby, you talked with a lot of pride about being a veteran. Besides the eight years, um when you were starting out, who was the veteran that taught you how to be an NFL pro? >> Yeah. Uh Anthony Walker, for sure, in Indianapolis. Um you know, every week he would send us notes, whether it was Monday, Tuesday before the Wednesday prep. Uh and he's writing down the run charts, first and second down, all the tendencies. Uh so, really seeing the way that he attacked the game uh mentally really helped me prepare. And then obviously Darius Leonard, he was just a year above me, but uh seeing the instincts and the play making he had uh was really incredible to be around. >> What have you taken from the way that they prepared and brought to maybe other guys that are younger than you and maybe show them the way? >> Yeah. Um yeah, just it's uh it's preparation big time, physical, mental, um spiritual, emotional. Like this game takes everything out of you. And if you want to be a great player, you got to pour everything into it. So, uh excited to bring that to this team. >> Uh Bobby, you're big on community, obviously Walter Payton Man of the Year nominee last year. Congratulations on that. >> Thank you. >> What um I know you just got signed, but are there any plans initially to get involved in the Charlotte community in this way, Boys & Girls Clubs, what have you? >> Yep. Yeah, 100%. Uh Boys & Girls Clubs has been great for me. Uh I work with Teresa and Andre Reed. Andre Reed has the Andre Reed Foundation where he works with Boys & Girls Clubs. Uh Reed for Reed, he starts reading clubs there. So, excited to get going with that here in Charlotte. >> Just joining a team this close to the first game, one, how do you just learn everything so fast and I mean that's less than 2 weeks. >> Yeah, 100%. Um I mean I pride myself on being a smart guy, so uh just staying in the playbook, studying, um obviously hanging out with Devin, um hanging out with all the linebackers, kind of uh immersing myself in the playbook, but uh yeah, I have There's a lot of carryover from my days in Stanford with the Vic Fangio defense. Uh I've ran a lot of quarters with Matt Eberflus, cover three with uh um Gus Bradley, um and then Wink Martindale, a lot of blitz stuff. So, uh I've probably played all the coverages. Now it's just learning the terminology and uh piecing it together and putting it on the buckets. >> What's something that's really stood out about the coach Evero's attack on things or like you know how he handles stuff? >> Yeah. Uh just his demeanor. Uh especially being at practice today, uh having the mic in my helmet, being able to kind of listen in on the calls. Uh he has great command and you can tell he's a seasoned veteran as well and um, you know, he he he gets the players prepared to play. >> Bobby, what what is it about Pete Hansen's coaching style that you like? How did you get obviously he was there the whole time you were there at Stanford. Um, how did you guys connect and when you first met him were you blown away by how tall he was? >> Yeah, definitely. Um, and obviously throw throw back to his Arizona basketball days and uh, field goal block days blocking all the punts. Uh, but yeah, Pete's a great guy. Um, great demeanor, great intensity. Um, you know, I I tell him I took from him in my Stanford days just conscious effort. Uh, and that's been the big thing for me. You know, takeaways don't just happen. It takes an intentional conscious effort. So, uh, just leaning on that and you know, he allows his players to play with instincts and I'm excited for that. >> How do you mention here in the having a mic in your helmet today is your expectation that you'll have the green dot? >> No. Uh, I mean I I I've been telling Devon since I got here it's his show. Uh, I'm here to support him in any way I can. Um, so yeah, I'm just excited to play whatever role they got for me. >> How easy or difficult is that for you as someone who's coming off of being a captain in your previous stop to to maybe let go of some of that responsibility while still also being a leader here as well, too? >> Yeah. Um, obviously coming in uh, a little late it just helps me acclimate better. But I think it helps me serve my teammates better. You know what I mean? I've been in Devon's shoes. I know what it's like when you're calling the plays and uh, you're running down the sideline. You got to come back and people are asking you to call. So, as much as I can help him with the tendencies, the down and distance, um, the ID formation, uh, however to help the team. >> 58 is a number that's got some story history here in Carolina with Thomas Davis. Uh, did you talk to any of the legends, you know, coming in or anything? >> Yeah. Uh, actually saw Thomas Davis yesterday. Um, you know, I'm sitting at the locker right next to his picture and uh, he was telling me he's excited for me to be here, but uh, obviously incredible linebacker tradition here and I'm excited to add to that. >> Any pressure now? Any pressure No, there's no pressure. It's just excitement and opportunity. >> Did you guys talk about you wearing 58? >> Uh yeah, I talked to my guy Moz about it and we worked something out. >> No, did you talk to Thomas Davis about it? >> Oh yeah, I mean I think he he he anticipated me wearing it and I think he's excited for me to add to that tradition. >> Did you have to pay to wear it? >> Uh we're working something out. >> Thanks, Bobby. >> Appreciate it, Bobby. >> [music] [music]

title: Dan Morgan: 'We're going to leave no stone unturned' | Carolina Panthers
text: First off, uh just excited about this team. Um you know, the direction that we're headed in. I thought we had got some really good work in during this training camp. Two joint practices. Um obviously one against Jacksonville, one against Houston, I think is really beneficial uh for our players, for our staff. Uh just really good work, you know, both those weeks. So, I think it's really going to help us going in into the season and you know, just prepare us for what's ahead. Um credit to coach Canales and his staff, um our training staff, uh equipment, and our personnel staff. Um I thought everybody did their job at a really high level. Um we're all pulling in the same direction and everybody's excited about the season and what's ahead of us. Um the players who made our roster and our practice squad, you know, they earned it. There was a lot of competition out there. Uh that's what we were hoping for is bringing in competition. Um guys going out there earning it on a day-to-day basis. And all the guys that made our team and our practice squad, they did that. So, we're really proud of those guys. We're excited to have them on our team. They're our type of guys. They're our type of competitors. And uh we're lucky to have the guys that we have. So, with that I'll open it up. >> Coach, you brought up earning it. And obviously Darren Waller was here for a couple of weeks. Caught one pass in team drills. How did you have to weigh the lack of information you created while he was here with keeping five tight ends? >> Yeah, you know, I think um you know, keeping five tight ends, you know, I think it really comes down to each of those guys have a specific skill set that we like. And you know, if you go down the line with Tommy, you know, really good blocker and receiver. Um Mitch, you know, just a big body wide blocker, you know, who who's also a very capable wide out for us. So, you go down the list and Daron Waller, to answer your question, you know, I think he has a unique skill set that I think we can utilize and you know, I think I know coach Canales and his staff are really excited about having him and and what he can bring to our to our offense, different dimension to our offense. So, you know, I think that all went into to keeping Daron. >> You made the decision to cut Trevon Waller. He was a part of your first draft class. How difficult was that? >> Yeah, it's difficult. You know, me and Trevon we developed a really close relationship. He's been in my office multiple times us watching tape together. I really, you know, wish him the best. Obviously getting claimed by the Jets. Really happy for him and his family. And a new start for him, a new direction and I know he's excited about it. But again, those decisions they don't come easy. But I think bringing linebackers in like Bobby Okereke, bringing Tyrell Dotson onto the practice squad, and then having Claude Cherilus and Jackson Kuwach, two young guys that we're really excited about. We feel good about our linebacking core. >> Dan, can you expand a little bit on how the whole Okereke thing went down? How did that deal come together and what can he bring to this defense? >> Yeah, you know, we kept in contact with his agent all through the summer time, all the way leading up to, you know, when we signed him here, you know, a couple days ago. So, he's a guy he's a veteran guy that he's been productive in this league. He's super smart, high football IQ. Really fits what what we do schematically on the defensive side. So, putting him next to Devin Lloyd, we felt were two big, long, uh rangy guys that can cover, they can blitz, they can do a lot of things. Um so, we felt like he was a really good fit for what we do. >> And despite that limited sample size in preseason games, >> [clears throat] >> what made you feel good enough about Haynes King to roster? >> Yeah, I think Haynes, you look at his athleticism and then seeing him out there on the field, you you watch his college tape, you think he's just a runner. He's not just a runner. Like, he can sit in the pocket, he can process, he can get the ball out quick, he knows where to go with the ball. And then I think you saw him in the Hall of Fame game, the way that he operated the offense, the way that he operated the offense. We felt like he was a guy we didn't want to expose to waivers. We didn't want to let somebody have the opportunity to get him. We He's our type of guy, uh the type of guy that we want to work with and continue to develop. >> Dan, you've mentioned really over the years just how much value you put into competitive rooms, creating more depth. How much more difficult were the decisions this go round once you've seen more of that depth develop? >> Yeah, I think I think they're getting harder every year and and that was the goal when I first took over is to keep building the depth, keep building the competition, and just get better in every single area. And and I think we're headed in that direction. I don't know that all of our feel like we're there. Um I think we just have that type of mentality where we're going to leave no stone unturned. We're going to be looking for players, you know, even today, all through the season, we're going to be looking to churn the roster and and find players that could potentially help us. >> Back to Haynes and Dan, it seems like it'd be difficult to roster have all those guys up on game day, all all of them. >> Yeah. >> How committed are you to sticking all five for the long term? >> Yeah, right now we're committed. Not to say that something couldn't change. I don't know what the future holds, but I know coach Canales has a plan for each and every one of those guys. What he does with them on game day, you know, is yet to be seen. So, but right now we feel good about it. >> And uh back on Bobby for a second, he's been a starter in this league many times. Did you bring him in with the idea that he will be your starting inside linebacker? >> Yeah, I think that's the plan right now. And and again, you know, he he's started a lot of games in this league. He's played at a high level. He's a really smart guy. Uh he's been with Pete Hansen before. He kind of understands the concepts of our defense and and what we're trying to accomplish. So, I feel like he's going to be a really good fit there next to Devin. And you know, of course bringing a guy like Tyrell in, another guy that's a veteran guy that, you know, we could elevate at some point if we need to, if if an injury happens. Um so, that was the idea with bringing him in as well. >> Uh to follow up on that, why Tyrell has started some games. He had a pretty good year last year. Why did he decide to join the practice squad? Did you guys offer him a 53-man spot at any point? How did that come to be? >> Yeah, we offered him a practice squad spot. Um when I was in Buffalo, we signed Tyrell as a as a UDFA. So, me and him had a really close relationship and just selling him on the idea of coming and being on our practice squad, he was all for it. I know he had other opportunities and you know, I think mine and his relationship uh I think definitely helped out. And he's excited to be here. He wants to he wants to help be a leader. Um and he and he wants to play, too. So, um again, I told him there'll be opportunity potentially down the road. You never know, barring injuries. Um so, he's he's all in and he's excited to be here. >> Do you expect him to play within that first month of the season, or do you need to kind of get him up to >> Yeah, I think that's to be determined. I think, you know, once he gets into our system and and figures it out and gets with our special teams coach, um then we'll just kind of go from there. >> Did you um at after we haven't talked to you since the joint practice with Houston where the offensive line kind of got overrun? >> How concerned are you about that OL, you you know, given that you had to put both of your tackles, you know, on those lists and I I mean, I I feel good about our our O-line and, you know, we made some moves the other day uh bringing Corey Bullock in. He was with the Ravens in the preseason, a guy we identified, center-guard flexibility on the inside there. He's really firm, um tough tough guy. He has all the things that we're looking for in Lyman, but back to your question, yeah, like the Houston practice, absolutely, it was rough, but I thought it was also a really good learning experience and being able to go against Jack- Jacksonville and their edge rushers and then go against Houston and their edge rushers, that's why we do these practices. We do these practices to get our guys prepared for the season and know what we have and Monroe continues to get better and better every single day, as does Rashid on the left side, and they're still kind of gelling in our system and our scheme and, you know, I think you'll see them continue to grow as time goes on. >> And staying with the >> three years, you've had at least one UDFA uh make the initial 53-man roster. This year, you've had three. How important is it for a franchise to develop uh players like that as far as cost cutting uh certain positions and and just being able to groom them? >> Yeah, I mean, it's big. Uh we've uh our college staff has done a really good job identifying guys that You all right? Bless you. Um, yeah, our college staff has done a really good job identifying these UDFAs that fit what we do from a schematic standpoint, but also the character part of things and and I think that's been the difference where these UDFAs are coming in, they're having success because, you know, they they have all those characteristics that we're looking for, not only from a personal standpoint, but from a football character and um, they fit our scheme. >> Dan, you always talk about the off season. >> season. You always talk about the wide receiver room having a lot of competition. What kind of went [clears throat] into that decision to keep six of them and also in turn keeping someone like J'Mar Smith on the practice squad? Why was that important to keep him around as well? >> Yeah, I mean, J'Mar Smith had a great camp. Um, you know, I think we we have our strategies and ways that we do things and you know, we have probabilities of guys getting claimed and you know, our formulas that I won't get too much into. Kind of keep that in house a little bit, but we felt like there was a good chance that we would get J'Mar Smith back on our practice squad and you know, Metche had a great camp out there. Um, he's making plays every single game, every single practice, uh, was creating with the ball in his hands after the catch, which we really value and he can return punts as well. I think special teams definitely plays a big part, you know, in those last couple spots as well. >> Dan, going back to the >> You haven't been quick to trade a draft pick for players, trade up. You've done pick swaps, you've done player for player trades. Why was T Rowe Edwards that appealing to you guys? >> Yeah, I think first and foremost, felt like we needed some depth there and I think, you know, since I took over, you guys have seen like we're going to attack areas that we feel like, you you are our areas of need and we identified him in the preseason and he stuck out on tape. You know, his motor, he's strong, he's physical, he plays the style that we're looking for looking for here. So, you know, giving away a pick, you know, for somebody like that, you know, was really an easy decision for me. >> Dan, going back to the offensive line for a second, you parted ways with Chandler Zavala. Can you just kind of go into what made you guys come to that decision? >> Yeah, we you know, we put a claim in on Corey Bojorquez and once we got him, you know, we kind of swap both those guys out. We wanted to get a look at a new guy that we felt like, you know, he could play center, he could play guard, brings a little more versatility for us there on the interior. So, we're really excited to have Corey and and um, you know, just see where it goes. >> Dan, I'm wondering if you have a formula to that that you'll utilize during the season in terms of likelihood that guys would get claimed off the practice squad. And and what I'm getting at is, do you think you're going to have to keep Haines on the active all year to to hold on to him? >> Yeah, I mean, I don't have a crystal ball to to know that. Um, but Haines is going to be on our team, you know, the for the foreseeable future is what I would say. Um, we're not going to expose him to waivers and and again, let somebody pick him up. So, um, we do have formulas for that and and probabilities for that. Um, but yeah, the right now he's on our team. >> The past couple of years you haven't had guys claimed off of waivers after cut down. You had two this year. Um, you had a couple guys signed to other practice squads. What does that say about the state of the roster over the last three years? >> Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, we're we're getting we're getting better as as a team. Um, you You I think our the type of players we're bringing in. I think we're bringing in the type of players that appeal to a lot of teams around the NFL. Um you know, both those guys that got claimed, they fit, you know, their systems. They fit, you know, what they're looking for and um yeah, I think it's, you know, a testament even to those guys, you know, that they they can play and those teams saw something about them on tape that they really liked. >> Okay, Dan, how important will AJ Dillon be on third and short situations uh this season? >> Yeah, I mean, I think he could definitely play a role. Um obviously, having Chuba and having Jonathan Brooks, I would think that they would be you know, getting those carries ahead of, you know, AJ, but, you know, I think AJ's definitely going to help us out this year and we're really excited about what he brought to us in the preseason and catching the ball, protecting, the way he ran the ball. Uh he looked really good out there and and and and a guy that's definitely going to help us throughout the year. >> Are you comfortable with him being the safety net, uh you know, the third back? >> Yeah, I think he's a capable starter, you know, I think he's a guy that, you know, is not only, you know, our third running back, but I think he could play for a lot of teams. He's he's big, he's physical, he's a bruiser. He's hard to tackle. He's not the type of guy that, you know, linebackers, safeties, and guys want to tackle all game when he's running downhill at you. >> You guys clearly put an emphasis on special teams with the guys that you kept. How did you take being Stansbury's special teams outlook kind of play into the the roster math at tight end, especially when you're bringing back Felipe and and you've got some of those other aces? >> Yeah, I think, you know, JT's shown that he can be a really good special teams player along with, you know, giving us receiving ability in the pass game at the tight end position. So, you know, JT definitely has a lot of traits that we like and and again, he's he's productive on teams as well. So, he definitely has a lot of value for us. >> Could you give us an update on Wharton, Ickey, and Taylor, please? >> Yeah, we really don't have any updates on those guys. Obviously, you know, you saw we put them on IR. Obviously, we can designate them to return it after 4 weeks. after that, I don't really have any update for you right now. >> You don't have any I'm sure internally you guys have a sense. I mean, can you ballpark us? >> Yeah, I think they're progressing really well. They're attacking their rehab. The training staff's done a really good job with all all those guys. So, I think they're all going to be ready at some point. When that is, I don't know yet. >> Do you look at Bam, Trevor, and Brady as long-term injuries, or are those guys that you think you could take advantage of the new rules with the practice window? >> Yeah, I think it could be the practice window. Um I'm not sure, you know, in terms of long-term or not. You know, it's up to the rehab and how they progress. Uh they are progressing. I You know, I I expect them to be available at some point. When that is, I don't know yet. >> Dan, you We talked about Hayes King, but you also kept Albert Reese and Hall, too. I wonder if why you did those >> two in specific. >> Yeah, I think um it's hard to find big tackles like Albert Reese. You know, he's big, right tackle only, a guy that can anchor. Um obviously, he's a rookie. He's going to have some rough reps here and there, but you know, he's big, he's athletic, he can move people in the run game. He's a guy that we're excited about for the future. Um same thing goes with Aaron Hall. You know, he's he was really impressive out there. A guy that, you know, kind of blew us away with how he's playing out there, how strong he is against double teams. Uh he showed pass rush. Um his motor's high. He can get up and down the line of scrimmage. So, those guys, you know, they they earned it. They They went out there every day. They competed. They attacked it. And you know, they they made our team because of that. >> Let's do a couple more. as far as the 2024 class, when you reflect on that, obviously kind of traveling like what's your takeaway on that class as it's been with Jonathan coming back and obviously Xavier having another year? >> Yeah, you know, we're obviously excited about the guys that are still on our team from that class. Um we think they have high upside and playmaking ability. Um of course, you're not going to hit every pick. Um no teams do. Um but again, that that's on me to go back and look at our processes, look at the way we do things. You know, if we do miss on a player, why did we miss on the player? And I think as long as we're getting better every single year, um I think that's the main thing is, you know, learning lessons, not just mistakes, but just learning lessons in every area. >> Were there any unique challenges to to that draft as you transitioned uh to the full-time role? And and you know, obviously the previous year, too, is only uh Bryce is the only one left from there. >> Same question to that class. >> Yeah, I think, you know, when it comes to me, you know, from the time I took over until now, again, I think what I just said, I think you know, you continue to refine your processes, go through your processes, be critical on yourself, um not be afraid to admit admit mistakes when you make mistakes, um but continue to just keep looking at yourself and not pointing fingers. And that's what we do around here. We we try to find solutions to things, and we don't point fingers. Um everybody's, you know, moving in the same direction, trying to do their part at a high level. I feel like we have a really good process in place um that everybody is doing their job at a high level right now. So, I feel really good about where we're headed. >> Just last one. Was there any guy that you you thought maybe had an outside chance of making the roster who just kind of blew you away with their production throughout the preseason and training camp? >> That made our roster? >> the roster. A guy who kind of maybe you were trying to find a role, you didn't know how he'd fit, and then he kind of became undeniable, sort of. >> Yeah, I mean, I think we can go back to Aaron Hall. You know, I think on a day-to-day he just he brought it every single day. Um, and credit to him, you know, and his mindset and the way he attacked every day, the way that he approached every day. Um, not just out on the field, but here in the building, in the training room, in the weight room, in the classroom, like he's, you know, mature beyond his years, I would say. >> Thank you, Dan. >> Yeah, no problem. >> [music] [music]

title: Panthers Live Press Conference
text: Hey, hey, hey. Heat. Heat. Heat. Hey, heat. Hey, heat. You are >> [music] >> Here we go. Hallelujah. I can't control. [music] >> Happy birthday. Heat. >> Donald I have a happy exciting times. Exciting times to be back on the grass um with what's our team right now and and uh there's a lot of great energy in the meetings, a lot of great energy on the field and uh you know, one of the just amazing things is that I can feel from the guys is there also is a lot of respect for the guys that aren't here. And uh I can feel that from the guys also. um while there's an excitement for where we're headed, there's also um just a sadness, you know, for the guys that we've been working with and that aren't here with us anymore. So, uh I try to balance both of those things and just remind them we got work to do and uh we got an amazing opponent first game against the Bears and uh we're after this division and so that's where our focus has to be and um got to be ready to take the next steps forward. >> Coach, um I think it came as a shock to a lot of people that the team moved on from Trevor Wallace. Can you share a little bit of insight to that decision? >> Sure. Um, you know, that was a competition between Claude and and Trevan going through camp and, uh, both guys competed their hearts out and really gave everything they had. Um, one game Claude's a little better. One game Trevan's a little bit better and it was it was neck and neck and um, with that evaluation, as you understand, you know, we're wa we're looking for all of the opportunities uh, to potentially make our our roster as competitive possible. And um you know the the thought of being able to get a player like Bobby Okareke um was an amazing opportunity for us, a guy who wanted to be here. And you know, as we got closer, we had to look at what what does his film look like and can we imagine a world where he's playing with Devin and um and unfortunately Trevan, I love him. I wish him the best, you know, where he's headed and a guy that was a part of our first draft class. Um but this was an opportunity to make that room more competitive and we took that opportunity. Um Claude competed and and provided some things on special teams and kind of had of an edge there, you know. So um that's kind of as much as I want to share about the situation, but um a lot of respect for Trevan and the work that he put in coming off of an injury with the big surgery, you know, getting himself back healthy to be able to compete. >> Coach Derek Brown left practice early and Bobby Brown looked like he aggravated his back. Any updates on the two? >> He came back and finished. Um, so I think they were just, uh, you know, Todd Wash was excited to get his new group out there. So, uh, you know, they were probably the closest group to the little creek that runs by the practice field and I was concerned Dererick might have went in there to cool off a little bit. Um, it was pretty warm out there. But, um, it was a great day to get back to work and uh, to get after it and that's what they did. But, um, you know, I won't I won't give just for any other questions about injuries, I won't give anything specific until we get to game week and we'll kind of honor those timelines as we go. >> Dave, five tight ends. Um it's hard enough getting five wide receivers out there. How are you going to manage the pass catching group of those uh I guess 11 guys? >> Yeah. Again, stuff that I'm not going to share about, but I will talk about that group um and talk about the unique skill set from the tight end group and just having different body types. You have Mitch uh Mitch Evans who is a big wide traditional body type who can body up with OLB's defensive ends. Um, you have Tommy who's got versatility, physical in the run game, fast enough to stretch the field and and make things happen that way. Um, you got JT who kind of does a little bit of all of it and can play in the slot some, you know, as a receiver. And then you talk about JT's ability to contribute on special teams, which he has improved um over the course of time. Felipe, one of the one of the really premier special teams players in the league. And then watching his growth as a tight end and his pass catching ability is really intriguing. And then of course rounding it off with Darren Waller. We know what he looks like on film. We know the element he can bring to us. So some things to work out there to see who we're going to have up helping us on game day. Um but a group that I feel really strongly about. Dan and I both felt that each guy had something unique that they bring to our team. Um and felt like it was a position we wanted to keep together. >> On that, uh Waller and Jonathan were working off to the side. Yeah. >> I know you don't want to talk about injury. Is that rev up related or? >> Yeah, just just normal maintenance kind of the rhythm that we're having Darren on right now. Just bringing him back and seeing where he's at physically. Uh JB's got a little soreness. I won't get into specifics right now. >> Any concern was Waller the fact that you're slow slow ramping him up. Was that part of the reason? >> Definitely a part of it. Yes. And guys that we trust being here, but then also like we got to see how Darren handles a full volume of a week. how does he come out come off and respond off of a gameweek? You know, we need to have all those uh factors. You know, we need to gather that information as we go. Um and you know, from his words, you know, this is last year, you know, he was he really going and and signing with the Dolphins. It was a little bit of a surprise when he when he showed up. This year, he'd been training ready to get into a camp. And um the timing of it, I wish we could have had him sooner. Um but you know when we brought him in again it's kind of we wanted to make sure that we get a full body of work to see where he's at. >> Dave, can you talk a little bit more about Dan was when Dan was in here [snorts] anticipate some starting point. >> Yeah, >> that's a pretty big move for you know guy who had been here. So what makes you confident that work? >> Uh a consmate pro, very intelligent um tackling machine. You know if you just pull up his stats he's all over the field. Solo tackles, assists. He's on every play. um that type of style, that type of mindset, um we love having, you know, Devin is that way. Um we feel like he he fits into the nature of what we're looking for at the position. And so, uh we're excited to get him. Uh saw him out there at practice for the first time today and uh was already running around. He's in great shape. Um if you know the guy that probably wouldn't shock you, this is a guy that was ready to go. Um and now it's just a matter of the communication factor, making sure he's clear on all the adjustments and all that. Dave, how vital is it to bring in guys that can play multiple positions up front? Obviously, you have Brad to go down, but you bring in Cory Bolick, you have Jake Kuran back. How vital is it to have those guys that can cross trainin to provide that depth? >> It's something that's served us well over the last couple of years. Guards who can play center, guards who can play tackle, Brady can play all five. Jake Kurhan has played guard and tackle. Um, and then Bulock comes in, his center film is really good. Then you look, you flip on his guard tape and that's pretty good, too. So, that versatility is really huge for us. Dave, three quarterbacks on the active roster, Hannes King being one of them. We've talked about it all summer. Is there a possibility where Hannes can have a couple plays, a couple packages assigned to him where he can just kind of pop in on game day and make an impact, whether that be in the run game or in select passing plays, >> anything's possible. How do you guys approach this week in terms of balancing [laughter] >> getting to know what the team looks like versus working ahead on what's happening next week? >> Say that again. I'm sorry. [laughter] >> Um, how do you guys kind of approach this week in terms of balancing how much you're looking ahead to next week's stuff versus just kind of getting to know this group of people as it stands? >> Yeah, it's a great question. So, a couple factors that go into it. you know, we are now transitioning into where we have to get our scout teams ready uh to be able to copy what the Bears are doing and and try to get their scheme so we can get a good look at that. So, this week is a great opportunity to start having some of those periods, but there's still also a lot of just core things that we want there's wrinkles. There's things we need to iron out and sharpen um as we go into it. And so I still like the competitive part of yes, we're doing some card periods, but then let's also go good on good so that we're making sure that the competitive element, guys, at the end of the day, we're still playing football. We had a one-on- ones, uh, sorry, first team versus first team blitz drill today. First team versus first team, two-minute drill at the end. Um, keeping the conditioning, keeping the competitive element of that going. So, uh, a little bit of a mix this week. >> The Bears, uh, are very heavy on their team. Um, so you clearly need coverage linebackers. How much did you guys look into kind of the growth of that 13 personnel package in all teams when you were considering Devin Lloyd and and Dodson and and bringing in I guess Bobby? >> Yeah, some some self I mean some opponent scout studies. You know, the Rams did a great job utilizing 13 personnel in the run game and the pass game. Um, having those versatile type of tight ends who are rugged enough to play in the box, but they can also stretch the field is huge. Um the Bears have done a fantastic job that way also of making 13 look like 12 look like 11 and then bringing it all back in and having some core runs and play action. So something we certainly have to work on. Um and definitely you know having having that profile of athlete in the inside linebacker position be able to match up some of those guys that they have uh is valuable. >> But with but with the five guys that you have now you can kind of do something similar. Absolutely. And how how exciting is that for you and Brad being able to kind of follow that trend? >> Absolutely. It's very it's very important to us. I go back to my time with Daryl Beville in Seattle and we were at 22, 21, 13, 10, 01, 11, all the basic personnels as well. We just wanted to make sure we got a good 11 out there and then we can present it however we wanted to. condensed formations in 13 spread empty and all of a sudden you got base defense with three linebackers out there covering concept. So, um having that versatility is important. We have the guys to do it. Um it'll certainly be a part of what we do. >> Dave AJ Dylan made the X roster. You have talked about how he can be a virtue not only in the run game but also on special teams. What um what about him stood out to you to ultimately make the decision for him to make it? >> Discipline. um running the runs the right way, pressing combos the right way, finishing plays violently, catching the ball out of the back field, which was, you know, he'd be up here telling you this. That was an emphasis for him this off seasonason was catching the ball um and being being, you know, uh being reliable in the pass game and he certainly s showed that um in the preseason as well. So, I'm just really impressed with all that. The way he goes about business um he's been around, he's a pro and uh it was really refreshing to be able to get him on our team. Dan traded a a draft pick for TR Edwards. What do you see in him and what's he going to bring to the depth of the room? >> Yeah, uh a guy that can play square to the line of scrimmage. Um playing down down down along the line, being able to move laterally, stout at the point of attack and he's got some sneaky pass for stuff. He had one nice rush today. Uh he was out there practicing today and um you know for a shorter guy uh not the longest guy, not the biggest guy, a lot of power and a lot of twitch and able to get on edges and uh and give us something that we like the versatility along the inside three, the ability to play nose, to play end in different spots and he brings that. >> How important was Meti's return ability in him making the roster especially with Trevor out? >> I mean it's huge. Uh a season veteran, uh fast sideline to sideline guy, high football IQ, and a playmaker. Uh I've had a lot of force fumbles, a lot of picks in my career. Uh I've had a lot of great coaches and a lot of great players next to me. So, uh just told everybody here, I'm here to serve, so I'm excited. >> Morgan just he basically said you're you're going to start. Was that one of the things that you that was important to you for you to come into a situation where you were starting? And then what does the next week or so look like for you as you prepare in a new system to take the field as a starter week one? >> Yeah. Uh just wanted an opportunity to compete for playing time for sure. Um and yeah, just with my experience. I've played Sam, I played Mike, I played Will. What have you taken from the way that they prepared and brought to maybe other guys that are younger than you and maybe show them the way? >> Yeah. Um, yeah, just it's uh it's preparation big time. Physical, mental, um, spiritual, emotional, like this game takes everything out of you and if you want to be a great player, you got to pour everything into it. What um I know you just got signed, but are there any plans initially to get involved in the Charlotte community in this way? Boys and Girls Clubs, what have you? >> Yep. Yeah, 100%. Uh Boys and Girls Clubs has been great for me. Uh I work with Terresa and Andre Reid. Andre Reid has the Andre Reid Foundation where he works with Boys and Girls Clubs. Uh Reed for Reed. Uh, just his demeanor. Uh, especially being at practice today, uh, having the mic in my helmet, being able to kind of listen in on the calls. Uh he has great command and you can tell he's a seasoned veteran as well and um you know he he he gets the players prepared to play. >> Bobby, what what is it about Pete Hansen's coaching style that you like? How did you get obviously he was there the whole time you were there at Stanford? Um how did you guys connect? And when you first met him, were you blown away by how tall he was? >> Yeah, definitely. Um and obviously throw throwback to his Arizona basketball days and uh uh field goal block days, blocking all the punts. Uh but yeah, Pete's a great guy. Um, great demeanor, great intensity. Um, you know, I I tell him, I took from him of my Stanford day is just conscious effort. Uh, and that's been the big thing for me. You know, takeaways don't just happen. I know what it's like when you're calling the plays and uh you're running down the sideline, you got to come back and people are asking you to call. So, as much as I can help him with the tendencies, the down in distance, um the ID formation, uh however, to help a team, >> 58 is a number that's got some story history here in Carolina with Thomas Davis. Uh did you talk to any of the legends, you know, coming in or anything? >> Yeah, actually saw Thomas Davis yesterday. Um, you know, I'm sitting at the locker right next to his picture and, uh, he was telling me he's excited for me to be here. But, uh, obviously incredible linebacker tradition here and I'm excited to add to that. Any >> pressure now? >> Nah, there's no pressure. It's just excitement and opportunity. >> Did you guys talk about you wearing 58? >> Uh, yeah. I talked to my guy Ma about it and we worked something out. >> No. Did you talk to Thomas Davis about it? >> Oh, yeah. I mean, I think he he he anticipated me wearing it and I think he's excited for me to add to that tradition. >> You mean you anticipate to wear it? Uh, we working something out. [laughter] >> Thanks, >> Bobby. four. Jackson. I do >> Heat. Heat. Tommy, are you already asking if you guys can run uh five personnel? >> Oh, yeah. We're talking about 05 personnel. Um, obviously 13's become like a pretty big craze around the league. How much does this kind of set you guys up to mix and match different guys? I know you're not obviously the play caller, but like watching it kind of uh come together, like how much versatility you feel like you have in the room? >> Yeah, I think it's uh it's awesome that each guy brings something different to the table. um you know, in our room, it's it's really good when you have someone um a lot of people that can do a lot of different things. You know, I'm a professional at the end of the day. I do my job to the best of my ability. >> Tommy, after last season, a lot of you guys talked about there's a new standard. Um, and really showing that no, uh, that having Brad at the helm and seeing the way he's running this offense has been a lot of fun being I feel like almost a complete offense now. What do you What is your vision for Panthers complete offense? >> I think just um, everyone going out there and being able to do their thing. Um, you know, throughout this preseason, everyone's been getting um a share of the rock and being able to do that uh this year has been really fun and exciting for every group and everyone's been able to go out there and just make plays. So, it's it's really fun. >> Felipe is kind of I mean has evolved a lot since 24. What What have you noticed about his game and how he's improved this summer? >> Uh Felipe, man, he's a dog, man. It's so fun seeing especially when he first got here in 24 um his development as a tight end, as a player, as a teammate is like it's out of this world, man. He's a really good football player and I'm excited for him this year, man. He's going to go out there and make plays. That's what he does and so I'm really excited for him this year. >> Having been through roster cuts a few years now, were you surprised at all that they kept 5? >> Um not at all. I mean, everyone, like I said before, has um a different aspect to their game. And so, it wasn't very surprising to us. Um, if anything, it shows what they think about us. And so, that's uh something after that uh deadline hit to see them keep five of us, it it was really uh it was kind of reassuring for us. >> Did Did you guys have a lot of deep conversations about the Houston joint practices or is there something you take away from those practices that you think you guys can really learn from? Um, I think it's really just, uh, I guess everyone being on the same page and, um, being comfortable where they are. You know, joint practices, that's the good thing about them. You get to test uh, what you like without showing really all your plays to the rest of the league. And so, I think um, in from these past during practices, we just realized we got to really focus on the details and make sure that we're just able to do our jobs. If we're able to do our jobs, we're able to succeed. You're the elder statesman, I guess, in that tight end room. >> For a guy like JT where there's questions surrounding he's going to stay, then they bring in Waller who may have the same skill set. What type of I guess wisdom are you imparting on him as he may go through some um uncertainty? >> I think JT's a professional man. He hands him he handles himself really well um not only on the field but in the building as well. And I think um there's no real story for that. It's just he's coming to work just like every one of us. Coming to work every single day ready to get better and that's what uh we've all been doing. >> Tommy, as one of the guys who's been around here for a while, what's it been like watching the improvement on defense with your defense over the last couple of years? >> Yeah, it's fun. I mean, when you add a Jaylen Phillips, De Mo Lloyd, Bobby today, but when you bring in those kind of big impact guys, >> uh, it's fun, man, because it's fun to see playmakers make plays. Um, same thing goes with Aaron Hall. You know, he's he was really impressive out there. Um, but again, that that's on me to go back and look at our processes, look at the way we do things, you know, if we do miss on a player, why did we miss on the player? text: Hey guys. >> Hey, how you doing? >> Yeah. Um, that's kind of how they put it. Um you know, just we've we've been here been here almost every day for God knows how long. Um and it's uh seeing them guys every day, you know, seeing them, you know, on the field, off the field, in the locker room, even hanging out with them outside. Um and funny enough, it it was called in it and it happened the way I wanted it to. >> Has has there been a moment where you've kind of whether it's on film or when you've been out there on the field where you're like, you know, I like I can do this? What's it like when you have to kind of know how to do all that? >> Yeah, they they that helps you out more than than than than hurts you. They can they can get out of sacks. All four quarterbacks can are mobile and can get out of sacks and, you know, it they they can extend plays and extend drives and that's that's ultimately what two two two play quarterback can do and, you know, blocking for those guys are great. >> Watson, your Florida when Anthony was there playing quarterback. Do you see some similarities between the Anthony, you know, and Jaylen in terms of traits, skill set, that sort of thing? >> Yeah, they're both really fast. They're really athletic and they they can they can run around, move around out there and, like I said, they can get out of sacks, they can get out of different things like that and yeah, they're they're very some of the about almost the same size, maybe the same height, about the same speed. Jaylen I think Jaylen's a little bit faster. >> Is there a challenge for a guy your size moving inside? Do you have to pay attention to anything specifically in that regard? >> Yeah, naturally just, you know, getting the pads down. Being being so tall, yeah, so you just got to get the pads down. >> You good? Great. Thank you, guys. >> All right, thanks a lot. Thank you. Thank you.
