Looking shiny as hell and the hood's up and the engine isn't isn't working the way you want it. I mean, that's just the way it is. They got to be driving it and the rest of it. Then it looks pretty driving down the street and the top down and the windows down and hell, you're really rolling. >> Todd, you just mentioned that uh that you're not oblivious to the outside noise about this shot. Um >> well, how is it the stadium? >> Right. So my question is right, my question is does it bother you how the fans reflect on your decision to start him? Absolutely not. Would I prefer, right, the the latter like that we'd all be on the same page? Yeah. But that has nothing to do with my decision. Can't ever have anything to do with my decision is right. My decision's got to be what's the best for the Browns week one and all the way through the season. And as long as I'm the head coach here, >> Todd, we we saw noticed Spencer Fono doing some work snapping the ball yesterday. What's the thinking there to kind of cross? >> Well, you're only going to have so many guys up, right, on game day. That's really where it comes. It's you always have to have a third center, right? It's you go through it at quarterback, right? You go through it like, uh, do we have a third quarterback up, right? And neither's good, right? Okay. If you don't have a third quarterback, what do we see with the Niners a few years ago, right? The game was over, right? It was done. They they didn't have a third quarterback and the game was over. It's the same at center. I mean, if you can't snap the football, so you only have so many guys up, right? That's you have to do the same thing really um with your specialist, right? Right. If something happened with Andre, someone's out there working a kick or your snapper, right? You're going to have Blake or somebody work because you have to have somebody because you can't you can't dress everybody. And that's really the behind it. You know, you've got a guy that uh we think can do it and we just have to have him at least somewhat up to speed. It's hard to get him the reps because he's he's still a young player at tackle. >> It seems like last one here. >> Sure. It seems like you know that explosives can take many different shapes and forms right now. Isaiah Bond is still in concussion protocol. We don't know where that's going yet, but do you feel like you have a wide range of explosives on this team that can come from many different people and look different in so many different ways? >> Sure. I think Harold Fannic could be explosive either with his route running or running people over. I think we've seen Q be explosive. We've seen Dylan Samson be explosive. I've seen number one and I've seen 12 be explosive. I've seen Jerry Judy at his best and Isaiah Bond be explosive. So, you're talking about still a very young core of players. Three of the top four receivers I just talked about were guys that are in their first second year. The two running backs and the tight end are in their second year. I mean, the future is really bright and they're only going to continue to get better because they're wired the right way. The way they go about it every day and then we got to build a system um that allows their talent to shine starting with the offensive line, then let those guys shine. >> Good. All right. Thank you.

title: Tyson Campbell Press Conference | September 1st, 2026
text: You felt like you know, you weren't out there all the time, but did you get the work you feel like you needed? >> Yeah, for sure, man. We put the work in. It was a grind for sure. Competed at a high level. It was fun. >> Did the the reason you It seemed like you weren't a team drill the whole time. Was there something nagging? Is it going to be okay? >> Yeah, I'm good. >> What's the first thing you notice about what a power receiver runs routes? >> Uh usually their split where they're lined on the field. Kind of you do the process of process of elimination of what routes they will run and won't and they won't. >> What about how to determine how they move, how well they move? What do you watch for? >> Um just like their hip fluidity in their hips, their feet work. Those light up. >> How do how do the new guys stack up in that regard, Denzel and Casey? >> Uh they stack up very well, you know, Denzel Denzel is a bigger guy, but he can run run his routes very fluid um in his routes and then Casey, you know, very explosive guy, quick feet, has twitchiness, you know, is quick and is and is fast, so >> Now that you and Denzel Ward have been together you know, for a couple of years and you know, you've had the off season here and everything, just how good can you two guys be as the cornerback tandem here? >> Um God willing we stay healthy, we can be very very good um you know, help this team win a lot of games. >> What about a week? >> I was just going to follow up. Do you I mean, do you feel like you can consider yourselves the premier uh cornerback tandem in the league? >> Yeah, talk is cheap. We just got to put it on tape, but I definitely feel like we can. >> About a little over a week away from the start of the regular year's You got some key pieces back on defense with Mason, our Oluokun, and Carson. But, in the secondary, like a week out, how much do you think it's going to be different on your play from last year? >> Um I don't think much is going to be different. Um as much as given, as much as required. So, you know, everybody owning in on their job and trusting the guy next to them that they're going to do their job. And if they're all 11 are doing their job, we'll see a lot of success. So, very confident in everybody's knowledge of the scheme. We've been, you know, running it for a while now, so. >> The safeties were talking about how, when it comes to the disguises that you're trying to do, a lot of most of it kind of is on their their responsibility. But, how much, in terms of the disguises, is there maybe on your plate? Like, and what what is that? >> Yeah, just back to the point of like everybody doing their job, you know, um you know, the the safeties can't disguise well if the corners aren't disguising well. If the quarterbacks are able to, you know, pick up man-zone tells based off um our alignments and the safeties' alignments. So, it goes hand in hand. >> Uh we talked last time we talked to you about the Jacksonville opener. Now it's getting closer. Have you like switched your head there to start to think about what that return's going to be like, or do you still need more time? >> What like thinking about it as far as like scheme or game plan? >> No, no, like you personally going back to Jacksonville, playing them week one. >> Um I mean, yeah, but um you know, that's how I haven't thought about it much, but when that time comes, I'll probably think about it. And um it's going to be fun. This is great way to start off the season um week one. Um just want to put our our our culture and our um our physicality on tape and and what we're about, so. >> Does it hurt at all to get traded? >> Hurt? Um yeah, man, you um you've been somewhere for a while, you know, and not only affects you, but your family as well. So, it's quick adjustment, but I know I had God on my side, and you know, he he got me through it. >> How does it hurt? >> Um what like? Oh, um emotionally, you know, you're emotionally attached to a city, a team, teammates, so. >> What do you remember about your time in Jacksonville? Not regarding the city and being part of the community there. >> Oh, it was great, man. I had a lot of um fun times there. I got there when I was 21, so I grew up grew up a lot. >> How have you and Denzel been helping KC and Denzel Boston get ready for what they're going to face in that open air? >> Oh, just giving them different looks, uh whether it be off or man coverage and um giving them keys on what what tells they've been giving us, so you know, we can uh uh have an advantage advantage to get against them. And then so when they go into a game, they remember those keys that we, you know, talked about, so it can help them in the game. >> How have you been finding them in terms of picking your brains, asking questions, asking what they're going to see and face? Have they been really energetic about uh >> Yeah, it just shows they're hungry to be successful um and they want to succeed in this league and in this offense and uh I think their future is super bright and uh sky's the limit for those guys. >> Hasn't um they got the Browns added the guy Blackwell last week. >> Mhm. >> Um he's been with you guys for a couple days. What does he add to this corner room? >> Uh great play making ability. Um he got a pick yesterday. Um like I said, he's only been here a couple days and he's always making already making plays, so a very smart player and you know, was a good player in in in Indy. Um so, excited to have him. >> Is it tough for that group when you bring in a couple >> Nah, cuz you you know, you want everybody to succeed, you know, so whatever it takes to make sure everybody's on the same page, you know, takes what it takes. >> And what did you see out of Michael Woods? The fact that he was able to make the team, undrafted guy, kind of really interesting story. What stood out about him to you? >> Um his grit um and his uh ambition, you know, to succeed and you know, make the team and uh his story is already inspirational as well, but just to see him the hard work he's put in day in and day out and to see it pay pay off is is been great. >> Do you kind of hold a special place for those undrafted guys that, you know, people kind of sleep on and then are able to make it? >> Yeah, you and and then the hustle it took to to get here, and to see how um how, you know, intrigued and locked in they are in their dream, you know, makes you, you know, appreciative of where you at. It's fun. >> What is this next week and a half before the first week of the season look like for you? Like you guys kind of have this like extra time, so personally like are there things you're working on? How are you like preparing for the first >> Um yeah, just, you know, preparing for the the opponent, you know, watching tape and taking care of your body, making sure you your first spot. >> Do Do you without Miles here, obviously that's a big change. Do you feel like from your spot that offenses are going to approach you guys any differently without him there that maybe they hold the ball longer than they would have um cuz they would in such a hurry to get it rid of the ball if he was there? >> I don't know. I mean, we'll have to see. Uh I feel like we still got the same D-line coach, and most of the same D-linemen in the room, so um you know, as much as Mayo was, they were they were rushing pretty well um too, so we'll see. >> I saw this morning that Michael Coach was waived, but I know that the team likes him enough to, you know, try and get him back on the practice squad or the roster soon, so I'm Did you see enough in him that you think he he can get this job done >> Oh, yeah, for sure. Well, like I can control what I can control. The business side of things, I don't know what all you know, went into him being waived, but um you know, like I said before, Mike's a great player, and whether he's here or any elsewhere, I feel like he's going to succeed. Yeah, thanks.

title: Jordan Love: 'It was a blast to be able to call plays'
text: What was your reaction when you learned that Josh Jacobs was placed on uh the commissioner's exempt list? >> Yeah, it's uh you know, it's a tough one to hear, obviously. Um still don't know exactly um you know, what the time will be uh for how long he'll be out, things like that. So, um still a lot of question marks around it, but uh it's tough and it's uh you know, it's a tough loss for the team right now and not having him around. >> How do you guys stay focused knowing that one of your star players is out right now heading into the season? >> You know, it's one of those things um where everybody's just got to just got to stay locked in to doing your job, you know, controlling what you can control. Um we talk about it all the time. It's um it'd be similar to if somebody got injured on the team. Like uh it's always the next man up mentality. Other guys in obviously in the running back room got to step up and you know, have more of a role now. Um and so, I think if you're in a a room where somebody in front of you goes down, you know, you just got to keep preparing like you're the guy, get those mental reps, so when you get do hit the field, you're ready to go. Um then I think for everybody else, it's just continue to focus on doing your job to the best of your ability um and just controlling what you can >> Is is it a is it a distraction? I mean, I feel like we kind of assume it's a distraction, but like as a pro, you know what you're doing. This has been something that has been going on for months. Is it really a distraction for you guys or not really? >> No, I think you know, to my last point, I think you know, when you're on a team um the mindset is always to focus on what you can do to be the best version of yourself every day. Um and there's going to be things that happen, you know, things come up when you're on a team um that are out of your control and it's you know, how do you how do you move on? How do you regroup? How do you handle adversity when it comes your way um or other people on the team? So, uh it's about staying focused and so, I don't think uh if you if you don't let it be a distraction, it won't be. >> Are you going to have to throw more than you have in the past? I mean, obviously you have faith in Zamir and Brandon, but without Josh, is that going to have to be more of a part of this offense? >> No, I mean, I think uh we'll see. We'll what, you know, each situation calls for in the game once you get into it. And kind of what our game plan and our approach is going into a game and then, you know, there's always in-game adjustments, but um no, I don't think as the offense it changes what we're going to be doing from that aspect. >> Has the head coach given you the offensive play calling duties given what a good job you did in the second half of the preseason finale? >> Oh man, no. You know, I think that was fun. It was a blast to be able to call plays, but no, I'm going to I'm going to go back to my role as QB1. Let Matt handle all the play calling duties like he does a great job at doing, but man, that was a blast, you know, for him to be able to let me call plays. Something I've never done and just, you know, the trust he has in me to be able to do that was awesome. So, very cool, very, you know, grateful for that opportunity and I had a blast. >> So, he brought he brought it up at halftime? >> No, he brought it up before the game. He kind of walked by my locker early pregame. Just kind of I thought he was just joking around. Like, "Hey, you want to call plays?" I was like, "Yeah." You know, I think he's just messing around and they told me before kickoff that they'd let me call the second half. So, you know, it was pretty cool. Obviously, it's preseason. You know, the the list of plays we have versus a regular season game is a lot different. What you're seeing from the defense, what you're trying to prepare for is a lot different. But, you know, still even on short notice it's kind of, you know, a little stressful to try and I wanted to put my best foot forward as a play caller. >> I mean, there's a reason that he does that, right? Is that to so that you know what it's like to be the play caller and to the communication to be on the other side? >> Yeah, I mean, I think as a quarterback there is a lot of good things that, you know, come from getting that opportunity to call plays. Like you said, seeing what it's like, trying to think through what am I going to call next? What what situation is it? And just thinking through all those things on the fly. Obviously, when you're out there on the field, you're already kind of thinking of those things and trying to think, you know, what would I call in this situation? What's Matt going to call? And just the situations in general, but it is different when you're calling plays, and you also have no control on the sideline about what happens, where the ball goes, things like that. So, um it does help as a quarterback just kind of for your process. >> When was it in your development that you might have been able to handle that with zero heads-up, total surprise? When when when at what point how far back? >> Man, um definitely after I took over the starting job, um I'd probably say you know, my first or second year starting, I felt like you know, in practice, there'd be situations where if Matt let me call two minute, my own plays, I could do that for sure. Like just my knowledge of the system and being able to call plays, but um you know, it is different when you want to call the right play. You want to call the perfect play. You want to uh obviously get a beat on what the defense is doing. Um but early on in my career, year one, year through through year three, there's no shot I would have been able to do that. >> Fourth-quarter comeback in your very first time, how would you grade yourself as a play-caller? >> Uh man, it was it was all right, you know. I think as a play-caller, you just you're calling plays, and the guys on the field are the ones out there executing. Um and so, um those guys did a great job. Kyle obviously was balling out. Um threw a lot of touchdowns in that game, which is it was great to see. Um and the guys around him were making plays, but uh yeah, they put together a great comeback. I was just I was calling plays, man. That's it. >> I think you got the speech and everything ready now. Yeah, that's what coaches are supposed to say, right? >> Exactly. >> Just the execution. >> Exactly. Come on. >> They made you look right. >> Huh? >> They made you look >> Yeah, of course. Come on. >> If [snorts] you're They had a lot of moving pieces on the offensive line because of injuries and things like that through the year. If you have to do some sort of substituting, you know, like if it's a hard time [clears throat] or else for Aaron or Zach or whatever, how's that going to affect you guys, especially going into you know, the playoffs? Do you think you can handle Guys can handle it? >> I mean, that's the expectation. These guys got to handle it. Um you know, there really is no no choice now. Uh the season's here. Um you know, you We everybody in the locker room to be ready for whatever situation is thrown their way. And those situations, you know, they'll come up at some point throughout the season of guys getting banged up, guys getting injured, and somebody else needing to step up. You know, whether you've played or not, the expectation is to be ready to be able to step in and and not miss a beat. So, I think guys are ready. I think obviously that's why you go through training camp, you go through OTAs of moving guys around, putting guys in, you know, maybe uncomfortable positions for them, something they haven't played, but just get those reps, get banked reps, and just to improve their process and get them ready. But, you know, that'll come up at some point in the season. Who knows when it'll be, but the expectation is for guys to be ready. >> Guys like, you know, Johnnu, of course, coming in here helping at the depth of the tight end room. And coach was saying that he was right next to you when he was introduced. Just adding him and obviously also Mark, too. What does that just bring for the depth of the tight end room? >> You know, it's good. I think, you know, it's always tough when someone hasn't been here for a training camp, for OTAs, for learning the system, getting those banked reps with guys. But, like you said, Johnnu has been around. He's been with Nat before. He's been in similar systems. He's a vet. Obviously, he's been around a lot of different teams. I think he'll be great to be able to pick this stuff up and, you know, get going faster than some other guys. But, it's still tough. You know, you want to have those banked reps. But, you know, I'm I love the pickups we made. I think they'll be great additions for us and you know, I think, like I said, Johnnu has played a lot of ball. So, he'll pick up right where he needs to. It's just a matter of how how quickly he can get a grasp of the full offense. >> With new guys coming in right before a week like this, and especially when you're offensive line has two tight ends, a running back, and just what's your process for kind of getting to know guys and maybe trying to figure out what they do and how maybe you think they can help on offense. Just what's your process and how you go about that on kind of a short week like this? >> Yeah, I mean, you got to kind of accelerate that process very quickly. You You I think for those guys, you know, they're almost here all day long trying to learn, you know, with their head in the playbook just trying to get up to speed on everything and for me it's, you know, trying to build that relationship as quickly as possible. Trying to get to know these guys and also just talking about, you know, if you got questions come ask me. Let's get up to speed and get on the same page with everything. You know, I think I think in terms of just you know, kind of us being on the same page is just a feel. That takes time, you know, that's something that'll you know, throughout practice, throughout the course of season we'll continue to build that stuff, but I think just understanding what to do, knowing where to be at and how to, you know, accomplish your job is the the quickest thing to get them up to speed. >> Having Caleb too, you know, that's that's a big addition too and maybe it'll change your scenery and might help him. Is that going to be good for the running back room having him in there and obviously Braelon Allen and other guys, but Caleb specifically, what does he bring to this team? >> We'll see, you know, I obviously don't know Caleb too much yet. You know, we'll get to know him and you know, see how his play style is, but you know, he was I think Steelers run a very similar offense with Aaron over there, so you know, he'll be up to speed pretty quickly and you know, if he's a guy that's got to go week one, I think it's just a matter of getting as comfortable as possible with protections and things like that and then, you know, when you get the ball just go go do what you do, you know, go go run hard and find ways to make plays happen, but I think that's where you just got to go let guys be free and let the guys go play. >> There's a big game here on Sunday and it's not you guys. It's Wisconsin and Notre Dame. Do you plan to attend that game and which team are you rooting for? >> Oh goodness. No, I I don't think I'll be at the game. You know, I think you got to stay with in state team here with Wisconsin, but I I think it's pretty cool. Cool opportunity for those teams to be able to play here. I think the stadium I assume the stadium will be packed out. So it'll be cool, but no, I don't think I'll be at the game. >> A guy like Kyle, you know, of course goes to the Dolphins, but just he said his development here for the last eight months was great learning from you and Tyron and the coaches. Is there anything that you say to him, you know, after he gets traded or you know, what was your relationship like with him specifically? >> No, it's been good. Um you know, our relationship's grown. Kyle's been here, you know, since OTAs and um we've got, you know, close with each other in that time. Um but you know, I'm excited for Kyle. You know, I think what a what a great opportunity for him. Um you know, he he balled out in preseason. Um he he played really good. Um you know, I was pretty pretty impressed by the way he went out there and handled business and um you know, that's how it goes in the NFL. You know, you get an opportunity to be go be a backup somewhere and you know, you got to take that. So, uh very cool for him. Uh very excited. He'll be with Malik. Um two guys I know pretty well. So, um they'll have a lot of fun over there, but yeah, I'm just excited for him. >> And then another one for Jaylen Mike, you know, him making the 53-man. You know, obviously pretty exciting for him and just in general, what is he going to bring, you know, to that receiver room and just that preseason game he had, I think maybe solidified, you know, what what he was able to do. >> Yeah, definitely. Um Jaylen Mike, I mean, he's made plays since he's been here. I think that's what stood out the most is just his ability to catch the ball. Um and obviously as a as a rookie, you know, it's just learning the offense. There's going to be plays you mess up, routes you might not run perfectly. So, I think it's just continuing to grow, continuing to learn each day, learn from the guys ahead of you. Um and like I said about everybody, just be ready. Um cuz your name will be called at some point to go out there. Who knows how much playing time you'll get, but you just got to be ready for whatever comes your way. Um but he did a great job throughout training camp throughout preseason to obviously put himself in a great position. >> Jordan, I could think of five starting receivers in July when you started, but talk about the competition on the back end at wide receiver this [clears throat] past six weeks. How's that compared to the other camps that you've had here? It was it was quite a show. >> It was. I mean, we had a good group of guys. Um you know, I think all those guys you talk about Shep, you talk about N'Keal, you talk about Jaylen Mike. Um they all have done good things for us and you know, I think that's a tough part you know, for the guys upstairs is making those hard decisions um and you know, you'd love to be able to keep everybody but that's just not the reality of it. So um you know, it's tough decisions and uh I think everybody you know, they did a good job in this last preseason game and then just the course of the preseason. So uh you know, this is always a tough part of year when cut downs happen and those are tough decisions but um I think all those guys did a great job trying to put themselves in a good position to make the team. >> Jordan Howard >> Obviously everybody's rooting for Marshawn. Everybody's happy that he's been able to stay healthy but now it's different, right? He's also got to be productive. What about him or what you've seen from him gives you confidence that he can do that part of it now that he's kind of got the staying healthy part knocked out of the way? >> Mhm. Yeah, I mean I think like I mentioned before you know, that's what they brought you here to do is to go be the player that they that everybody knows you can be. Um and for him it's just obviously he hasn't had the game reps that um you know, people might have seen that but he's been working. You know, he's been working. He's been watching Josh. He's been in practice doing great things. So uh it's just for him just consistency. Finding the consistency, staying healthy, going out there making plays. Um we going to be a test. You know, it's a test for everybody going against this defense especially for O-line, running backs, anybody in protection. You know, there's a lot of different looks you're getting thrown your way. A lot of things we might not have seen from our defense that they're going to be bringing. So um I think for a guy that you know, hasn't played as much ball it's just um stay locked in in the protection game and like I mentioned with other guys when you get the ball just go go go do what you do. So I know he'll be he'll be great when he gets the ball in his hands um but I think it's all those other things just getting up to speed um and trying to be as as best as you can.

title: Tucker Kraft: 'You can't replicate this locker room anywhere else in the NFL'
text: So, I've seen all these uh newcomers uh in the tight end room. What's your thoughts of, you know, John New and Redmond as they enter this tight end room? >> Yeah. Uh having John in the room is significant add. You know, I've never been in a room where we've had an experienced veteran. So, it's kind of interesting like he's coming in, we're teaching him the content of our offense, and the whole time he's like, "Oh, we've called it this here, we called it this here." You know, he's had he's had a range of different quarterbacks, talented quarterbacks. So, it's cool to get his perspective on things. I don't know if this is what you were going to say, but with the contract maybe getting done week one, maybe not. Kind of where's your head at with that? >> My head with that is, you know, from my rookie year till now, I I've come into this organization and I've I've left it all in this building, on the field, on the practice field, in the meeting room. Like everything I have, I do it with 110% effort. Um, you know, I'm not someone to to orchestrate a hole out. Mostly because they're going to find me. But, um, mostly because, uh, I I know the value I bring to this team and I think best odds of us, you know, playing in the postseason are are with me early on in the season. And and I'm just going to continue to attack everything the same way I attack my rehab. You know, I I want to be out on the field and I want to play every play that I can play. Um, so you know, I'm I'm really leaving uh now all this contract stuff, it's it's in it's in the hands of my agent now. Um, I've done all I've can all I can do, you know, this off seasonason, attacking my rehab, coming back, proving that that I'm not afraid of any contact, you know, I'm not afraid of anything and and I I hope they see that. Um, so I'm not afraid to keep working and then keep trying to make this team better. >> So, just to be clear, will you play week one without any contract? I will be on the field to play for the Green Bay Packers regardless of any contract situation because I love this team and you can't replicate this locker room anywhere else in the NFL. >> As as far as uh snap counts are concerned, that's for the birds. I uh I don't really if we're out there trying to win a game, I'm gonna be on the field to help the team win the game. If I can get a break or two, it'll probably help me out. But um I don't I I can't tell you how many reps I'm going to get in the first game because just it's such a long season and >> but I want to play. >> Do you have to fight for that? Do you have to say come on, let me loose or are they in the same page? I have to I have to fight for that in the fact that I have to I have to show that in practice. I have to show that in the preparation of the tail end of my rehab here. Um you know that I can consistently um you know sustain contact, sustain my blocks, win contested catches. Really like a lot of the back part of it is just adding like that last piece of cardio. Um because you know the less tired you are the more you can just lean on your fundamentals. I was going to say, haven't you showed that with a hit you took against the Cardinals and all that? >> Keep train rolling. >> Was that as close to game like as you'll get? The Cardinals practices. >> Yeah, that that'll be the the closest game like situation that I'll get. >> Pretty well. I mean, did you come out of it pretty well? >> Yeah, you know, I I was I felt good. I felt confident. >> Okay. I understand how you feel about your teammates and how important they are to you, but when something plays out the way this has to this point contractwise, there can be some acrimony or frustration. You're a human being. Is there still is there a little bit of a frustration that it hasn't been taken care of already, regardless of how you feel about playing for your teammates? >> I I thought about it in that lens um early on. you know, I was excited to get it started and then when it started, it almost just kind of stopped at the same time. Um, especially with, you know, my mindset and my involvement in training camp. Um, so looking at it now, like I I can't be I can't be upset. Um because you know every team every GM does this to almost every player you know like it's it's just a game of back and forth and and my job my responsibility is is to focus on the Minnesota Vikings. Can you move a guy? Can you execute a double team? Can we just, you know, get in a fist, not a fist fight, but can you play physical? I mean, I think we were pretty fortunate, you know, other than Kingston, you know, really didn't lose any players, so I mean, it worked out. I mean, some years are a little bit different than others, but you're trying to factor everything in and just go off the information they have. And, you know, there's a little bit of a projection element. And again, maybe it doesn't reach that point. And then, okay, maybe that player's on the roster now, maybe at some point he's off the roster, right? Are they tough? and are they athletic enough? Like that was his like baseline. Okay. And then there's a coachability aspect to it. You know, can they apply the principles that you're actually teaching them? All right. For an offensive lineman, you got to be able to plan your feet and you basically got to be able to prevent you from going in there. All right. So, can you stay inside out? All right. Can you just play with the right technique? Can you process information quickly understanding that the dynamics and fronts are changing? So, they're not going to run around in short. So, you got to be able to play strong, you got to play physical, you got to be able to bend enough. Um, and in the end, offensive line play is about a mentality, and it's about a mindset. And it's about toughness and physicality. So, you can't teach toughness and physicality. like if they're athletic, they're athletic, but you can't teach toughness and physicality. And then it's a mindset. And then it's just you got to be able to apply certain techniques. Can you move a guy? Can you execute a double team? Can we just, you know, get in a fist, not a fist fight, but can you play physical? And can you, again, as basic as it may seem for the interior players, can you stay inside out in protection? Right? So inside out and protection is really the the start with that premise. All right. So offensive line you got to be able to take coaching be able to apply coaching and you know understand the basic premise and principles of you know what they're being asked to do and it's hard. It's really hard. Um but in the end it goes back to mindset and offensive line play is about toughness and physicality. If they're athletic enough they can play on their feet enough they at least have a chance. Again it doesn't mean we're going to be right on every offensive lineman. I'm not sitting here telling you that, but I think we have a baseline understanding of the things that are important. >> How much of uh the evaluation process during training camp? Right? So, you go off of practice, you go off their performance in practice. some of the things they've done. You go off of some of the other things maybe done in the building. Maybe the guy didn't play that much in the preseason. So then you got to weigh a calculus of all right, you know, he didn't play, so what's that going to look like when he does play? So there's a little bit of guesswork involved if I'm being honest. Um, but you know, Demo and I have talked about this. We're just trying to keep as many good players in the building as possible, however we do it, however we feel that we got to do it. So again, if you got to carry a player, look, there's probably a number of players that were carrying that going to be inactive, you know, early part of the season or during the course of the year. So again, your depths on the roster inactive, your depths off the roster on a practice squad, they're inactive players, but they could be active. So you're just trying to do the best you can and make a determination and, you know, just try to keep as many people in the building as possible. I mean, I think we were pretty fortunate, you know, other than Kingston, you know, really didn't lose any players, so I mean, it worked out. I mean, some years are a little bit different than others, but you're trying to factor everything in and just go off the information they have. And, you know, there's a little bit of a projection element. And again, maybe it doesn't reach that point. And then, okay, maybe that player's on the roster now, maybe at some point he's off the roster, right? So, there's going to be some roster mechanics that are going to take place like during the course of the year, which I'm sure you guys are used to by now. >> All right. Thanks, You can take me.
