title: James Gladstone Speaks to the Media | Sep. 1, 2026
text: over the course of the the training camp and preseason games and we were exploring a couple different options of which Quinn came to life there Saturday morning and that was really the first time that we had engaged in conversations with the Dolphins and it didn't take long to to reach an agreement and ultimately between myself and Liam pouring into some of the the games that Quinn had in his rookie campaign felt good enough about the upward trajectory and really what he showcased over the course of those performances and trying to tap into that and continue to work with him and build with him into the future and as it relates to Carter's injury it wasn't a specific role off of that as a a next step but nonetheless appreciate what Carter did. I mean for him to come back to his hometown and be able to throw a touchdown and convert a two-point conversion. I know that that was a really special moment for him and he was doing it while that injury actually occurred prior. So he was battling through there. So major props to him for coming through for the team. >> There were 11 defensive linemen on the initial 53. How did you arrive at that number which maybe takes one linebacker away? >> Yeah, that's exactly right. There was a little bit of roster math that looks different than this time last year on that front. So lighter at LB but heavier across the defensive front and you know we had a real good competition going there and brewing on the edges for our defensive ends and that consisted of a lot of young guys and so they were doing their parts and earning their paths. Ultimately Zach Darfy went on IR with a designation for return. So nonetheless they're certainly happy with what we've seen from from that group in particular on the ends. And Brian Thomas Jr.'s emergence over the course of this off season and through the preseason games themselves is certainly lent us lent it lent us to keep him on the 53 man roster. >> Was keeping Nick Mullens part of your steal too to make sure that you had someone that could bring them along a little bit at the same time or >> Yeah, Nick's presence here, I mean, it means a ton. His familiarity with the system, it's like having another coach in the room and certainly being able to understand that he can operate our offense in the way that it's intended to is something that we don't want to just separate from. And so, that was a real conversation and authentic conversation that we had to have with Nick and appreciate very much just the way that he went about it and the professionalism that he showcased. And he's such a great teammate, such a great partner in this and is pouring right back in starting out on a practice squad and we'll see how it all unfolds here as we get into the season. >> Second year in a row getting the team down to to that 53 number, how hard were those last couple of spots? Is it Was it more challenging this go around since I guess more of these are guys you brought in? >> You know what? It doesn't matter whether or not I was a part of acquiring a player. More time you spend with them, the deeper the connection is. So, yeah, there's a little bit deeper rooted dialogue as a part of these conversations. It's not as surface level as some of them may have been a year ago. But in the same breath, um you know, that day that we go through those roster reductions, it's really met with a wide range of conversations. You got some players who are really excited and fulfilled with the fact that they earned a 53-man roster and others who may be facing a path coming to an end. And and so, vacillating between those two ends of the spectrum and everything in between is certainly an interesting dynamic to walk through. But can't thank the guys that came through over the course of this offseason and training camp enough. Those that are still with us and those who are going in a different direction to get us to a place where we feel good about where we are heading into the season. >> Heading into Friday's preseason game, was Brian Thomas Jr. someone you kind of had circled on the 53 or how much of his performance on Friday really sell you that he had to be on the roster? >> Yeah, there was still more to be done and I think he went out there and and continued to prove it. He left no doubt. Um I think anybody that was on that sideline, in those stands, or watching on TV uh could feel that. I think uh he himself uh probably felt that. It wasn't shortly thereafter the next morning um that I walked past him and it was very brief interaction and all I said was congrats and he said I really appreciate it and all I said was earned and he said, "Yeah, I feel that." And uh you could just sense his confidence uh on the grass that night uh in the locker room post and that next morning because that's something that we preach and I think uh our players certainly uh are coming to grips with it, but when you earn it, you're going to get it and we're not afraid or going to shy away from the fact uh that when that is is something that surfaces to the top to pursue it regardless of where you started, regardless of how much you you make. Uh we're trying to win football games and we're going to do what we feel like's in the best interest of the Jacksonville Jaguars and our team heading into 2026 and best 11 are going to get out there. >> James, when camp got underway, did you have a 53 or a number that you had either written down or in your head? And how much did that change Sunday? >> Did I have a 53-man roster set ahead of training camp? >> head like what you thought the 53 would be as camp began and how much did that change? >> Uh I did not. I can tell you that uh like to keep things pretty uh fluid and organic. Um and you know, as you inch through it, uh you kind of set certain thresholds and and dates on the the calendar for check-ins to begin building that out and shaping it and shaping some of the dynamics in a more formal matter. Uh but walking in the door at training camp, that wasn't the case uh and all the way up until uh the day we had to make the calls to players to bring them back into the building and let them know uh that we were moving in a direction or not. It was something that we we kept on the table and and remained fluid with from start to finish. >> James, a little bit off topic, but a couple parts of this are Parker Washington. How would you describe the tone and the progress talked between team and player? >> Yeah, there's been a lot of positive progress. A lot of good back and forth. I think you know, as I think back to this time last year, Parker was coming off a really strong training camp. And over the course of the first half of the season, he had certain games really really showed up and made a significant dent. And it was a little sporadic. By the time mid-season hit, started to feel his presence a little bit more and more. Really down the stretch in those first in those final four games, his impact was notable. And he's carried that momentum through the off-season program and into training camp. So certainly love where he's at at heading into the season. Look forward to seeing that show itself once we get into games and for so many other people to see it, but really in a good spot with that. >> Following up on that, are both sides comfortable with talks going into the regular season? And what is it about his makeup that says he he can handle that? >> Yeah, I think there's a ton that you know, he showcases just on a daily basis about who he is, how he operates, the focus, the determination, and the consistency. All that stuff is is rooted in just his actions more than any words that he speaks. In terms of any discussions around contract extension or what his future holds, I think we're certainly in a position where we're not going to stop talking and trying to figure something out. And I think we've certainly not shown any unwillingness to do stuff even during the course of the season as you point back to last year. >> With the trade for Daniel a couple weeks ago, did the folks ability knowing your projected comp picks in the future kind of help you guys, you know, be able to make a move like that? Does that kind of show the value of what they can give you guys moving forward? >> I I appreciate the question. I think that's something in the spring we highlighted quite a bit about you know, the idea of going down the compensatory pick formula approach and not signing immediately some of the street free agents. Really where we were going to turn our attention to was during training camp in the regular season knowing that we had a larger stock of future draft picks to utilize to answer any questions that we might need to in those moments. So yeah, that gives us more flexibility to pursue those paths and those options and you know, I think that that's an ever-evolving strategy as to whether or not you're going to deploy that one year after the next. It was where we found ourselves this past cycle, but I think that's why you probably saw some willingness there not to say that we weren't unwilling a year ago because we were. I think the equivalent to that was probably Tim Patrick and using a sixth-round pick to get him from Detroit and you know, we still have you know, avenues for pursuing those into the regular season as well. >> Is he right now a little bit ahead of schedule and maybe where you thought he'd be at this point? >> I think he's in a really good spot. He uh he has earned a lot of trust, a lot of equity from both teammates and coaches over the course of the off season and training camp. It was really down the back stretch of training camp that you start to see his superpowers show up and his flaws begin to diminish and I think he really settled in and has put himself in a position to really help our team right off the bat. >> Speaking of the keys to the win, what did you think about the receivers, CD Williams, Josh Hammond? >> Yeah, those guys have done a a great job and I think that room as a whole has done a great job together and all of them you know, give a lot to the one beside them and they've done a great job of absorbing information uh, really soaking up and observing the way that others go about business and have tried to put that into action. Now, innately the two of them are, uh, are certainly in the category of rooted in intangibles and I think that shows up, uh, in in their routines and in their consistency. I think, uh, other than that it's just getting out on game days and performing in a way that their preparation allows them to with quieted mind, uh, but they certainly round that group out uh, in a real way and have earned trust from so many, uh, in a rapid manner. It's not easy to do, uh, up at up until this point as a rookie and, uh, I don't think that there's anybody that would talk about those two and flinch at the idea of really contributing over the course of the season. >> How encouraging by Trevor Lawrence's camp and Travis Etienne's camp? >> Both of them have continued to climb and get comfortable in in their roles and how they're operating and how they're moving. You know, from a a perspective, you know, pointing to Trevor, there have been quite a few more wow moments throughout the course of this training camp, uh, than we may have seen a year ago today. Uh, I think that speaks to his comfort, uh, in testing things, right? And really, uh, not ever second-guessing himself because of his familiarity and understanding of intent behind plays he can get away with. Um, so that element has certainly been something that I've I've been inspired by. Uh, I think that'll show itself over the course of the regular season as well as he continues to to build game chemistry with our our pass catchers knowing that that spreads across receivers, tight ends and running backs. Uh, I think from Travis's perspective, uh, I think that's a a great work in progress knowing that he's put a lot more focus on the defensive side down the back end of the of training camp stretch uh, and still getting his plays on offense but really settling in so that that defensive backfield can have the continuity that it needs. >> What impressed you about Christian Braswell that he outed a guy like Jabari Muhammad? >> You know, I think there's there's tough dynamics with a lot of those decisions. Christian's been there, done that. Uh has a a notable role on special teams come game day. And you talk about actives versus inactives and what it is that is going to differentiate guys. Uh whereas Jabari clearly a hungry player who has made his presence felt in a few different settings, whether that's our own internal practices, joints, or preseason games. I think the the fun thing about the cornerback position in in particular is uh you know, they all give up receptions, right? They all uh have a chance at giving up points. So, inherently they're going to fail. And uh what I appreciate so much about uh the guys that sign up for that position and what Jabari did at the end of the New Orleans game, you go from a play where you get a reception called on you uh as New Orleans is trying to mount a a final drive to to win. And then you end up getting a DPI. So, back-to-back negative plays. And then we get an op where the ball's coming your way and you end up with a PBU, the buzzer sounds, and game's over. He looks around like, "Why the heck would they even try me?" You know, that level of confidence to to continue to perform at a high clip despite negative plays having just happened is a really unique thing that many that play that position possess. And so, that certainly stood out to me specifically with Jabari. Uh but nonetheless, when it comes down to Christian, his experience, uh his comfort in our system, uh all those things when we think about the game day active list, uh really jump out and lend itself to his the decision to keep him in that place. >> When you look at three uh defensive ends over the last couple of years making it as undrafted free agents. Is that just like a super rare situation that's happened here? >> It's not a position that typically lends itself to undrafted college free agents making it on initial 53-man rosters or A or B performing in games through that. So yeah, to to have that happen back-to-back cycles is unique. I got to give a ton of credit to our coaches and scouts who are paired together in that process um and executing those signings post-draft, prioritizing the list of players who they're going to pursue. Um I I think that that's a very sound approach that we take, but it's a collaborative approach and it's not any different than in comparison to the decisions we make across the roster through other avenues of acquisition. Uh so I think it's a reflection of of that collaboration for sure, those individuals themselves and earning the ops. Uh but at this point in time, got to say excited to see what the the real output shows once we get into some true action. Uh but yeah, I don't think that that's a a normal result. >> How was Anton settled in at left tackle? And if Cole wasn't injured, would you have made that move? >> That's a good question. Don't know about uh the second part of that question. Uh but think that he is naturally uh someone who fits the bill for the left tackle spot, and I think he would tell you that as well. Uh is where he's most comfortable naturally, and uh you know, I don't think anybody would uh say that they're concerned or have uh some sense of questioning whether or not he can perform at a high level there or any different than he did at right tackle. And Cole, on the other hand, uh says something really similar. Is that look, I can do either. Uh naturally, I feel best suited at right tackle, but from a Cole's perspective, he He play any position across the offensive line, regardless of what side it's on. Um so, I think it's it's certainly a a new take, but one that we feel really strongly about heading into the season. >> Hey James, how much with a couple of the roster moves, with then Hightower reworking his deal, how much flexibility do you have come trade deadline to add veteran money? >> Yeah, I think that that's uh that's a a move to make so that we're not forced to do anything should we pursue an avenue. Um and so, we want to make sure that we have the flexibility that we need to keep things on the table as the season progresses. And uh in the same breath, we're always going to do our part to you know, consider all options. And um through that lens, not all those are going to come to uh to the table or to public's understanding. Just I think the understanding that we are uh always going to turn over every every stone is certainly going to be the case. >> Have the guys in the running back group shown you enough to feel really comfortable with this season? >> Look, I don't know if anybody feels what you might call like the comfortable. I think there's certainly still a sense of urgency that I feel across the the team, the roster, and each position group. Uh but I do think that the combination of those guys is uh is certainly showing itself in a positive way. And you know, as I think back to to New Orleans and the joint against them, to Carolina the joint against them, and then Tampa Bay closing things out in that joint, our run game certainly uh became a focal point in each of those progressively. Um and I think that that's a really positive element because a year ago uh we were in a position where we were relying heavily on a run game over the course of that first half of the season. And so, to get out into on a fast start in that phase of the game will be really important. And uh I think that that group of RBs right now feels confident, but certainly urgently attacking uh the op that lies in front of him. >> When it comes to Cole, are you happy with the progress he's made in his recovery and just in the fact that he's on the active 53 and no non-destination or anything? >> Yeah, certainly. I think he's in as good of a spot as we could hope for and obviously we got about a week and a half more time to to get him work in a a more authentic football environment, team settings, and those sorts of things, but he's in a great place. >> And then Ameer Abdullah, I mean just seeing what he did over the course of training camp and then his experience, I mean what what stood out to you the most when you're like, "I mean this guy can kind of complete that room." >> Yeah, I think similar to some of the other comments I've already made, his daily routine, his mode of operation, there's when you when you get a chance to see it first hand, it's no surprise why he's still in the league a dozen years later and you know, he carries that that routine out into his performance each and every day in practice. Um, you know, we gave him a ton of work against New Orleans in the joint, didn't play him in that preseason game just being mindful where he's at in his career. He comes out in the next against Carolina and just looks like he's operating at a little different pace than a lot of the other guys that are playing against him and you know, so I think he's still got plenty left in the tank, but you know, his knowledge base is certainly one that's good for a a relatively inexperienced and young running back room that's surrounding him. So I think he's certainly played his part up to this point and look forward to seeing how that unfolds over the course of the regular season. >> How how comfortable did Albert Okwuegbunam look in terms of the role you envisioned for him? >> Yeah, I think he slided right in as expected and you know, in 12 personnel groupings, you'll see him out there with Strange right away and really has has come into his own and is showcasing his personality. You can feel that tight end room, especially between him and Tanner really bring some some youthful energy and and think that that's a good thing. It continues to make it so that we have position groups that are you know built in depth that aren't just young or old or veteran and youthful. I think that combination of those two in conjunction with Britain and Quinton is a really good pairing. >> Um, Miller comes competition. How pleased were you with the way that played out there both of them can help you? >> Yeah, I think it's really exciting to know that neither one of them if thrust into a full-time role is going to be in a position that we feel like there's a void. At this point in time, you know, we're really excited about the progression of each and knowing that Ventrell's walking in the door with a a more experienced standing. I think that'll certainly show itself in a positive light and Branson continuing to take steps knowing that his contributions on special teams are still going to be something that really adds value on a on a game day operation. >> In January you talked about your vision for Travis. I think he was in month two of his rehab at that time. How has that vision kind of evolved or has it evolved at all now that he's back on the grass and with the team full? >> Yeah, I don't think that that vision has shifted in any way. I think that great part about having him on our roster is that as dynamics shift over the course of an off-season over the course of the regular season, you get to use him in different ways. And as it stands the composition of our our roster would indicate, hey, defensive output full-time is going to be where we see him contributing in the most ways and then supplementing that on offense in the instances that it makes sense to be in as productive and efficient as we can be while also threatening any defense that lines up against him when he's at wide receiver is Uh, certainly something that we're looking forward to. >> James former general [clears throat] manager here said that rookies are not drafted to play immediately unless they're a top top pick. Um, I look at the roster here. Yeah, I mean, you six or seven guys could really be major contributors. Has this changed and even with 19 returning starters is is a game change where rookies are expected to do this early on or is it just kind of set up that way because of the decisions that you made? >> Yeah, that's an interesting question to dive into. I do think that you know, every player's path is going to be quite a bit different uh, whether they're first round, seventh round, undrafted college free agent, second-year player, third, fourth. I I think while they're on that rookie contract, I mean, you can see a number of guys that just last year as they were entering their third seasons really began to come into their own. Uh, whereas before that, there were guys who in their second and first were already proving who they were. Uh, so I don't know that you can tag a uh, really concrete answer to that. I think everybody's going to show up at different intervals in different ways and they're not all going to look alike in terms of their contributions, but uh, certainly feel good about where we are in terms of the rookie class. Uh, the volume of guys that are going to be getting hats on game day uh, walking into week one as it's projected and certainly can't wait to see what that ends up showing up like and looking like, uh, but in terms of the progress up to this point, uh, I think there's some really positive positive elements to it. >> For Caleb Brandt, >> For Caleb Brandt, so how important was it not just for him from your guys' perspective, just to see him this preseason get those kind of game-like reps? >> That was critical because uh, I think you can fit him in essentially as a rookie this year without any real action a year ago. Uh, so to be able to put him under the lights and be able to get the pads pop and tackle again, I think that's a a really helpful piece of the puzzle and a necessary piece for his sake. I think he'd tell you as much as well, but you know, that safety room as a whole, I mean, it's relying heavily on Eric Murray and Antonio Johnson leading the group with a bunch of younger guys behind them. So, look forward to their development. Not all that different than what Antonio was able to showcase last year. Cuz at this point, you know, a year ago, he was one of the best gunners that we had on the team and potentially across the league and you know, continued to level up his play and get comfortable in the defensive system to a spot where he's able to get his hand on the ball a lot, be used in a variety of alignments and really became a weapon through that lens and you know, so his progression is something we're really looking forward to. Not any different than those guys that are behind them, just on a different timeline. >> Is that one of the best parts of this job, seeing stories like Antonio, even Braden Coms going from practice squad last year to on the 53 this year? >> I think that's certainly an element that brings some fulfillment with it. Obviously, we're focused on winning football games, but that's a underlying piece of the puzzle that you certainly look at and can, you know, get a little grin or a smile to your your face when some of that stuff shows itself. >> And James, on the card obviously out the first four weeks, how confident are you that maybe not week five, but a couple weeks after that he can become an option? >> I think he'd be quickly thereafter the threshold for return to to get in. >> Okay, let's cut it off right there, guys. Thanks. Thanks for your time. [clears throat] Appreciate the time. >> Mhm.

title: DL Zach Sieler meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Glad the feeling healthy. Our coach just said he'll be ready for the opener. Was the injury ever a concern in terms of you worrying it could be it could seep into the regular season? >> I mean, any injuries obviously gets concerning and you got to take it with uh carefully, but honestly no, I was very excited and yeah, it's a setback I didn't want it, didn't plan on it, but to tackle like anything else and I tell the guys that have the same thing same thing's going on like hey, control you control. So, wasn't part of my plan, but find a way to make it better and hopefully come through it stronger. So, I feel great. Um and I feel good to be out there again with those guys and run around and set the tone. >> At this stage of your career having been through so many training camps, is that something that you can just get right up to speed right away? >> [laughter] >> No, it's not. I mean, at least in this for the D-line O-line for myself, at least I've always felt like like I need the reps. I don't care what it is. I'll start to feel antsy. Um there's it's just really hard to simulate O-line D-line play, reading blocks, holding up blockers, stuff like that and on your own. Um and these guys, the training staff here, Todd, Kyle, all them, now do a great job of getting as close as you can. Um I think they had me doing something like 35 some laps in the pool or something like that. So, little bit of resistance, but but yeah, you can only do so much, but when you get back out there felt good today. >> How did your experience dealing with the three rookies on the D-line last year prepare you for leading one of the youngest teams in NFL [clears throat] this year? >> Yeah, um obviously with the the three rookies last year it's not just the leaders, it's also the rookies and those guys and the willingness to learn and to want to be a sponge and to really try to take their game to the next level and I think Solly, Haf, all these guys have done an amazing job with the guys that we have here and the guys that are in the room. Um in the D-line room, defense, the whole team is just they just put together a great group of guys where they want to win, they want to learn, they want to be situationally smart, aware football players and that's how you win games in the league. So, I'm really excited for these guys. It's been great to be out there again and communicate and work through uh, work through the kinks and take this bonus week we have right now and run with it. So, and take it to week one. >> As someone who arrived the way you did from Baltimore, when a day comes along like yesterday and you see seven guys picked up on the waiver wire, Harris, what your reaction is when you see that number? >> I mean, it's part of the game, right? Like it's it's a sad part of the guys that make the 53 then the next day they're cut, but you know it's part of the games and it's you again, you control your controllables. Uh, I've always in Baltimore I was a guy Jaco Willix, Navy Navy SEAL guy, but his big thing was just saying good. You can say good, you're alive, you're kicking still and that's something I did from early on. Um, I got cut in Baltimore I just good, okay, what's next? And then I got a call from Miami and just taking it and run with it. Um, so I've tried to embrace that and just in everything in my life and my game and I tell these young guys the same thing like, hey look, good, okay, what's next? How can I do the next thing? What can I do How can I show the next team or these guys if I'm back in practice squad, how can I be the best player possible to trust me on Sundays to be out there. Um, so, you know, I just tell those guys and try to help however I can. Having been in those shoes before and just do what I can to help them get through it. >> I think Clark might have asked you a few months ago about being an older player on a rebuilding team. Did you and Sullivan ever have a conversation about that where you just were curious about where you stood and he told you he sees you as an important piece despite the fact we're going younger. Did that conversation ever happen? >> Uh, probably not in that sense, but me and Flo did sit down a couple times and just kind of talk like talk ball and like what the visions for the team are the plans for myself and the Dolphins and all that stuff and you know, it's just it's been exciting to have these guys uh, back me and just fully embrace um, what I've done here and say, hey we want to keep you around and keep going. So, uh, it means a lot to have that and I I appreciate these guys and all that they're doing. I'm really excited for where this is going. Um, like I said, the guys they've brought in have been incredible and just to be able to work with these guys and get to learn and grow has been exciting. I'm really excited for this season. >> Zack, we know physicality is a big emphasis for Hafley. Where do you see the physicality surface in this team? Run game, front seven at >> Every play. Every play. Every player, every play. 11 hats to the ball, not turn down a hit and just running running every single play. It starts in the front, ends in the back with the DBs, receivers, everybody getting the block. You know, offensively they kept saying no block, no rock and I love that. You got to prove your trust and prove what you can do. And uh it even starts I was actually just talking today about the guys in the practice squad and guys coming back and stuff like that. Hey, look, like it's about building trust. It's about making those practice squad reps look as good as possible, clean as possible so they'll say, "Hey, look, we need to see this guy on Sundays." And so it starts from the ground up from practice all the way till Sundays. >> So you would definitely describe this as a physical team? >> We got to do it first. We haven't put any money out there yet. There's been no games. Once but I fully plan on that's exactly what we're going to be. >> Zack, how how soon can you tell if a young guy has it? You know, like I I remember when Davante got here everybody said, "Okay, that guy's a player." To have so many of those young guys, how soon [clears throat] can you tell? >> You know, it's being older now. Uh No, it it it's definitely a different light on things. When I was younger, obviously I was just figuring things out and go. And I'm sure there's plenty of coaches and that's why I ended up here and not staying in Baltimore that were like, "Hey, I don't know if he's got it." And they moved on. Um so some guys it takes longer and some guys like a Davante it's like, "Hey, look, this guy's got it." Um but I think what Hafley and so on these guys have been saying from day one is like, "Look, you might not have the technique right, you might not have this right, but if you can be in your spot, be lined up and do the technique we're trying to teach you to do and do it fast and physical, we can work with that." Um and to grow as a player and grow as to see these guys kind of grow throughout camp, myself included, has been really fun to just take this and take these new coaching techniques and style of plays and all that kind of stuff and work into the team we're becoming now and show it up on Sunday for the Vegas game. >> Was there a moment this summer in the huddle where you could tell that Jacob Rodriguez had matured to a point where he probably plays a big role this season? >> I'd say the spring, man. He stepped in and just once he got that defense rolling to take that to to be a rookie coming and taking take that charge and lead that the huddle cuz obviously he's the green dot right now and to take control and to see just to see the game and talk to him and I talked to him a few times during the preseason games and just see how he sees the game from his lens at this age has been incredible. Really excited to play with him this season having behind me. >> 2019 Um the last two games you played the team [clears throat] won. >> Uh-huh. >> Um >> How's it? Bengals New England? >> the Bengals and the Patriots, yeah. Overtime and a three-point win. >> Yeah, so so clearly you were the the key to to those two wins at the >> You could say that? No. >> Yeah, I'm curious. Obviously the perception is that that's the last time that the Dolphins did a dramatic rebuild. Um what [snorts] do you remember about how the players were feeling that season? And then at the end, what did you notice about what was achieved? >> 19 when I got here, that was just hey, let's go out there and play. I was here for 3 weeks, so I really wasn't able to absorb. I was celebrating with guys I didn't know their names. But 20, that that that season what I loved and what we had I think going into that year. I don't remember where we ended up, but I think we were one of one game away from the playoffs that season. But 20 was backs to the wall. Doesn't matter who you are, you're going to go out there and play fast and physical, we can use you. And to have that mindset and to be situationally aware, to run through two-minute drill situations, different like end of quarter, end of half, end of game, all these different things, you that's where you win football games. Obviously it's all 60 minutes, but to be a smart and uh What's the saying? More teams lose the game than win. Um to put ourselves in a situation where we are in the right spot to win games. And I fully believe that that's where we're trending, where we're going. >> Every person and every coach is different. >> Mhm. >> So, Jeff Hafley is not Brian Flores. Different people. >> Yep. >> But, are there any parts of the messaging uh that are similar? >> For me, what I've loved um from what from Flo was here and what Half preaches now is just that situationally tough, smart football team. We are not going to beat ourselves. And uh sure there might be issues, but it's how how do you go through that? And that goes back what I said earlier, where you say, "Good. Okay, fine. 15-yarder, fine. Good. Whatever." Find a way to get make it work and keep going. And uh to be smart and be situationally tough and aware um every single snap is that's what's going to take to win games this year. >> Also similar to 2019, a lot of people on the outside don't believe this team is going to win a lot of games. Uh do you embrace an underdog mentality >> Man, I I mean, honestly, I I I don't like to listen to all that stuff. I really don't watch that. I I know what they say. I hear things. People send stuff, sure, but what matters is what we're doing in this building day in and day out and what we see in the dark. And then that comes to light 17 times a year. Um so, it's what we have to do put our best foot forward for those games. >> How have you seen Cayden Proctor grow since you know, first day he arrived? >> He's been great. Um the whole rookie class really I got to um talk them up on how well they've just professionalism from day one. Um they understand the assignment like, "Hey, look, you guys are going to be playing games. You got to take this from day one and go." Um Obviously, O-line, D-line can get chippy during camp and during preseason and stuff like that, going back and forth each other every single day. Um but, from him, Pat Paul, Jonah, the whole front, AJ, Brew, all those guys just to be professional every day and like between the whistles, you're going hard every time. >> [snorts] >> After the whistle, "Hey, what you see there? Or what why'd did that? Or what did I do?" To make each other better? Um has been incredible and he's he's a part of that just like anybody else. So, he's done a great job jumping in and stepping into that role and uh playing.

title: ILB Jordyn Brooks meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Jordan, we worried about you for a little bit when we saw the compression sleeve. Were you ever concerned about being ready for the opener or you always knew that it wasn't going to be anything long term? >> No. Um I know it wasn't long term. It was just something I had to uh get taken care of. Um couple days, couple weeks. Um it's all good to go now. >> Jordan, tell us about the the physicality of this team. That's something that Halfley has uh stressed. You heard me asking Han about it. Where does the physicality surface with this team? Run game, front seven of the defense, attitude. Tell me about that. >> You want it at all positions. Um to me, physicality is a choice. Um that takes no talent. It's just a decision that one man's got to make whether he wants to be physical or not. And so that's a mindset that we're trying to bleed into this team um on a consistent basis. It's been some times where we had very physical practices. It's been times that we haven't, right? And so, um, that's what practice is for is try to build that consistency so to when we get to the games, that's what shows up on tape. And so, that's what we're in the process of doing, um, being the most physical toughest team that we can be. With so many young players and young newcomers, how much of a responsibility do you along the old old guys on the team feel about, you know, getting everybody on the same page, writing a wrong as quickly as possible if you see something not right? >> Yeah, it's a great responsibility. Um, what are we the youngest team now? Whatever. Um, it's a lot of young guys, a lot of inexperienced guys. And so as older vets on the team, um that's a responsibility that that we have to be responsible for. And um it's going to be a gauntlet of a season. Um when you got such young guys, it's easy for young guys to, you know, kind of ride the wave, the highs and lows in the season. So our job is to be somewhere in the middle and um and help those guys in in the best way that we can. And so, uh, we're up for the challenge, um, and excited for this upcoming season. >> Were you surprised Dodson was let up? >> Yeah, I was, um, somebody that's, you know, off the field, you know, one of my best friends, uh, somebody that I've got to know, um, very well over the last three years. So, just seeing him go that, you know, that's that's always difficult. And then, you understand like the business side of things. So, um it's hard not to take some things personal um in this business, but um I'm excited that he's, you know, already found a new home. Um spoke to him. He's in great spirits. Type of person that he is, he's just going to keep keep going. So, I'm not worried about his mental or spiritual right now. I know he's going to be all right. But, uh it does suck to not have him as a teammate anymore. >> On your side of that coin, uh what have you seen in terms of growth and development from Jacob Rodriguez in order to go out and win that battle? Yeah, I mean, Jacob is a um I like to say like a rookie vet. Um he's already seasoned. Um whatever he was doing at Texas Tech, you know, he was doing the right things. Came in very knowledgeable of the game, very mature, um and just ready to go. So, he's just gotten better and better uh since since OTA's, honestly. And so, I'm excited to see his growth and um what he does this year. Did did what did you learn, if anything, from watching Cer deal with rookies last season and bring them along and how do you think that'll help you this season? >> Um, I learned that it's a challenge, you know what I mean? We got a bunch of young guys and you know, they need guidance, you know what I mean? It's just like like a a baby needs his mother, you know what I mean, in a sense. But, um, they need that guidance. Um, watching Cer have to, you know, carry that weight last year. um you know it's not easy and so we got to do it again this year. Um and like I said earlier like that's the challenge that we're up for, you know what I mean? And I think that we are the right vets to be in that position to help these guys cuz we've walked those shoes. We we've been burned many times in this game. Um so I've got a lot of knowledge to give to the young guys to help them. And so like I said, I'm up for the challenge. >> Kind of along those same lines, how will you evolve, I guess, as a leader this year? man, I've got a it's you never stop evolving. Um, you never stop growing. Each year is different and each year presents a different challenge. Um, and so one thing I've just learned is that you got to have patience. You got to have patience with the process. And I'm talking individually for myself. Uh, patience with the process of of us as a team, as a defense. Um, and learn how to stay steady. And like I was saying earlier, not ride the waves, but stay somewhere in the middle. Um, even when things are great and when things are bad, stay somewhere in the middle. So, that's something that I'm constantly learning each and every day and trying to grow as as a leader. Jordan, >> has the emphasis on physicality this year been new during your Dolphins tenure, or has it been the same the last few years and it's no different this >> I mean, I mean, every team is going to preach physicality, you know what I mean? Um, I don't think it's something that's like we everybody preaches it. Um, I think the difference is is do we practice what we preach is that's that's going to make the difference. You know what I mean? Um, do we actually go out there and be physical rather than just talking about it? And so, um, it's been the same message since I first stepped foot in this league from every team I've been on. Everybody wants to be physical, but like I said, it's a choice. We have to make the decision to go be that kind of team. And so I think we got the guys in this locker room to be that. >> JB, if I could get you to be selfish for a second, um, you've got the the allp pro, you led the league in tackles, you've got, I think, five straight seasons with 100 tackles or more. Which of those is most important to you, which do you want to replicate this year and why? >> Um, I'm not going to say it's not important cuz those are goals that I was reaching to get. Um, but right now it's not important. It really doesn't matter no more. Um, we got a new season ahead of us. Um, I'm just blessed to be here, man. Um, I thank God every day for the posi the position that he's put me in to be able to um to lead a group of men and and play this this beautiful game of football, man. Um, it's something I don't take for granted. And so, I guess the things that I've accomplished in the past are just a byproduct of just my love for the game. um you know and so every time I'm on the field I'm going to give everything I got to help us win. So that's that's the mentality. >> Do you feel like the team has an underdog mindset? >> Uh yeah. I mean I don't think we have a choice. Honestly, I don't think it's one outlet on social media, anybody that's got us picked to win anything. You know what I mean? Not that it matters, but it's just what it is. I don't I don't think any of our opponents respect us, you know what I mean? So, 100% underdog mindset and I think that's always the best position to be in, you know what I mean? Um, and so we're going to carry that mindset into the season and uh have that us against the world mentality and and you know, do our best to win win football games.

title: RB De'Von Achane meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Devon, tell me about this rushing game. I think you guys were 13th in the league last year like 120 yards per game. Do you think you can be that good? Do you think you will be better this season and why? >> Um I'm I'm going to go better cuz like I said um we try to get better every year. For as me, I know the line want to be better. And I know as a team we want to be better. So um like you said we 13 last year, so I mean if we anything higher than that um um it should be something that we don't like. I mean but as a running back, you know, I'm always better every year. >> What do What do you like about the the run game? I mean this this offensive line seems to be very equipped to to run blocking. What What do you like about the run game so far? >> Um like I said um I like it a lot, man. Like I said it's it's I it really is the bond that we create. I know we we all been here now for a minute now. Um I mean KP, of course he the the rookie, but like he fit in well. Like I said um I think everybody comfortable up there and I feel like when you comfortable you can play faster and you don't got to think. >> I heard the the team will be voting for captains this week. Is that something that you would want to do that would be important to you this season? >> You said are we voting now? >> No that that Well, Halfhill told us that on Thursday and the team will be voting for for captains. So is that something you would like to do be a captain on this year's team? >> Oh most definitely. I feel like um I mean who don't want to be a captain? Um you know, you get in the game day you got to see on your chest and I feel like um you know, I could be a great leader. I could be a great captain for this team and I mean if I if I get that vote then I'm happy with it. >> Kind of along those same lines, like what will it take to lead this team? Obviously you have like one of the youngest rosters, new coach, um one of the second hardest schedules in the in the league this year. Just >> Well, I would say all of us. Um it ain't not just going to be just one person. I mean we might have, you know, a couple captains, but it's not just going to be us up there out there on that field as well. Um like I said the young guys, um like I said it's a business and it's a league they knew they came into and I feel like, you know, they ready to play. They hungry and I mean you know, no matter how old you is when you out there in the field, I feel like they going to perform. >> Devon, you guys have some new faces at the quarterback position, at the backup quarterback position. Um I I guess how how long do you think it's going to take them to get acclimated to this offense? I mean, you you've become acclimated to it. How long do you think it'll take a quarterback to get acclimated to this offense? >> Uh I don't know, man. I mean, I'm pretty sure it's going to take some time, but I mean, you know, when when you play that position, I mean, they're pretty smart. I feel like they can learn on the fly, I mean. I mean, I ain't even they shoes, so I I don't know. They got to learn a lot, but like you said, QB1, he he the lead leader of the offense. And like you said, even though he's a backup, you never know what might happen. So, to be to play that position, you got to be smart. So, I feel like they'll they'll learn pretty quick. >> When it comes to that QB1, do you think you guys form the fastest quarterback-running back tandem in the league? >> Yeah, most definitely. I don't see no other duo that's like that like fast. You know, somebody can have fast running back, but not like a fast quarterback like we do. So, yeah, I feel like we one for sure. >> Ronald, I know uh physicality has been a big thing with with Huf and this team. Where do you see that physicality showing up? I mean, is it in the run game? Is it in the front seven of the defense? Where where do you see that physicality showing up with this team? >> Like you said, when when you when you running the ball, y'all going to be physical. Like you said, but it also comes in when you got when you got receivers blocking. And um you know, DBs who don't want to get blocked. So, I feel like, you know, with us, you know, passing against defense and our receivers blocking, DBs not trying to get blocked, they actually want to come and make tackles. I feel like I mean, that's what we've been working on all camp, and I feel like we just everybody just ready for week one. >> Ronald, you were you were successful from day one when you came here, had a good year as a rookie. But now that you're a veteran, in what ways do you think you're a better back today than you were when you started out in this league? >> Uh like I said, just learning more. Like you said, um you can never um grasp enough knowledge of of game. And you know, me just understanding the defense a lot more for when I came in. Like I said, I'm in my fourth year and I'm in the I'm in the same offense that I've been in since I first got here. So, that's a good thing to be to uh to be into. So, for me it's just, you know, learning the defense and you know, knowing personnel and who out there and uh defense tendencies. >> Looking back, how did Hackley's training camp differ from McDaniels? >> Uh I mean I mean, we we practice hard regardless of who coach. I just feel like you just their personality was different. I wouldn't I wouldn't say like I mean, we was doing this with this person, this this this this this person. Um just different coaches. >> Along that same vein though, what differences have you noticed just about roster construction that go from one of the oldest teams in the league to now the the youngest team in the league. >> Um like I said, we do got a lot lot of young guys, but I mean, that that ain't going to stop us from going out there and trying to win. Like I said, I feel like we can win with the team we got. And I mean, just cuz, you know, we we a young team, I feel like the young guys are ready to play. >> Zonovan, on on that type of I remember when you came in, all the vets knew you were you were ready to go. The confidence you have, like you said, it's a young team, but have you seen that talent, which is why you maybe you're you're more confident? >> Yeah, I'm going to say like I said, um I'm you know, very confident in the the guys around me. Uh I feel like they're ready to go and prove themselves and uh that's how I was when I came in like as a rookie, you know, knowing that like people looking at you like a rookie, oh, he not ready. But I mean, I I feel like they the same way. They put the work in and I can't they just want to go out there and prove themselves. >> Hackett said uh previously and maybe somewhat jokingly like he'll give you 40 touches a game, he's going to have to carry you off the field sometimes. Uh what is kind of like a realistic limit that you you feel uh you can handle in a game? >> Um I don't know, to be honest. I feel like um it really depends how the games go. Like I said, um you know, when you be out there, man, it's it's it's adrenaline. And especially when you're close games and them type of games that you want to be in. Uh you don't really be tired out there for real. I mean, you come out there and me at 4 4 is me. I'll be out there like having fun cuz you know, game is always fun, but at the same time it's like I mean, I want to win. I mean, I want to do everything I can for this team. So, I try not to come out a lot. I try not to be available for um the team and I mean, how are you mentally I get I mean, that's just what it is. That's That's how it happen. >> Is that something you like to hear like you're going to be a starter? >> Yeah. >> What have you learned about Maling Qualls that's impressed you over the last few months? >> Um just just how fast he was to get the offense. Like you said, um he he a very smart quarterback and like you said, he don't make any, you know, bad decisions. I feel like, you know, he great with the ball in his hands and I feel like when he don't have no the the good look that he want, I feel like he good with using his feet.

title: Coach Jeff Hafley meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: Morning. >> How's it going? >> Good. Good. We we covered a lot with Selah. >> I know. So you So I don't You guys don't need me for much today after that. >> But there were things that we didn't get to yesterday on some new players. I wondered if the three defensive backs we claimed yesterday, any of one or two in particular among Dial, Reese, Taylor, Julius Wood that you've seen a lot tape of having an opinion on scouting report. >> Yeah, I mean sure. I've watched their tape and excited to get them out on the field today and work with them. Um you know, we watched them. We watched the tape. Um we thought they gave us a chance to help us on our team. And now I think as a coach, you're just excited to see him in person. So that will really be for the first time when we go out there today and this week and and we'll see what we have and what they can do and how they fit into the scheme and excited to get them ready. >> What struck you about Wood in particular? Safety's obviously a spot where you could use more depth. >> Yeah, physical uh live body. I thought he played really hard. Um he's a fun tape to watch. And just we saw some traits that that we felt would be fun to develop um and take a look at it in person. So we'll I think I'll have a much better picture of all these guys once we get out to the field and can see them live, but there were certain enough on tape to be and want to want to take a look at them. >> You have H.N. Brooks and Seiler today. What do you expect out of them as leaders this season? >> Um I think they've already been leaders this season. I think they've helped a lot of the young guys out. Um I think the way they've gone out every single day in practice, how hard they practice, just their attitudes in the meetings, they're they've been upbeat. And I just expect that to continue. I want them to be themselves. They've They've clearly gotten to where they are today because of the intangibles, because of the work ethic, and then obviously the production. Um I just want them to be consistent with that as we go, and that would be my expectation. I really enjoyed them, and I really have appreciated them. And I've really I like the relationships that we have. They're fun to be around, and and I'm excited that they're on our team. >> And what is the What is the process, I guess your process for deciding captains? I think in the past previous regimes have had players give speeches in front of the team. I think one was a vote. What is your process? >> Yeah, I think it's important for the for everybody who you know, is involved to have a vote in that. Certainly starting with the players. Um I think it's important that they have a vote in in who they believe the captains should be, and I'm excited to see that. So, we'll do that. We'll do that Thursday. We'll do that later in the week, and you know, whether I announce that Thursday afternoon or when we get back, it just all depends on how much time I have, but but we'll vote on it and and take a look, and I think there's a couple candidates that really deserve it. So, I'm excited to see who our players think they are. >> Can you tell us about Kenneth Grant's injury, and if you think he's got a good chance to return after four games? >> Um I'm hopeful. You know, I I was hoping that he wouldn't have to have to go on the injured reserve. So, I would say that I'm hopeful that he'll be back, um but we'll see. >> And regarding Chris Bell, want to look back and look ahead. How did he feel Saturday, the day after the game, with a big workload physically? And then, what are his chances of playing or starting in the season opener? >> Yeah, I think he would tell you he you know, he needs to continue to get in football shape. I think he took the one hit, and you know, you get There's a lot anxiety take your first hit and you start breathing a little bit heavier. You got to get in your routine get the rust off and and make sure you're in football shape. But I think he felt really good. Physically he told me he felt great. He did say it was nice to get hit that first time which you guys had asked me the night after the game. I'm sure you guys asked him that as well. It's always good to get the first one over with. He got a chance to catch a ball though. The DB made a really nice play on the one when he caught cuz even Chris said to me yesterday said he thought he hit it might have dropped it but the did a great job getting his hand in there. I thought it was a really good play when I still think he's got to hold on to the ball but I really respect the way the defender played it. And you know, if he continues to improve get in shape and my expectation is we see him on the field. >> With a couple new quarterbacks on the roster, what's the process now of getting them up to speed quickly? >> We got a bunch of guys that we got to get up to speed, right? And I think that's exciting, you know. We talked about depth in here and I appreciate Saleh and and all their staff and the work they put in try to help improve that depth and whether it's the quarterback or another position it's we'll have practices and then usually what you do is you have rookie meetings, right? Now it's rookie meetings and some of those new player meetings. We got to get them caught up to speed cuz they'll be limited reps. But I know the coaching staff's going to work really hard at that and they're excited to do so. It starts today on the field and we'll continue in the classroom and we'll use this week and then we'll use you know, I think we'll have four or five days next week and it will be a continued process as as we start the early part of the season. >> And what about the edge rusher room around Chop and Josh? It seems like there were a bunch of guys of similar ability. Can you share what went into ultimately choosing Herring and Beal over Luwellyn, Ojabo, Clelin obviously, Campgood uh in that group? You know, seven guys and you picked two. >> Yeah, I I want to speak on the guys that aren't here. Um I respect all the work that they put in and and their effort and appreciate everything that they've done. Herring is a guy that we saw on film. He's got good size. I'm not sure if you've seen him yet. I mean, he gives us a bigger end who we feel is a physical guy that can set edges, play a six technique, reduce down, um play a nine technique, and can be really strong against the run. title: The Saints Could Unlock Something Special With Alvin Kamara & Travis Etienne
text: Travis Ham meeting with the media back in training camp made a really interesting comment. >> Oh yeah. No, we did I I did a lot of this since I've been in league. Just been at the F position. I've been like the slot receiver. We did a lot last year in Jacksonville. And that advantage is just uh just just coach running me across the field. Now defense got to just put their eyes on me. You got Alvin Steen at the back field, things like that sort. Now, you got Alvin just running right by him. So, things like that. And vice versa, like Alvin, cuz like we're both guys you got to be aware of each each and every time of the game. And I feel like coaches are only going to manipulate defense with us and uh, great things going to happen. >> So, how could that work? Both those guys, they can do a lot of things. They can get on the field. They can line up different places. Just takes a little bit of creativity and you could really unlock some stuff. We're going to explore some of that idea on today's show. Welcome back to New Orleans Football presented by Loft 18. Best car dealer in the whole entire galaxy. Check him out at one of his many locations. And of course, we are coming to you from the Ashner Andrew Sports Medicine Institute podcast studio. And I don't think it's just those two. There are four backs on this team between HN, AK, Esté, and uh Kendrick Miller that I think all theoretically could get on the field together, but those top two because of the versatility Han just talked about, I think makes them incredibly incredibly interesting. So, I think it's on the coaching staff to find a way to be creative with them, get them into different places and both get them in spots where they could be highlighted and play off of one another to create inconsistencies in the defense and also to open up opportunities for them on offense. And one of the reasons I really like this idea is because the Saints use so much tempo and you can get guys out there, you get the defense trapped in a look, you're going really fast. Saints last year snapped the ball with more than 11 seconds left on the clock. The number two team in the league was in the 9-second range. So, they move a lot faster than other teams. And if you have Achan who can line up in different places, but especially AK who can line up in different places and do a lot of believable things, I think you can get the defense into a mismatch, trap them in it, and then just shape shift your way down the field. Maybe you're you're spread out on one look. Maybe you got two backs on the back field on another. maybe on one play one guys in the slot and you just can create all this different stuff and get advantages and that's really what the game is all about is kind of creating those advantages and you got a lot of guys here like I said that can do different things. Let's just look at the slot numbers right now. 72 to 63 to 41 to 45 to 37 in 2021. you got this downward arrow and then all of a sudden 2022 14 like what the hell happened? I remember when AK signed his first contract part of the argument about the value that I made was like well you're also getting a guy that can you know pseudo play slot if you want him to. So you're getting double value there. And then all of a sudden you're at 14 and then 2023 17. What the hell's going on here? And then 2024, Kubiaak comes, jumps back up to 51. Way more normal. The that just the the lining up there at least the usage still really not super high. Only 12 catches from from that spot. Um which I guess is in line with kind of I guess I would make it his third overall. But and then last year down to 21 and -2 yards receiving from the slot on two receptions is basically non-existent. And then you know being split out kind of the same thing. 56 routes in 17, 55, 50, 38, 44, 23, 17, 16, 15. Just straight down, straight down the tubes, man. Like that first year he had almost what do you have 250 yards from from split out positions. Second year, uh, 220 plus and then it was just kind of basically over, which is always been fascinating to me. like now I know he he ran the ball more and then you know 20 obviously um was running the ball really well but it it's just fascinating to me that this kind of special thing didn't get used a ton and I hope as they go forward I think this is a way that you know I don't think it ever goes back to where he was at in 17 but that is a place where you wanted to get two guys on the field you had Mark running the ball you wanted to get AK use because he he was special you needed to find other ways to get him going And you got a lot of yardage there. 18 the same thing. I don't know that you ever get back to this high of volume of usage. But I mean that there has to be something in between two targets and 20 targets from the slot positions.
