And uh so we're excited that he's, you know, getting back healthy and um he'll be important for us this season. >> And then you ended up keeping five other edge rushers and and only four other linebackers. Will that lead to even like more of a permanent switch for him into that room or will he still be kind of 50/50 at this? >> Uh I think that remains to be seen. Um but I think just the fact that he was trained this off season at inside linebacker, we now feel very good about him being able to do that if called upon. And then he's got such a background in our system as an edge player. Uh we know he can do that. So it was really about getting the other group of edge guys, you know, Anthony being new with us, Tyree being new for us, uh make sure that they got the right reps. And then young guys like Fidel and Mike Heldman, you know, we wanted to make sure that those guys, you know, got up and running so we could enhance the depth and quality of our team. So um Chris was awesome and um you know, like I said, it's it's going to help our team. >> Have you noticed the way that Cam Jordan has attacked uh this rehab with his hamstring? >> Been so impressed. Uh he came on the trip with us to Dallas and um that was probably one of the my favorite things that um I've I've kind of seen because he didn't need to come with us. Um he wanted to and it really helped I felt like our team play better uh in that last preseason game just his presence. Everyone knows um how hard he's trying to get back and how fast he's getting back. Um so, you know, he attacks everything like um like he always does, but I just think it it it his age to show the purpose, uh the urgency, how much it matters to him. Um you know, I was very impressed how he practiced um before before the hamstring. Um that was the the best I'd seen in practice, you know, um quite honestly since I've been with him. Um, which is saying a lot, but it just it was the best that he had he had looked. So, um, just, you know, we got to take it one day at a time so he comes back whole, but as you guys know, um, Cam's not going to put uh any limit on himself. >> What are like what kind of differences did you notice in practice that like you like >> Just, um, you know, I think he's in very good shape. He was in very good condition. He was running really, really well. Um, and then playing really fast. And so I think just another year in our system and then him just being at that right sweet spot for himself. Um, there was a he was making a lot of plays. And, um, you know, there wasn't any of that veteran pacing himself into training camp. He was going for it and, um, you know, we're excited uh for his return. >> Granted, for forgive me if I got the wrong read on this, but I I mean, I think nine returning starters this year, but two of the guys you're you're changing out are kind of different stylistically than the guys you had before in Cayden and and Yonas. Do do you have to kind of then tailor your defense more toward their skill sets? I mean, I imagine that's probably something that's true every year, but, um, >> Yeah. >> just like like considering a quarterback as the starter and then and then like linebacker, you just kind of then change it up a little bit more than usual. >> Yeah, Luke, um, I think a great observation and a great points. Um, you know, DeMario and Cayden are different players. So, they're they're not going to be playing the same position. so, but I think I think that, you know, Cayden's skill set is very unique in terms of the type of player that he is as a defensive player and then I think Yonas, um, and Alontae are are very different players, too. Uh, and just like with Alontae at star, we played a little bit differently to suit his strengths as a player. Um, you know, little things obviously, little nuances within the scheme, um, but really just trying to feature their game. And that's been I would say that probably the biggest um, change is learning Yonas and truly who he is and what he can do out there. And that's still going to be a work in progress because he's new, but I think we've been able to see him now against some, you know, top quality in the preseason against these three guys. And then when you're having to cover our guys every day, too, we I think we have a good sense of it. But once it starts here, we'll be able to continue to grow with But he's proven to be up for the task and that's going to be more ongoing than Cayden where we kind of know who Cayden is. We know what he can do. But how that fits with us will probably look different than our defense was last year. So we're going to have to, you know, grow together that way. But we're excited about >> What's the what's the focus of the bonus week? Are you are you looking to the lines or is it more internal? >> Yeah, you know, Nick, it's a it's a balance. I think it it mainly has to be about you because you have this like new You have this new team, so to speak, and you're gearing it now for the regular season. But you know, whether it's, you know, getting the scout teams up and running, you know, there's there's a process to that. So you're trying to get, you know, kind of into rhythm. And when you're trying to get into rhythm, you got to make it about you. So I think that that's where our focus is right now is focusing on, hey, we've got a month of training camp to look back on. Hey, these are the things that we like. These are the things that we need to improve on. So put our focus there. And then as we look ahead a little bit, it's really more just tying in some of those logistics for next week so that when we hit the ground running, we're truly going for it. And so anything we introduce this week will be just that, an introduction. But I think, you know, one of the top things about week zero is just getting these guys conditioning. You know, a lot of these players just making sure that, you know, they get their wind back. They get their legs back. And that, you know, they're ready to play an NFL game here, you know, in about whenever it is, 2 weeks. >> The the thing >> Was it a tough call to move on from Yiadom? Was it a tough call to move on from Isaac Yiadom? >> Yeah, we love Ike. Definitely. I'm sure Calvin talked about it. Um, those are the tough ones. >> Hey Brandon, you had a chance to coach uh Aaron Donald I guess one year. What did you just think about him coming back to the NFL? >> He's the best player I've ever seen. >> The The first thing you mentioned about Mike Reed was his length. Uh it obviously Martin and Tyree. Was that like a concerted effort this off season on the defensive side of the ball to bring in longer guys or was it just happen that some of these guys you brought in are longer? >> Yeah, I mean if you can get it, it helps. Um, it helps. So, no matter what the position, if you can get the the the length with the right other uh position characteristics with it, it's certainly an advantage. Um, and Ed Donatell used to tell me that uh those type of guys are harder to shoot over. Um, so, you know, if you can get that especially in the secondary, it can be it can be a help. Uh but I think one of the top things that Mike brings is the physicality at safety. He's going to go for it and and run and hit the right way. So, um there's still a lot for him to prove, but uh we feel like he's the right guy to be coaching. >> The new guys seem to be using the word freedom a lot when they talk about your defense. What do you think they're alluding to when they say that you give them a type of freedom that they didn't feel before in other defenses? >> Um, hopefully that means that um they have clarity of their assignment and they have clarity of the technique that we want to play. Um, and that they really trust in those things that are being taught to them because I think when players have clarity, that's when you feel the freedom to go for it. Um, and it's our quest as a coach, you know, as a teacher is to to get them to that space. That's what you want all for all of your players is for them to feel like they're flying out there. Um, and but you got to earn your way there. And so that's something that we talk a lot about is how much work goes into playing fast. Everybody wants to play fast um but not everybody can because they're being held back by something, you know, whether they don't have command of their assignments, they don't have command of their techniques, they don't have command over the opponent, you know, what they're looking at, you know, from the scouting report standpoint, what they're actually facing. So you know, we've got a a group of teachers on our coaching staff that I think is a winning edge that do a great job for our players and then we've got a great bunch of guys. I think when you have guys that are wired the right way, it's a lot easier to get them there. And so we've been fortunate with this group now for, you know, this going into our second season of of just true professionals, no matter what their age, whether they're a rookie or or, you know, Cam Jordan that that love the game the right way. And you know, you get it back if you love the game. So um hopefully our players continue to do that. >> What are some of the the qualities that separate a corner playing on the field side versus a corner that majors in the boundary side? >> Um there's a little bit more space and time to the field. There's space and time for Things happen faster into the boundary. A lot of the tough adjustments happen into the boundary in in the NFL cuz it's still a field league. So um you know, there's subtle differences that way and so I would think that that's, you know, from a corner standpoint, that's probably the the primary differences. Um And then again, depending on what type of secondary you have is where, you know, those guys are going to play. You can play them left, right. You can play field, boundary. Can match them up. Uh I think that depends on your group. >> With Brian's injury happening so early in camp, is it a ton of reps for Vernon. Are you happy with kind of development you saw from him this year? >> Yeah, I'm happy that Vernon's been available. Um, he had a really good training camp last year. Um, and he led us in reps on the D-line last year. So, we wanted to make sure that he activated himself in that same way now just against more premium competition. You know, he was able to earn his way in that first group and and get more looks with the with the ones. Um, but he still has a long way to go. He missed out on a whole regular season worth of of opportunities. you know, but as I mentioned to you guys, you know, we feel really strongly about the type of player he is. Um, he's had a good training camp and now he's just got to stay at it. >> Chatarius, who was who led the reps this year? >> Yeah, those those rookies for us were the ones that that held the rope for us again. You know, our our our rookies and then you know, I think what we were able to do this year, um, as you guys saw and I think JP's a good example is we just we were able to get even those second year players again a ton of work because again, when you're a young player in this league, you have the most room to improve cuz you haven't seen as much. So, that's been our kind of our goal is to make sure that those guys get as many looks at it as possible. Um, while obviously getting your your starters and your primary players enough of the live looks too. I think we we struck a good balance of that, but um, we try to be a developmental program and uh, those young guys that really, you know, you got to focus on them, you know, if you can. >> Yeah, with all the work that the starters got during the joint practices, how valuable did you find the ability to see the the rest of the roster in the preseason games and kind of just playing more snaps than they usually would? >> Yeah, I mean, I you know, Ross, I think in the presea you know, the way it works, you know, um, those guys that are in the second and third group just they play a ton. I mean, cuz they play a ton in the joint practices too. It wasn't just the starters. I mean, you saw I mean, Suggsy was with our first group and versed the Rams, you know, so I just think that it's awesome when guys get to play football. So I mean the more football the better. The more [snorts] they get to improve, the more they get to see you know, us getting three different looks for teams this year. I thought it was awesome. Three different styles, all premium quality. And so I think our our guys are able to measure themselves both individually and then unit and then collectively as a team. You're just able to see where you need to go and how you need to get there.

title: Saints ST coordinator Phil Galiano on Charlie Smyth, Daniel Carlson and special teams standouts
text: What did you kind of really just see from Daniel Carlson? Last week. >> Um Just really just need to kind of see where he was at. You know, it's different when you're training by yourself or you know, I know he was telling me a story he had some of his former college buddies that were working 9-5 jobs and he was getting them out of, you know, lunch break and stuff like that. So, I just wanted to get a chance to see, you know, where he was at and uh >> [snorts] >> where he was timing-wise and and that's where the deal and so we came here he did a really good job, had a good showing for us and made most of his opportunity. >> Phil, he he obviously wasn't an accomplished veteran who was available throughout the off-season. Was it like did you want to spend the off-season working with younger guys before like checking in on the veteran market at the last minute or like you know, I mean >> Yeah, it's a good question. There's a lot of things that go into that. Like I know there was whether it was younger market or veteran guys, you know, when free agency rolled around our personnel people had checked on and dealt with that and then there always becomes financial issues that come with that that fortunately I get to stay out of. I don't deal with that, you know, that part of it. Our personnel people handle that and finally they were able to kind of come to an agreement of what they want to do there. >> I saw that kicker finally stopped like [snorts] who are some of the other special teams guys that you thought like had a good camp and you're excited to work with them? >> Yeah, I think you know, obviously I'm really excited about a couple of guys who we drafted right to start with. I know, you know, excited for Barryan and then it's unfortunate, you know, Styles had a little bit of a nagging injury but I think you kind of saw what he was able to do there and then couple of the other [snorts] guys that showed up that wound up making our roster for us, you know, like a guy like Mike Reed comes in and makes some good plays on special teams. JP Price, you know, has the ability to not only play core special teams but is also an accomplished returner in college. We liked him coming out. And then there were some other guys, you know, that maybe we wound up keeping around the practice squad, you know, like I look at this point we're watching today a couple plays in the game because I just think they're really good teaching reps for some of the guys. And a guy like you know, Fidel Diggs even though he's back on our practice squad, but he really got better and and understood it. And so, he's a guy that, you know, has a bright future for us as well. >> Barion's kind of been your Is Barion the primary return guy? You've been rotating guys in through the preseason. >> We have, yes. Um and I think our plan going, you know, with that is is Barion, yes. But, um I think, you know, we have a couple other guys that we have to make sure are ready to go and um but yeah, [snorts] that's that's the plan going forward. >> What's your reason he didn't get a ton of return reps in the preseason? >> Um so, just cuz of his role in offense or >> It was It was a combination of um how much he was going to play on offense, um what he's accomplished in his career as a kick returner. There wasn't, you know, very much that we needed to see from that standpoint of it. And we really just wanted to be able to get him the the punt return reps that he needed. And there were some other guys that we wanted to evaluate. And you know, those come into play cuz when you go on the game day, you kind of have to have an idea of who's going to be active that if something were to happen to to your returner, you have somebody else who can go back there and do it. >> So, there's I mean, it's fair to say that you have a pretty high degree of confidence in him if you don't really need to see him much in the preseason there. >> Uh very much so. Yeah, I'm very confident in him. We've got a chance to If you If you've If you've seen even like in today's practice, when we get 10 punts off in a practice, you know, I mean, he's catching the majority of those. I know he could do it with the ball in his hand. >> When you bring in um like different kickers, how how important is to have someone like Zach Wood that that's so steady with what he's done? >> Yeah, I think it's extremely important. Um between Zach and I'll be honest, the guy who was hardest on was was Ryan Wright. You know, you have three different kickers that like the ball held it slightly different way, you know, and you're doing a pregame warm-up, which was the first in my career of having three kickers in a pregame warm-up. And Ryan's got to try to you know, and he doesn't want to let those guys down. He wants to be able to put it perfect for them, you know, so um but having three veteran guys that were able to handle that and they didn't let it distract them from from what they needed to accomplish. That was the other thing that, you know, I kept telling Ryan about like, I appreciate, you know, him being so diligent in how he wants to get his hold, but he's got to get himself ready to go play in games as far as, you know, his punting and his routine and that sort of deal, too. >> Is it the first time in a while that like Zach has noted that you don't have to worry about that because you have Ryan? >> For sure. Yes. >> It's the first time in a while that you haven't been kind of working in a rookie punter. How much of a luxury is that to have an established guy in the role? >> Yeah, I think it I think it's a really it's a big deal for us. Um I think one of the things that we were so attracted with Ryan is you watched him from a rookie and how he continued to get better each year. And um so it's something that that, you know, we feel good about and um I think he brings like a quiet confidence to him that I think the other guys pick up on and I think he's been a huge asset uh from a leadership role as well and dealing with our returners, dealing with our punt returners, and helping coach Damron film when you're seeing, you know, the opponent's punter, how he lines up, and you know, different types of kick he can have or how he's going to line them up on game day and stuff like that. You know, there's just all that acquired expertise over the years is a big deal not only for him but for for the rest of the team. >> Forgive me. I've I've never studied this, so forgive me, but your counterpart Zach, like how long do the good long snappers play? Like What what's his starting career like? Can those guys play forever? Like >> Yeah, I mean, I think if you look at the average age of a long snapper, it's probably the oldest on an NFL NFL roster. And um the one thing about Zach is you can look at him and they're like he keeps himself in unbelievable shape. He takes great pride in that and keeping his body healthy, and I think that as long as he continues to do that, I think he can still play for a while. Um it's interesting when you watch him and there's on average maybe there's one new long snapper to the NFL each year, and um part of that is is because of the college game rules. It's so hard for long snappers who didn't have to protect in college to now get to the NFL and have to figure out not only have to be able to snap the ball accurately, but I also have to be able to block this guy that's lined up across from me, Carl Granderson for example, one-on-one and not let him block the punt. Um it it just takes time for those guys. I think one of the neat things about the you know, this other league, the UFL league, I think that is it's a huge asset for specialists especially. You get guys like a long snapper or kicker or punter that can get um more game film of what it's really like in the NFL as opposed to you know, in college they snap the ball, their rules are different. So, in the NFL you can't be down field right when the ball's punted. Only the two widest guys, the gunners can. Um in college everybody can release right now. So, there's so many long snappers in college that snap the ball and they just go run right down the field. They're not asked to protect. Um and and as you know, that's a challenging deal to do. >> What do you see in the mechanics and the mechanics at all from you got Tanner and Charlie fairly similar. But Charlie uh Daniel's mechanics is he's 6'5, steps back. He's always looks like a full yard deeper than maybe Charlie or Tanner is. Is there any adjustment there? >> Um no, there's not I wouldn't say there's an adjustment. It there's each guy is different and and you know, as you see Daniel, he's bigger but the way the operation works, you know, like Zach's going to snap the ball when he's supposed to, Ryan's going to put it down at the spot where he's supposed to and you know, I'm going to stand back there in time and I'm going to make sure that we have the same get-off time whether he's 2 yards, 3 yards, 4 yards away. Um and so Daniel's been doing this long enough that he knows operationally like what our get-off time needs to be for him to be successful. So, there is differences in each individual one but the end result winds up the whole process I should say winds up becoming the same. >> As you I guess it's preseason so it's hard to tell anyway with the gunners and jammers and personal protectors. A lot of those guys that are out there in the preseason a lot of those guys aren't with the team currently. Uh could there be new gunners, jammers, personal protectors, returners? >> For sure. I mean that's welcome to the life of the special teams coach. You get to play who who's out there. Um It It's That's part of the deal. It's part of what, you know, what I signed up for. I understand that and um you know, there's conversations throughout, you know, the building of what our plans are and we try to all, you know, do the best that we can and be on the same page and try to accumulate, you know, the best 53 guys on your roster that can help you win. Um and so, there'll be some there'll be, you know, some new guys in a bunch of different positions whenever the roster changes over. I look back to last year when we played uh Arizona in the first game of the year. We had one returning starter on the punt team. That was That was Zach Wood. We We sent 10 new players out from the year before. So, there's a lot of turnover and a lot of change in in the special teams world and that's not just us. That's, you know, throughout the NFL and that's part of the deal. We have to be able to figure out who can do what and get them caught up to speed and get them to do it as well as they can and not hurt. >> What do you think led to some of Charlie's inconsistencies this season? >> We're still trying to figure that out. you know, Charlie and I have had a bunch of discussions and as disappointed as he was, I told him I'm I'm disappointed in myself that I haven't been able to help him, you know, get it fixed yet. Um but a lot of it comes down to majority of, I should say, it comes down to when he's kicking the ball from the left hash is where most of his issues come. We're trying to figure out, you know, what is it a I think the thing we may came up with is it is it a depth perception from that hash of where he sees the ball because whenever he misses, he just gets his his plant foot, his left foot, it gets too far in front of the ball and he can't get his hip through and that's why the ball always goes right. And so, we've messed around with different alignments and walk off steps and stuff and I think that we have all that correct. It's just on that left hash and so, we just got to get him to figure out not to step with that plant foot too far. >> Is Can any of that be attributed to just time on task and only having a few years as a kicker or or you're all past? >> No, I don't I don't think No, I think that's I think that's a real thing. It's something I you know, I talked with our personnel people and you know, with Kellen and then with Charlie about there's he didn't have the luxury of playing high school football or playing college football and he he got a chance here and then he got a chance, you know, to get started there and he's become so much better when he first got here and then you know, we had a little bit of it last season when he got a chance to get real live game reps and I just think the more he can do it and the more he's able to figure it out on his own and come up with, you know, what the issue is and how do I fix it so the same mistake doesn't happen twice and it's like anything for any of us. The more you do anything the better you become at it and I think that's a real thing. >> Also, this might sound silly, but when you say depth perception thing is any of that have to do with vision or is that >> I don't think so. Um I think now I'm getting really technical and so with it. But I do I I think it's just I think it's a visual thing when the ball's on the left hash, when it's on that tick mark for him of where I think in his mind he may think that the ball is more forward than it really is and that's sometimes why he steps too far forward left because it doesn't happen in the middle on the right hash. So, we try to get that ironed out. >> Does his kick shape have anything to do with it? I feel like it's he has a very unique kind of kick as opposed to like you watch Daniel and it's very straight whereas Charlie's got a kind of draw. Is that a factor at all? no, I don't think it is because um like I said, when he when he misses, he tends to go that way with it which when he hits a good ball, it isn't that. So, I just I just think it's really where his plant foot is and where he makes contact with the ball at. >> Oh, Mike Reed, just what did you do on special teams that got your hand so far up? >> Yeah, I think you know, when you take a look, you go out there, we throw him he gets here, we throw him out there at at Canter and he's able to go, you know, beat two guys and go make a play. And then when you see him go at Jammer and there's a couple reps throughout the preseason where you know, those guys, him and his partner, they didn't let the guy get more than five or 10 yards down the field. And so he just came here and he just went to work. He put his head down, "Coach, what do you need me to do?" He's another guy that not only did he go to Gunner, but he also learned and played PP for us as Played on kickoff. You watch, it's the little things that it's really sometimes it's hard to see unless you're looking for it. But when you go back and you watch um to our second preseason game. If you just watch him block on KOR, it's one of the better KOR blocking performances that you could actually hope to see in a one-on-one situation. He did it multiple times. It It was really impressive.

title: Saints OC Doug Nussmeier on Tyler Shough's development, growth of the offense from Year 1 to Year 2
text: So, we we asked the players a lot about second year in the system with Kellen Moore. Obviously, you've been around Kellen a lot more, but how does that feel now settling into your second season here in the morning? >> Obviously, we're light years ahead ahead of where we were a year ago at this time, but we still got a long, long ways to go. >> And what Grayson noticed is Tyler maybe doing things naturally now that he was maybe struggling last year, but things come more naturally to him where he is. >> You know, if you go back to this point in time last year when, you know, we're going through the process of trying to decide who was going to be the starter, um the biggest thing with Tyler was you could see he was seeing things, but he just wasn't able to get that fast enough. You know, his eyes were seeing what they needed to be seen, but he was just a little bit late and uh you know, as he's talked about, as we've talked about, uh we were able to get him on the scout team there and let him actually speed up his play and uh I think that helped him tremendously. So, what you're seeing is a guy now that did knows the timing of it and now he's starting just to, you know, evolve to the next step of things, which is you know, it's always the little things the quarterbacks see. I mean, you watch the guy best players at that position in this league played 15, 18 years. Those guys are always working on something cuz the game's always changing and their bodies are changing and always finding a different way to make this type of throw or a different footwork on that type of throw, something it doesn't feel right or natural to them. To them, so obviously Tyler's got a lot bigger curve than some of those guys at that point, but you know, there's a lot of things that we've progressed through and now we're on to the next step of things. >> Was there a point Was there a point last year obviously before he started that you saw that change for Tyler when he was running scout team? >> Yes, you could see that um you know, it's a little different cuz you always worry as a coach when they hold the card up and you know exactly what this and that is and it's all okay to throw it to that guy or do that. Um it's a lot different than when you got to call the play, you know, and get up to the line of scrimmage and be able to process everything that's going on with protection and and coverage, and then okay, now where is that is that route going to sit or is that route going to stay on the move? All those type of things. So, you always worry about that transition from scout team to playing games. But, we'd already seen that. We knew, like I said, his eyes were in the right place. He was seeing things. Just wasn't happening fast enough, but I think probably week four or five, you really started to see like, "Okay, he's starting to get it." >> Along, I guess, somewhat similar lines. I had talked to Tyler about when you're in these college situations versus the uh you know, more scripted periods where maybe if no matter what happens, it's going to be first down or it's going to be third down the next play. You try to fit it in or you hold it a little longer to see if something like do you encourage him to maybe hold on to it when the next play is scripted versus just letting it go or do you want to just let it go no matter what? >> You know, I'm not You know, I'm not a big into you know, a lot of guys are coach off the script coaches. Uh believe in that because to me, you don't know what the player knows. You know, as coaches, sometimes we fool ourselves because we may know it, and we can recite it, and we can have a player look at a script and tell you. And your player isn't stupid. Now, they figure out kind of when their reps are coming. Okay, so when you script it, and they go out there, and they know what's coming, it's like, "Well, does he really know that or did he read the script?" You know, so uh you know, to me, college periods are phenomenal because you get to see guys play. Um and you know, obviously, the number one job of the quarterback is to move the team. >> There's a couple of guys that have talked about the mental processing particularly for Tyler being beyond what they expect from a second-year quarterback. Do you agree with that, and what stands out to you about the way that he goes about it? >> Uh obviously, he's an extremely bright guy. Number two, um you know, I think that what we've seen is this era of college football, we're getting older quarterbacks that have seen more at the college level and have more experience. And I think that's a plus for them when they get to this league. >> Did um the way that Varian Brown and Bryce Young have progressed in camp, has that stood out like from the traditional like was that different than how rookie receivers normally go like >> Um >> what you expect in terms of >> I don't know that you ever expect that from rookies. You know what I mean? It's It's kind of like um I don't know anybody who's drafted a player and said, "Well, I don't think that player is very good." You know, so you obviously when you draft them you think they're going to contribute and be good players on your team, but but some of them it takes longer. Um and there's a lot of players that maybe at first you're like, "Whoa, I don't know. Maybe we missed on this one, right?" And then it takes an off season or two and then all of a sudden you're like, "Wow, we were right. We got a really good player." Um so I will say this about those two guys. Those two guys have done outstanding job of coming in and learning the system. Um they've been productive players when they've been in the game. Obviously, it's a new game when you get to the regular season versus the preseason, so they'll need to elevate their game again, but uh we're going to count on those guys to help us win. >> David Edwards, his presence on the offensive line it just seems kind of just like a big deal. Like how much has that impacted that group? >> Uh substantially. I think the addition of David has been a substantial upgrade to our offense. Um like I said, we we still got a long, long ways to go, but when you bring guys in like that that love football, that have um really good football knowledge, a lot of experience, um and willing to share with the others. And and for young players, and we have a lot of young players that come into the building and see how a guy that's had the success that David's had, how he prepares, how he how he works day-to-day, uh his routines, I think it's invaluable. >> I know like you guys focus probably a lot on like that stuff and all those and everything that happens in practice, but can you tell just being around Travis how much playing for the Saints means to him? Just like being back in New Orleans. >> I wouldn't want to speak for him on that, but you know, just my discussion. Obviously, you know, I remember when he came out of Jennings High School, you know, and um so I you know, I don't I don't want to speak for him, but I do believe it's probably pretty special for him. I know to put on the black and gold and play in this dome and um he's a special player. He's been a great addition for us also. >> And what do you got just what do you think what kind of difference can he make on what you guys want to do in the running game? >> Well, obviously, you know, it starts with the running game. We got to we got to run football. We thought last year about this time that you know, we wanted to see if we could run football. They said obviously, that didn't end up being the case and uh so we've got to go out and prove that we can. Uh we haven't proved that yet. So uh like I said, we still got a long long ways to go um in every area of offense, but obviously, he's a big piece of what we're doing. >> How does yeah, how does he help? I I know it's I know it's obvious, but how? >> But you just said it's obvious. How do you uh you know, obviously, the guy uh is really um interesting to me is I think people have a perception of Travis when he came out of this he's a receiver slash running back. I see an elite running back. An elite running back. Great instincts. He has great vision, great contact balance. You don't know you know, I just watched his tape in Jacksonville. Um >> [clears throat] >> there's a lot of things this guy does at an elite elite levels. Just a true tailback. So I think that maybe it's a little bit of a misnomer about him. He does have good hands. So um like I said, obviously, uh he's been a big addition for us and we're really excited to see him go out and get to play. >> When free agency is unfolding and there were other teams like mentioned with him in the mix, were you kind of just checking in to see like do I get him? Can we get him? Like what was kind of what do you remember from that? >> Yeah, yeah. Well, I mean, obviously, um we have a plan and our front office does a great job. Um, and obviously, you just watch the plan and hope it executes the way that, you know, you kind of going into the plan. Um, but you never know with these things, right? Obviously, um, finances play a big part of things, and sometimes your cap restricts what you can do and those type of things, but give our management team a lot of credit for everything they've done. You know, we talk about David, we talk about Jarvis, you know, we know we talk about all the guys we've added on offense to help us be a better team. >> Good Doug, I hate to assume, but I'm I'm assuming Jordan Tyson's a big part of your plan, and now you you know you don't have for at least the first 4 weeks. Um, have you guys had to kind of shift things a little bit to to kind of make it work when when he's not available? >> Sure. I mean, um, like I said, you know, when you draft players, you kind of like have a vision for them, or you wouldn't draft them, and you say, "Okay, well, here's what we think the guy's going to do. Here's how he's going to impact our offense." >> Um, and a lot of that is really unknown right now with Travis. We just haven't had a lot of time with him. I do believe he's a special talent. Um, and we do have big plans for him, and we'll just have to wait until we get him ready, and then, uh, he'll come out, and we'll we'll kind of watch it evolve. >> What stood out to you about him before before the injury? >> Um, I just turn on his college tape, and guy's explosive, he's dynamic, he's twitchy. Um, you know, each each game he played in Arizona State. >> And did you see some of that already starting to translate in y'all's system in in, you know, with what was >> Yeah, I I mean, yes. It but it's just hard. It's a small sample size, you know what I mean? So, um, like I said, we're going to get him healthy, we'll get him out there, and then, uh, you know, but I I do believe that he's going to be a really good player for us. >> Did uh, I'll be more of a tone question, but did uh, Kendre Miller return? He left with a trainer when we saw >> I mean, like can't really address those type of things. Good try. [laughter] Let's see, A for effort. >> Um, but Jeremiah Wright, one thing that he said a few times is the words controlled aggression. You know, how do you go about coaching a player like that where you don't want to like train that aggression out of him, but you need to kind of keep it within the confines of, you know, not getting penalties and all >> Yeah, he uh You love the competitive spirit that he plays with. And just like you said, you don't ever want to take that away. Uh and you walk a fine line um between playing on the edge and not playing very smart football. And he's crossed the line a few times. Okay, and he'll learn that. And uh the biggest thing for him is um he exhausts himself with some of the extracurricular things and it takes away from his ability to be uh a [clears throat] really good player. But really excited about the player physical physical part. You guys have seen it. Um very talented young man. We just got to channel it in the right direction. >> What kind of leap did What kind of leap stood out to you uh around Chris Olave from last year to this year? the biggest thing with Chris was just having him out there and and and having him playing. You watch um the dimension. You know, it's funny because everybody says, when you look at offense you know, people look at receivers and say, well okay, how much of did he change the game? Sometimes a receiver doesn't have to catch the ball and he changes the game. Because what people don't see is they're taking two for one. So, when you get the checkers out and you start playing, okay, this and where did that guy go? Well, wait, you know what? Their guy's short over here. And teams don't realize, well, how come they rushed for 150 yards? Well, because the safety up there supposed to be down there was over there doubling trying to make sure the ball didn't go to Olave. And so, there's a lot of things when you talk about receivers. Everybody wants to look at stat lines. Um and they don't always tell the whole story. So, having Chris on the field, having his availability, um not only is he a special player and is he going to make big plays for us, but he forces people to look at how they want to defend you. And uh you know, like I say, when you put a guy in one spot that they take two for one, well, now we've created equal numbers everywhere else, which is a good thing for us. >> Having four wide receivers down on the roster can play, does that change how who you're going to be putting out on the outside? Possibly. You know, like maybe you have more running backs on the outside or more tight ends or etc. >> Um you know, I think you're always looking at you know, and that's I don't know exactly where we'll be heading into a week from Sunday, but um you know, cuz you got to factor in when it gets to the roster phase, special teams plays a factor in this. Um there's a lot of different things, you know, assuming guys are coming back off injury. We're hoping to get back guys that may not be healthy. So, obviously, four you're very thin. So, you better have contingency plans. Um so, that being said, obviously, you would look at other positions and how do we address this or do we have different packages? Um but we just have to wait and see where our numbers are at. >> What do you all like about Peyton Teo? >> Big physical guy, you know, obviously. I don't know a ton about him. We just got him here. So, the biggest thing will be getting him out there with us and letting him do our things, but excited that he's part of our team. >> You did have some overlap with Stone Smart though, right? Yeah. What what stands out to you, Buck? >> Uh Stone's a great kid. Um you know, college quarterback. We got him at the Chargers. He was very green. Very, very green, especially playing the position of tight end. Um but the guy can run, man. He can run. He's a smart guy. Catches the ball well. and and can do a lot of things because um he's really smart, you know, and thinks well. So, excited to see haven't been with him obviously since the one year in LA. So, excited to see really where his growth has come in the last few years um when we get him out with us. >> Was he always a tight end with you all or was there ever any conversation with him about wide receiver? I feel like there might have been some really conversation about that. >> Man, you're taking me back. I'm getting too >> [laughter] >> It's all right. >> No. >> we had him at tight end the whole time. You know, he was doing the F thing for us um a little bit kind of me. You know, if you want to paint a picture of a guy, uh paint him in the Juwan Johnson family of tight ends so to say. Does that make sense? >> Baltimore Ravens this this year? >> What's that? >> Baltimore Ravens this year? >> Who's that? >> No, I'm excited excited to get to see my son play. Thanks for asking. >> Thanks.

title: Saints WR Barion Brown on adjusting to the NFL, flashing in preseason, staying positive and more
text: you learned the most about yourself just going through preseason making all these plays cons being consistent like what what coming into it to where you are now like how much more confident do you feel? >> Um I'm feeling real confident that's um I just got the right support system around me. Coach Doug, Coach Mo, Coach Nus, uh Coach Phil and all these guys in the um locker room. So um just being able to rebule and um you know generally just have a great connection with them makes it a lot easier. Is there anything that that was surprising to you about like how easy I don't want I don't know if easy is the right word but like it seemed like you just hit the ground running and there really wasn't like much of a learning curve and it was just kind of go go like right from the start. >> Yeah. Um it may look like that but um best believe me and coach Doug we in the film room and um even the plays that y'all see where I'm doing something good me and him is still um he's still coaching me up still finding ways to get better. Um just um being able to have fun while doing it. I think that plays a big role in it. And um that's one thing about me being very energetic. So being able to have fun and you know do something that I love is a blessing. >> What do you like about having the ball in your hands? Like the the run last week you kind of hit the ground and able to plant real easily like and get in. Like what do you like about that? >> Um I just feel like I got the whole New Orleans in my hand and um you know won't let them down. So, um, you know, just doing what I can to, you know, be the best version of myself and be the best version, um, of a great teammate for these guys in here. And, um, uh, yeah, just having fun. >> Feeling like you got the city in your hands. Where's that come from? >> Um, I mean, that's kind of how it is when you got the ball in your hand. It's, um, you carrying a lot of weight um, with that rock in your hand. So, just being able to um, you know, show the city and the state that um, you know, I'm here and and here to do good things. And what are you looking forward to, you know, just showing week one? It's coming up. Like it's about to be about to be real. Like what's what's kind of the expectation for yourself? >> Yeah. Um just being the best version of myself and um whatever happens happens and you know take it with a smile on my face. So um you know can't wait um a dream dream come true for sure when that day comes. So um you know but as of right now you know just keep staying in the playbook, staying on the grind and um you know just trying to get out there each and every day. >> You were smiling on draft day. You're smiling now. Like, have you stopped smiling like since you got here? >> Um, no man, a smile can go a long way. Um, a smile may brighten somebody else's day up. So, I try to keep one on my face and um, you know, just take take whatever life gives me and, you know, just take it with a smile on my face, whether that's good or bad. Just trying to, you know, stay the wave. >> What does it take to be a good returner? There's a lot of guys with speed in the NFL. What is it, what is the quality that makes a return man special? >> Um, just being fearless and having a heart on back there. Um, no telling how it may go, but um, you know, just be heartless and, you know, run through the smoke. >> What was your mentality for the offseason and training camp and preseason? What was your mentality to, you know, really not just earn a rope, but obviously impress all the out of the coaches as well? >> Um, just grind grind each and every day and um, you know, just show these guys um, what they brought me here to do and um, just again being a great teammate. Um, you know, getting coaching points from CO V and all the older guys and, you know, just being able to gel with them guys. >> Cool. >> You mentioned when you got here the new like kickoff rules and jumping into those. You said you were excited that people weren't going to be running at you. >> Yeah, for sure. >> Like just what's the uh the experience so far with that? >> Oh man, Coach Phil has put in a great program for me and um he's he's on me um on me hard and um he just know where I can get to and he know where I want to go. So, um each and every day, man, we just attacking the day.

title: Morgan Moses, Kyle Williams, Quintayvious Hutchins & More Address the Media | Press Conference
text: understanding that Rome wasn't built in one day. So, um, we got to, you know, we got to go out there and work. We got to earn it. You know, um, you know, it's game one and obviously, you know, you can't really look preseason games because nobody really puts, you know, that much out there. But, uh, looking forward to whatever curve ball they throw and knowing that we have to operate as a unit and not as individuals. >> What would you say the offense like as a unit has taken the biggest step forward to start the off season? >> Well, I just think the camaraderie, you know, um, adding some guys, you know, ABT, you know, obviously seeing what Will has done over the the offseason, coming back and being where he's at and um, and then um, just, you know, going out there and um, you know, playing as a unit, you know, five equals one. and um you know we got a lot of great guys with a lot of you know opportunities and a lot of you know veteran leadership and so we look forward to going out there and playing against a great defense. >> How much does it ramp up when you get to this week? You got 53 on the on the field. >> Um it you know it definitely ramps up. You know obviously coming off a off of training camp but um understanding now like hey now we're we're preparing for a team. You know we had a little little spurts there with you know the Colts and uh and the Eagles but now you get to really dial in and really study your opponent and um get familiar with them. So, >> what's it been like watching the film back from Super? >> Um, it's been, um, obviously, you know, you look at some of the things that you you did great. You look at some of the things that, uh, that you can, you know, polish up on. Um, but at the end of the day, when you look at the film, it's the effort stands out. You know, no matter what the circumstances were, we played until, you know, every whistle that was blown. And, um, you can walk, you can walk off the field with your head held high off of that. Um, but, you know, we got some things that we got to correct and, um, obviously, like I said, it's the unknown. you know, we're coming off a training camp and preseason where not a lot of things are shown and so we'll know they they'll have some curve balls for us as well and um we'll look forward to just you know going out there as a unit and attacking >> last year with Rainbow coming in such a new establishing culture is so important. How well do you think the new players have gotten? Um, I think it's, you know, a lot of our core values on this team is is part of our DNA. And I think, uh, when you, you truly believe that, and you replicate that every day, and you got older guys and some of the younger guys that were rookies last year that, uh, that that live by that every day, and it makes it a lot easier for the the the newer guys to come in and um, and obviously see the roles that we're guys are at and um, and establish that DNA themselves. And um, so we look forward to just, you know, keep on jelling. you know, it's uh we're getting into week one and so keep on jelling and like I said, you know, Rome wasn't built in one day, so we're just going to keep on chipping at the block. >> Three touchdowns in three games, a lot of deep balls that that you were able to get to. How do you feel like your preseason performance leads you into this season? >> I feel like it was pretty good, but you know, I mean, it's a preseason, so all that's behind me and now we're on week one, so that's all I'm worried about. >> How excited are you to to get another shot at the Seahawks? >> I'm excited, man. You know, the bo blood's been boiling. So excited to get out there and just play football. You also get the chance to usually you get to sit back >> till Sunday, you watch the early games. Now you are the early games. What's it like to kick off the season for the whole league? >> Uh I mean I ain't really looked at it like that for real, honestly. I mean it's just it's just week one. You know, everybody plays at different times, different days. you know, I guess we the ones that set it off, so we just got to set the tone, right? For our >> I know we've touched on it with you, but now that the wide receiver room is set, um, what do you feel you specifically bring to that room and and you know, how your skill set can help this team? >> Um, I mean, I feel like I bring a lot just as much as the other guys do. So, I mean, I really want to single myself out, but as a whole room, I feel like we nasty, you know? I feel like we got a nasty group. >> Why are you nasty? >> I mean, because we could do it all on all cylinders. You know, everybody could do everything. You know, it's not one person that does this better than anybody. What I can do, AJ, Rome, Pop, they can all do and what they can do, I can work with. So, it's, you know, it's just good competition and it's I think we really ready to go compete. >> How excited is the whole to see what it's actually going to look like? >> Um, I mean, we haven't played a full game together. You know, it's been really practicing and joint practice. So, I think we're really excited to go see what the whole puzzle piece looks like when it's put together. So, it's going to be fun. >> How much confidence does that give you just preseason you didn't have? with the key that carries it over. >> I mean, it's a lot of confidence. I mean, it's something that I knew I could always do, you know? It's just putting it on display and it's just like that confidence just going to keep carrying over week by week by week and just steady growing. >> Is there a chip on your shoulder? People call you old tricks on you. >> Uh, I mean, I've been hearing that my whole life, man. So, I would say is a chip on my shoulder. I know what I can do. I know I'm more than just a vertical guy, but you know, whatever my role is, that's my role and I'm accepted. Kyle, what would you say you feel like you grew the most over the course of the offseason and training camp? >> Uh, I'd probably say from a a mindset standpoint, you know, the physical traits is the physical traits, but the mindset is what separates you. So, and then obviously I went back in the locker room and, you know, played the game. So, I mean, you know, I can't complain at all about, you know, how my life's going. So, it was it was a fun moment to be to be in for sure. >> Was the waiting tough? >> Yeah, it was tough. I'm happy to be here. Um it was one of the best moments of my life, you know, all the hard work that, you know, I put in. For sure. Um, I mean, yeah, like I said, I can't complain. I mean, all the coaches here have been super great to me, um, pushing me to be the best player I can, also be a better man off the field and stuff like that. So, you know, it was a it was a pretty cool moment for me. >> As cool as it was, how much now the journey has just begun for you? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, obviously, this is just the start uh stepping stone into, you know, my ultimate goal, which is playing on Sundays. And, you know, that's a process for sure. Um, so right now my focus is just helping the team can helping the team do whatever they can to get ready for the week one for sure, which is that scout team, playing special teams for them and, you know, doing all I can to stay in this building for sure. >> Congrats. >> Thank you. I appreciate it. Thank you. Appreciate you. >> Seen a 53man roster and was like, "Oh, damn. I really made it. Um, all the hard work paid off, but it's still more work to do." >> Do you feel you had a chip on your shoulder from maybe the round you were drafted in and having to work through camp? I got more to do. >> You found out from a tweet? >> Uh well, the Instagram, excuse me, the Instagram post when they post the 53 man roster. That's how I really found out. >> That's amazing. What What are the emotions that run through when you see you know your name and just knowing what you just went through for training camp? >> Uh I say uh it was joy. Uh I had a lot of faith in myself and God. So I I I say a lot of joy from me seeing it to like excitement. >> What what is that next chapter like? Just when you walk in here and obviously like so many blessed guys, you know, still standing. >> Uh it's just the job's not done. You got to come in, work, keep your head up, and keep going. >> How personally do you take the path forward here, especially where we know Greyel likes to be pretty hands-on with your position group and you know where he played in that area, too. >> Um as long as I'm meant to be here. Um I don't really put a time on it. Um, like I said, I'm local, so it it feels good to stay in the New England area. Uh, I have to be around great players. Um, yeah. >> Have a lot of people from BC reached out to you. Glad that you made the >> Oh, yeah. I heard from all my OD linemen. Uh, Coach O'Brien text me recently. Um, coach Josh Beakman. So, a lot of people very excited for me to be with the Patriots and be in the area. >> What's the uh what was the message and what's the mindset just going into the regular season mode now countdown in Seattle? >> Uh, like I said, uh the job is not done. continue to prove my point my myself uh to earn a role in the team um and just be dominant every chance I get. >> Lewis out. >> Yes. >> What was it feeling like when you got claimed and what's it like to be here with the New England Patriots? >> It was actually a crazy feeling. Um I was actually in the middle of signing my practice squad papers for for the New York Giants and then I got the the co uh the call from coaching Braves and all of them and they hit me up saying we're going to play you here and and I was excited. I was excited, you know, from there on. I was on a flight last night. Got here early this morning, man. And I'm putting on the the Patriot helmet all now. I'm ready to go, man. I'm excited to be here. I never been here. This is my first time in Boston, Massachusetts. So, I'm I'm an island boy. I'm from Hawaii. So, I'm far far away from home, but and I'm I'm loving every second of this. >> What was the message from Mike as far as what he wanted from you? >> Uh, just come on here and just just play ball, man. because I I I knew some of the defensive coaches that were here are DC, Coach Zack and and Coach Shane and and all of them. So, I'm very familiar with them and and I'm just ready blessed with this opportunity to come on here and just play the sport that I love. >> What do you think you can add to the linebacker room? >> Just depth to the linebacker room. Uh just, you know, add some someone that's experienced in in this defense. Uh, I played in this system for two years now, so I feel like I can bring some knowledge to to the room and, you know, just go out there and play special teams and, you know, give it everything I got. >> And Frabel said he really liked that you and Cameron both had NFL experience in terms of guys they were looking for on the waiverss. How much do you feel you've grown in your time in the NFL to the point now, like you said, where you can contribute? >> Yeah, I feel like it's a continual growth having that that mindset every year of, you know, stacking each year on top of each other. And I feel like, you know, I'm ready to stack this my year three of my career on top of my my first and my second. >> Also, it's all about winning, I'm sure, for you to be here on team that's the defending AFC champs with Drake May leading the way. How good do you feel about that? >> Man, I'm I'm excited to be here winning culture. You know, that's what you want to be as a competitor. you want to be on a winning team and and man, it it's just so awesome being here and being surrounded by, you know, this mentality and this it's just a different vibe here that, you know, guys want to win and guys want to be the best versions of themselves and I'm excited for this opportunity and hopefully I can take it upon myself to, you know, contribute as as much as I can for the student. >> What have you heard about Mike Craraven and have you seen when he takes the pads and puts the pads on with some of the linebackers and gives them tutorials? >> Oh, yeah. Oh man, Cook Bridge is a big body now. So, I'm I'm excited for that. But, um, yeah, he told me uh on the phone when he called me that he used to uh he played L5 and R5 was his uh one of my my uncles, Uncle Chris Malo, and he's one of the Polynesians um running back back in the day. But, man, just them running down the field and just blowing stuff up, man, is is what I'm excited for. And it really bring juice into my my body because man, you know, I feel like that's what I'm going to bring to the table is just, you know, going down there running down on special teams or defense, whatever it may be, and just, you know, bringing that bringing the the energy to the team. >> What was the conversation like back to Hawaii, telling them that you were going to the New England Patriots, >> I'm going further away from home. That's what that's what they all say. So, I'm, you know, usually it'd be nice to make my way back home, but man, I'm going further away from home and, you know, I have no problems about that, man, because I'm I'm here, man. I'm a New England patron, and I'm fully 100% bought into this program now. >> Thanks. Thank you guys.

title: Mike Vrabel on the Season Opener: "Wednesday Night is When Everything Has to be Ready to Go."

title: Jets 53-Man Roster Reaction + Is a 2-0 Start in Reach?
text: The Jets 53man roster is set and there's a lot to discuss with that. Kate Clubnix, the backup quarterback. Right move or wrong move? That and much more is what we're breaking down on today's Jets Collective, which starts right now. [music] It's the first day of September, which means the Jets play regular season football this month. Hello everyone. My name is Jake Asmin. You're watching or listening to the Jets Collective right here on YouTube, wherever you get your podcast, Apple, Spotify, and iHeart. We are presented by Prize Picks. And as always, I'm joined alongside Rich Samini and Brandon Tyranny. Fellas, the 53man roster is set. We got that to discuss. The practice squad, Jets Titans, is just 12 days away. Rich, you've covered a lot of these cut down days. What was your experience with this one? My experience is that we had to wait a long time until they put out the roster. It was about 9:00 and I, you know, just to give the fans a little background, they do that strategically, the Jets. There were five other teams that did that. They don't like to advertise their names during the day, uh, for competitive reasons. So, that's why we waited till 9:00. Um, but no surprises at all. I mean, this was the roster I think many of us expected. The big story for me was the kicking situation because we saw what happened last Friday night against the Giants after Chris Banjo told Rich Samini that Jason Sanders won the kicking job. Well, that was shortlived with a missed extra point, a missed field goal from 54 yards that was at least five plus yards short. So, you knew they were going to add a kicker. And one of the big takeaways, Rich, from the Jets roster is the waiver claim they put in for Groupy. He's about an 81 to 82% career success rate, which was, you know, 85% is considered good. He's uh he's got a strong leg. He's only 5'7, by the way. I'm sure we'll get back to that as well. I mean, what is the equivalent of a of an NFL kicker coming up at least five yards short? What is that? Like a major league pitcher throwing an 81 mile per hour fastball. Like, it's so substandard. It's alarming. And the fact that it got to this point is really embarrassing and really unacceptable. So, hopefully this pivot works out. Otherwise, not to be, you know, I'm prone to hyperbole here, but I mean, there's a chance this could destroy their season. I expect a lot of tight games and if the kicker is not good, the Jets have massive issues. If let's say Greg Zerline hits that kick in the rain to beat the Denver Broncos, right? I mean and there were several other games that year where their kicking situation cost him. I go back 2019, the Adam Gase debut game. They're up 16 nothing on the Bills and Kareem Vivik is shanking kick after kick that cost the Jets that day. I think Chris Banjo's really good at special teams coordination. So I'm hoping that, you know, groupy could be their guy. I don't think he's making the final call on which kicker they keep. I mean, that would be a little bit more acceptable, but but they were absolutely flush with cash. Here's one thing I've always wondered, and this is not even just the Jets that that don't do this. I I I question why every team in the league doesn't do this. We see all the time these sixth and seventh round picks in the draft turn out to be nothing. >> Yep. >> I would draft whoever the top kicker is in college football every year in the sixth or seventh round. I don't see the harm in it. Especially if you're a team like the Jets where you had multiple day three late in the draft selections. I don't know why more teams don't use seventh round picks. I'm just trying to take the best kicker possible. >> I I agree with you as as a concept. I think it's a little more it depends on the team like the specific needs. Like some teams get the benefit of the doubt. Uh, not that you're making moves based on public sentiment, at least you shouldn't be. But also, you know, a bad team like the Jets, I mean, there's been a lack of depth. I mean, when you're so bad uh for as long as they've been, teams like the Browns, the Giants trying to pull their way out of the wilderness, the Raiders, you know, the Dolphins now like, and I I get it. It's a little tougher to sell unless you get it right. But but but I so I I agree with you, but I I do think if you're a team light on depth like the Jets have been, it it's a little tougher sell a little bit. Not much though. It's a good point, Jake. >> Yeah. Two things on that. When these GMs treat these late round picks, sixth and seventh rounders, like gold chips, you know, so we we may kind of minimize the value of them, they don't. They they they see players, you know, they see, you know, backup safeties and backup linebackers. Giants took a chance and it looks like they struggled gold with, you know, because he looks like a pretty good kicker >> and and that's a guy that I'll take a chance of like he's kicking at the big house in front of 110,000 people. text: Morning. >> Coach, your your decision to uh go with Jaylen as your number two quarterback, when did that become the most apparent to you and and um just what is it that you think you know, he'll be able to function without any experience in the role? >> I mean, we started seeing it in camp.
