I don't think anybody rookies going to go through preseason unscathed. He's going to learn some things that way, but he's a very bright guy. He understands what he has to do to get better. He works at the things he needs to do to get better even when he's on the scout team. So, we see a lot of promise there and he's just got to continually get get better and I'm sure we think he will. >> Does the fact that he has some of the skill sets, he's almost the exact same size as Baker, but can throw on platform, make plays with his feet. Does Does that help from an offensive standpoint going in if there is a transition at some point? >> I mean, it helps his escapability and familiarity to Zach, but at the same time, he's a very bright guy. He's not just a uh roll out and run around passer. He can sit in the pocket and throw the ball. He can direct traffic very well. He just needs time on task. >> Coach, you hear my coaches some coaches don't like rookies as much or like trusting veterans more. You'll have a lot of rookies all over this defense this season. Do Do you even think of it that way or what You don't seem to have a lot of hesitance to to throw these guys out right away and ask them to make plays? >> There's no age limit on when you can play. You know, once you come in the league, if you can learn it fast enough and you're a good football player, you're going to play here. >> Every season teams have different identities. What What do you feel like is a strength of this team that it can really lean on? >> I believe we're mentally tough. Again, we haven't played a game yet. Our identity is yet to be revealed, but I think we are very mentally tough and we have more leaders overall than we've had in the past. >> And um to that point, do you see an area on this team that is your biggest strength? >> I think all areas right now working to be better. That'll determine itself. We feel like we got a lot of depth in some areas. We feel like we got a lot of front line strength. So, if we can stay healthy, hopefully every area is a strength on this team. >> Coach, these two practices obviously they're shorter practices. Is it just getting guys in the rhythm of this is your room, this is what you'll be working on this year? >> Well, Well, gives us a head start on Cincinnati. It gives us a jump start, you know, you can't get into much, but we we got to get in shape and we got to go from playing eight to 10 plays to 60 to 70 plays. So, that part that's part of it as well. So, we got to get in a rhythm and they got to get used to the grind of the season. >> Jason had told us when he spoke to us this summer that he had never seen Baker so focused. Have you Have you picked up on that as well? >> I believe he's the same since he's been here. You know, he's always focused when he goes out there. He's always in the building early. He's always studying to be better. That's just him, whether it's this year, last year, the year before. He probably has a better grasp of things, especially the offense, after being in one similar a couple years ago. So, he probably has a better grasp of things. >> Todd, we saw Reuben Bain out there participating. AC joint sprain, was his recovery a little bit faster than expected? >> Uh I don't think so. We were expecting him to play. He said he's feeling good, so we're going to roll with that, but he feels good and we're going to play with it. >> Anything else? Thank you. >> Yep. >> Thank you. Should be a good game.

title: Jason Licht Discusses 53-Man Roster Decisions | Press Conference Live Stream
text: Morning. All right. Fire away. >> Jason, talk about the decision to make Jaylen Daniels your number two quarterback. Undrafted rookie, hasn't played a snap in the NFL. Big year for you guys, obviously. What was it that gave you the confidence that he could step in there and get it done in week one? >> Well, that's a it's an incredible accomplishment for an undrafted rookie to get that position. Um I can't think in the last decade another time it's happened. And but the the number one thing is he earned it. Um he wasn't just give it given to him. You don't get that honor by just being lucky or or having somebody pull strings for you. He um He earned it, like I said. He earned the trust of his teammates, his coaches. You guys have seen him out here practice during camp. Did some really great things in the game and you know, you can go back and forth with the experience um argument, but we'd rather have a very talented prepared inexperienced quarterback than going with experience just for the sake of saying it the guy's experienced. So, he's like all rookie quarterbacks, whether you're the number one overall pick or undrafted, um you're going to there's going to be a learning curve. There's going to be ups and downs, but we feel good about where he's at, his trajectory, and and uh we're excited. >> It probably had some stages where like you realized like wow, he he has to be on the 53 now. And then you go from that to wow, could he be the two? Was there Was there like a a clinching moment or a a reinforcing moment for you to where he gave you the confidence to do what what most teams don't do with their backup quarterback? >> Todd and I have a lot of conversations after during practice, before practice, after practice, uh at night. In his case, early in the morning. And um I think it was we before our first preseason game, we loved what we were seeing out here, the the what we were getting from uh Zach and Chandler and T.J. Um and then I think after the first preseason game with the Jets, I think that uh that started to the conversation started going towards well, he's got to prove that he can't be the number two more so than he's got to prove that he can be. >> What about Aidan Gardner? He's a guy that every single day it seemed like he was coming out here and making plays. >> Well, didn't seem like he was, he was. >> True. >> Um it yeah, every day was making a play on the ball, interception or multiple plays on the ball. He's He's got excellent instincts. He's tough. What I liked about him and I was talking with some of our players about this that he he didn't have a I'm not saying cocky air to him. He just had a very confident air to him and he he knows he's good and and he kind of carried that with him and at that position you have to have a lot of confidence. So he's got that going for him, too. He's also a rookie, so still got a ways to go here, but we we're very excited about him as well. >> But like every time that that room had an injury or somebody had a a day off he he stepped in and it didn't really matter the competition that he was going up against. It could have been Emeka Egbuka, you know, it could have been Ted Hard like those are all really talented players. Seems like he held his own. >> Yeah, he that's you nailed it. He doesn't care who he's going against. He sees them all as the same. He doesn't have any bias. >> Can you talk about the running back the situation? I see that you decided to keep Sean Tucker, do a little different, you know, with his deal, then also bring Josh onto the practice squad and then combine with Gainwell and Bucky Irving. >> Love that group, that entire group. And just the way that you can construct your roster and keep guys on the practice squad and elevate them. You can, you know, do that whole thing and there's the roster management, the puzzle. It's It's We feel very, very fortunate that we can keep all four cuz we like all four, but you know, Sean's done some really good things for us in the past. He's an explosive runner. He's He's got very good speed and I think it's a nice compliment with uh running backs that we have including Josh. >> What's the toughest position group to decide on when building this roster? >> Well, I don't want to know toughest the one you know, the first thing comes to mind is we have really good depth as good as I can remember or have had here in my tenure at outside linebacker. very very feel very good about that. I had to make a couple decisions on whether or not we were going to keep extra there. But that was that was tough. That's a good It's a good position to be in though. >> Jack Coons had a couple of big moments in the preseason. You know, obviously as you said it's a loaded position group but and uh people have been talking about him obviously with the college situation but he was locked in on trying to get a spot. How difficult was that decision to cut him? >> It was Yeah, it's it's hard. None of these decisions are are easy for us. Uh it was tough. You know, he did a he did some really good things but so did some other guys that we decided to keep on the 53. Um would love to have him on the practice squad. Would have been great. But you know, you you don't always get what you want. You can't always have your cake and eat it too. So, uh wish him the best of luck. He did a great job for us and and uh has a chance to be a a pretty good player. >> Jason, edge rushers have been that position you've been trying to solve the last couple of years now and you just kind of mentioned you have depth at that position. How much of a relief is it that not just depth but the talent you have at that position now? >> Yeah, it feels good. Now, we haven't played a game yet but it feels very good from what we've seen so far and from all of them. Uh I want to name all of them. I mean, you guys know what's on the roster. So, and I mean, I'll just go down to Anthony Nelson who also had a strong preseason and he's been Mr. Clutch for us over the years. So, feel very very good about that that position. >> Jason, one of the tricky parts with with cutting the 53 is is wanting to get the the 16 17 guys on the practice squad the way you want. And you guys kind of went against uh like the traditional norms in terms of positional lines to carry seven D-linemen and have only three safeties. How How well Auburn is gone, but how well other than that did this go in terms of you being able to keep the depth you wanted to have both between the roster and the practice >> I I think we I think we we the the plan that we had, you know, it's it went into effect and been able to keep like uh you know, the safeties and the ones that we wanted on the practice squad and we think can line up and play on Sunday on next Sunday. So, because of the uh rules that we have, elevations and things like that, it's obviously this roster is not set in in stone. It can be fluid. It could be fluid today, tomorrow, next week leading [clears throat] up to the game. So, we're always going to be looking for ways that we can upgrade depth at all positions. So, but it we were happy with the way it turned out. >> You have some pretty young corners on this team. To be able to get Sean Murphy-Bunting back even on the practice squad, how how reassuring is that? >> Yeah, they know that was great. He He really wanted to be here, too. He had a lot of opportunities and um I went down to talk to coach about it yesterday and, you know, he was obviously all in and, you know, he's done some really good things for us. And you know, it could be a player to watch for us and you know, he's going to add to the to the group and provide a lot of competition there. So, that's that's that's what you want. >> Is there one thing that stands out about Now you got the 53-man roster. You wanted to get tougher, I know on defense. Based on everything you brought in, Baine, what's the one thing that you think this roster, this team is better now than since last year? >> We already had a lot of competitive mature win-at-all-costs types of players. We wanted to bring in more and we think we accomplished that and just the vibe at practice, the vibe in the building, meetings, all those things just because of the the more that we added, it's really increased. And I just I really like this team. I've been in this business long enough to know that I can't come up here and give you predictions, but I just know that I really like the way that Todd is leading this team and what we've what we've added and uh it's it you know, it's pretty apparent. >> It's always great to have a team to have a go-to receiver, the guy that's going to make the big play in the big moment. You have to replace a guy, but it may be in the aggregate with your receivers. Who is that guy among this group that you know, that emerges now or is it just there's so many that, you know, you just let things take their course? >> We We have a lot of options at that, but I mean, I can't I'd be remiss if I didn't mention Chris Godwin for all that he's done for this organization and talk about being a consistent, steady, Mr. Clutch player, that's that's him and he looks very, very good out there right now. >> Jason's sticking in the wide receiver realm. Your thoughts on Trey Palmer's growing as a wide receiver? Has he kind of picked up faster or anything of that nature since arriving and getting more opportunities with Jalen McMillan out and Emeka Egbuka? >> Well, that that certainly helped him. You know, after after we drafted him, I personally thought, okay, this is a great situation for him to be behind these guys and learn. May not make a big impact for us this year, but you know, one for the future, but I think he's proven to us throughout camp even OTAs and um um practice every day that he's been very very steady. And I think it's kind of evolved into okay, we can use him this year and he's going to play a role. So. >> The last time we talked to you, you said that you had never seen Baker this focused. It's been some time now since that conversation. What more have you seen from him? >> The same thing. You know, we love Baker. you know, Baker there's there's nothing fake about Baker. Sometimes I wish there was maybe 10% more fake, but um he's certainly uh motivated and uh we love that. >> What about the fact that he's not afraid to say what's on his mind and what's on his heart. He wears his emotions on his sleeve, but when he's out there on the field he's able to manage that to in terms of like not letting that affect his performance, whereas some athletes it can result in in you know, mistakes and things like that. So, just his ability to kind of keep himself composed uh amid you know, a summer where I know he wanted to get a new contract. He wasn't able to get it, but just his ability to go out there with that setback and and perform each day. >> Yeah, that was never a question of whether or not he would be able to focus and compartmentalize. Uh that's a really strong trait of his. So. Yeah, I'm very excited for for the season. >> Obviously, the offensive line feels it's their responsibility to to protect Baker. As he gets older, how much responsibility falls on Baker to protect Baker? >> Um that's a great question. Um he's I think I think he's very mindful of that. I think all quarterbacks as they as they have progressed through their career, um I think they are a little bit more uh in tune with that. So, I think I think if if you would ask him, I'm not sure how what the answer would be, but I think he's probably pretty mindful of that. >> You talked about Kaden Fordham and what you saw from him this camp that got him on the team. >> You know, he's a very instinctive Uh every day, practice, games, making a lot of plays in the right spot. He was I think the leading tackler in the NCAA last year, and I don't you don't do that [clears throat] by accident. And so, I think he's he's got a really bright future being a you know, not only as a linebacker, but special teams. And we're putting a little emphasis on that. >> I'm going to paraphrase a little bit, but you said before the game the other night that you were confident that Baker will be here for a longer term. Um roughly uh from my understanding, there's not been any communication going either way at this point. Will that re- connect Will that reignite? Do you have plans to to re-engage that, or is are you just like, "I'm going to respect the deadline, and we'll talk after the season"? >> Well, we certainly respect um him wanting to focus on the season. We're focused on the season. Um to get been here long enough to know that in this league, I don't want to make predictions on what could happen, what will happen, what won't happen. Right now, we're all focused on uh I've been waiting to say this for a long time. It's on to Cincinnati. >> Coach, I don't think we've talked since uh last year when some receivers went down. Just what do you look for him in in year two in this league? >> I'm sorry, say that again. I couldn't >> You saw a guy like Chester Johnson step up last year when some guys went down with injuries. Just what do you look for him in year two? >> Uh making taking a step forward. Um he's explosive player. Love his energy. Everybody does. Can see him having even more of an impact for us this year. >> I don't think we've talked since uh you guys re-signed Mebane. I know we haven't. So, if you could speak on that, I saw you were rubbing his back there on his first day of practice there, and you guys were smiling. So, how happy are you guys to just kind of figure that out and get back in? >> Very happy. Very exciting. Anytime a man of his presence and what he's done and his size comes to me and says that he wants to stick around and you normally want to accommodate >> Jason, aside from Baker, you have a number of other guys in contract year. You have A.J. Epenesa, Chase McLaughlin, Cody Mauch. Any dialogue with any of those guys and their agents at this point? >> You know, I'm probably not going to talk about that. Apparently, I don't like to talk about what's going on. Um, but those guys are all outstanding players for us and love to have all of them in the future, but once again, on to Cincinnati. >> There's a high number of quarterbacks in this league that are that are making over 50 million a year. I want to say it's like 12. Um, that's that's a huge chunk of change. Um, can you just explain like the thought process about, you know, when you when you're preparing to make an investment like that? And and also, you know, is that something ownership is comfortable with? >> You know, you're always comfortable with a great player and you make things work. >> Jason, with with Keaton, we kind of talk about undrafted rookies as all one thing, but a lot of these undrafted guys get like $200,000 guaranteed. Keaton got $2,000 to sign here. I think there's four guys that made rosters across the entire league that got less than that. Um, in terms of the the reach and the depth of scouting, just what that says and then and how cool it is to have a long shot like that go through. >> Uh, that's awesome. It's it's a scout's dream. It's uh it's what they do this for. You know, I think I said this on the radio the other day, that if there's once the draft is over, that's the part that everybody gets gets all the media, all that, rounds 1 through 7, but then rounds 8, 9, and 10, that's when I step aside and let them do their work and and they uh they love it. They they crave it and they've been doing a really, really, really good job um for us. It's uh it's always a you know, it's always a bonus when you can get somebody like that. So, you know, but then you root for him to play well and give him a second deal, which we've done a lot of. >> Jason, what about Josiah Trask? What's one of the biggest things that stood out to you after some preseason games going into the camp and everything? What stood out to you the most after drafting him? he's he's a dog. He He turns his uh has a switch once he gets out there and everybody sees it. And it's what the great players have. So, we're hoping that he keeps ascending and becomes a great player that we think he can be. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Thanks, Mr. Licht. >> Thanks. Appreciate it.

title: Darius Slayton: 'We have a lot of really talented guys' in the WR room | New York Giants
text: your name had come up as a I don't know how much you've paid attention again. Feels like an annual thing, but came up as a potential trade ship. >> Yeah. >> What did it mean to see that and then to make the roster? >> Uh, nothing really. It's not the first time. Probably won't be the last time, but you know, I really don't pay it too much in mind, honestly. You know, I just take it day by day. >> Is that easier just as a vet obviously seeing so much and being around as much? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, you kind of just figure out the league as you're the more you're around. So, at the end of the day, it's you control what you can control and let the rest fall in me. >> How do you feel like the summer went for you? >> Uh, it went solid. I think I had a solid summer. You know, obviously, um, trying to shake back, you know, from rehab and all of that. So, you know, I had some bumps along the way, but, you know, overall, I think, you know, I put together a solid summer. >> Say, how how are you feeling? How close to 100% are you feeling at this point in terms of getting back to football shape and all that stuff from a major surgery? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, I feel pretty good. You know, I wouldn't I wouldn't say 100 yet, but you know, definitely trending in the right direction. >> How do you think you fit in this wide receiver role? >> Um, just another playmaker. You know, I feel like we have a bunch in the room. you know, a lot of really talented guys um that we've added to the roster, but you know, I see myself as one of those guys and, you know, whatever um capacity that I can be. >> What do you make of the room as a whole now that it's more settled? >> Yeah. Um kind of like I just said, I think we have a lot of really talented guys, some vets, some some young guys obviously like Malachi and Malik that kind of round out the youth of the room, but you know, obviously Mooney's a really good vet, Braxton's a good vet. Um, Odell obviously, you know, has has done well this preseason. So, you know, I think we have we have a strong room. >> What have you seen from Malaka just throughout the summer from start to finish? >> What have I seen? >> Yeah, just his growth as a rookie. >> Yeah, I mean, I think he's done a great job being on top of his assignments. You know, he's a smart kid and, you know, he's a big kid and he plays big. You know, there's a lot of big people in life that don't always play big or or, you know, act to their size, but, you know, I think he does a good job of that and that that's what allows him to be successful. just for a typical spot for you where you're, you know, every single year as long as you've been here where you've just got to prove yourself again. >> Yeah. Well, I mean, it's mostly kind of been exacerbated by the turnover. So, anytime there's new people, you know, there's there's going to be that. And so, you know, just for me, I've just been fortunate to be here for four staff. So, um you know, I don't I don't I don't take it personally. You know, I understand that, you know, you have to you have to show and prove yourself um you know, whenever there's new. So, it's what I plan to do this year. >> Does does being the longest tenured here through all those changes mean anything to you? >> I think it does. I mean, I think, you know, maybe contrary to common belief, it would studies would suggest that I've done more good than bad. You know, otherwise I probably would have been gone with three different people coming here and evaluating me. But, um, you know, it is what it is. You told us before that I think in West Virginia that um you were this close to playing with Odell and you thought it was some mythical creature, but now that he's actually here, what does it mean to be his teammate or season? >> Yeah, I think it's really cool. I mean, I think obviously, you know, it's cool to see somebody be able to get their chance at um redemption maybe, I guess, or you know, kind of just having a chance to to rewrite a story that kind of felt, I guess, a little bit unfinished, you know, with him leaving here so early. And um you know, I think it's a beautiful thing for him to come back here. Obviously, you know, the fans love him, you know. Well, really, if you're a football fan, you probably love him, you know, cuz he was such an iconic player, but yeah, it's definitely awesome to see him get a chance to be back. >> What is the most different thing about these practices, you know, under this regime for someone who's seen, as you said, several several different versions of how the preseason looks? >> Yeah, I mean, these practices have definitely been probably the longest in duration, but I would say they've been the fact they've been the longest in duration, but they've been the most efficient. So like the way we practice is very the tempo is high, you know, we're going from period to period. So even though the the time is long, it doesn't feel as long as you would think because of the speed at which we practice and the efficiency that we practice at. >> What have you learned about John Harbaugh in that time? >> What have I learned? Harbaugh in the time since he started coaching you guys? >> Um, he's a stickler for the details. You know, he's a stickler for the details. you know, he has a he has a um an appetite for excellence and that's what he expects out of everybody, you know, coaches and players alike. So, you know, I think that's definitely something that he's enforced from the first day he's been here and enforced throughout camp. [music]

Really the only outlier year of Andrew Thomas's career is his rookie year, where, you know, he gave up 57 pressures. His only missed games were carryover from the year before injury, which the Lisfranc injury was legitimately scary, you know. >> miss the last two games with the hamstring. We all think that he probably could have played through that if But it But like that's >> nothing to play for, yeah. >> Yeah, there there still is worse, and like these things do pop up with Andrew Thomas. And and that, you know, the hamstring has happened before, you know, in 2023, you know, the the disaster season. You know, he sprained his He played the second half of that year on a sprained MCL. You know, and like like you mentioned, every year's like after his rookie year, for uh 2021, fourth for left tackles in pass blocking efficiency. 2022, fourth. Uh 2023, seventh. Last year or not last year, the year before last year was a little bit of an outlier. Um but you go you when you look at it, it's like, all right, yeah, that game against Micah Parsons. We didn't get a sack, but that was the toughest matchup. And I actually want to talk about that when we're Micah Parsons or not Micah Parsons, Myles Garrett, um when we go forward here. And then, he gave up uh two sacks to Trey Hendrickson on the Lisfranc injury that that, you know, had him out for up until through the next year. So, like those numbers were a little skewed. Like And it's And this is a guy who you know, some of these guys will go, "Good pass blocking efficiency. They get so much help." Thomas like leads the league in island rate every single year. I like and I don't think people understand how much of a luxury it is to have your left tackle like that. Like it's going to suck when he leaves. Like maybe we'll be like the Green Bay Packers of left tackles. Uh and we just replace him. But like I I I dread the day that he's not a New York Giant anymore because it's such a luxury to number one, you don't have to give your left tackle any help. That helps what you can do offensively. text: It's everything. >> Uh, man, it's everything. Um God had a plan for me. Um and now being able to be here, to walk in here, I remember coming here practice and seeing the '86 to '90, the 2007-11 banners, and I was like, man, I just just want to bring one here. And um I think you'll always hear me talk about it. I feel like no matter what team you're on, like that's the goal. Nobody's playing just to play and, you know, you all want to win. Um so that was kind of the message I had to the group is like it's one thing to get here, it's an honor and a privilege, but how do you take that next step each and every day? Um and find ways to level up. >> Take us through the emotions of the last of yesterday and and even the last couple weeks here. >> Yeah. Um over the last couple weeks, it was just a grind. You know, like you you obviously trying to think if you're going to make it or not or >> No matter what, it was on the back of my mind. Uh Don't know last year whatever it is. Uh I just know I'm going to give my all, but definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the some of the the pain that I feel like I've went through. Um and and it was just a very healing, very very emotional uh uh something I was very happy about. >> What was that like to deal with that kind of pressure first time to have to experience that at >> It It definitely, like I said, it was um it was a different feeling. You know, slow news days, some sometimes people are going to use my name to boost their own whatever it is, so it is what it is. It comes with the territory. And I think if we're if we're just judging everyone through the lens of Jordan Mailata, it's going to be hard to give these guys a fair chance. Still very excited about them. Really glad that they did get through. Certainly wasn't certain about that. Certainly wasn't certain. But, anyway, you've been around long enough to have have a good pulse of how you want your roster to look and have those gut feelings at this point in this season. Just from a broader point of view, how do you feel about this week heading into week one? >> Yeah, I think this is a humbling game and every time you feel good about something, something comes up that makes you feel not so good. So, I would say, you know, from our perspective, what I feel good about is that we have conviction about certain areas of our football team that we want to keep strong. Um it shows up in our roster. That will show up over time during the season. Um what that means, we're going to have a lot of things happen during the course of the season. Adversity will strike us. Unfortunately, injuries are part of the game. Who that is, when that happens, all those stories are not yet written. And so, I just sit here and just going to take it one day at a time. Continue to evaluate opportunities to continue to get better. Um and just make sure that we're putting our players in the best position to have success and our coaches do a great job of that. >> How where is you all Bernard in his development? I know he had played organized football. Where where might he be in progress? There's good things and bad things that he can >> Well, it's it's all new to him. I mean, every single thing you think about it. Even the first preseason game for him to go play that game for the first time in front of that stadium. Um tremendous work ethic, tremendous character. Obviously, he's got some God-given ability there in terms of strength and power, but you know, when you think about this game and and blocking schemes and getting off the ball and all the things that guys have taken for granted. You know, those are things that that come with time and reps. He's got a great coach and coach Hurt there working with him and again, I think the expectations have to be a little bit reasonable. You know, we saw yesterday or two days ago that there was a trade of an IPP guy who came into the league in 2023. You know, and and for the first time he's making an active roster in 2026. And I'm not saying that's a timeline for anything, but it's just a reminder that things take time. We live in a world where there's not a lot of patience and what we are committed to is patience and development. >> There were four guys claimed as as you referenced. What was your interpretation of that? And as you put the bottom of the roster together, it seemed you have more vested veterans this year and you've kind of used those spots for developmental purposes in in the past. Am I Am I right in that and is there a change in that thinking? >> No, I think that you got to look at the roster of 70 guys and you know, I think when our practice squad comes out, you'll see that maybe it's a little bit younger than it than it has been in the past. And so for our from our perspective when we're looking at the bottom of the roster, we're kind of looking we're trying to do our best to see who we can keep. Some of those guys, you know, think it in a vacuum it's easy to say, "Hey, put this guy in the practice squad and you'll get him back and he's a vested vet." But understanding that those guys have other options to go other places and when you say that to a veteran and and they say, "Hey, I'm going to explore my options." and you got 31 other teams and they say, "We'll give you 53 man spot." now you lose that guy. And so you're trying to combine that with the knowledge of how guys are doing and try to make an educated bet on on losing guys. You know, from our perspective over the weekend probably anticipated we would lose a couple of guys. To be fair, we always anticipate that. The rate of claims in the league is about 4%. Um, certainly those percentages didn't apply to our roster over this weekend, unfortunately, but that's the risk of doing business and don't feel good about that. Don't feel good about losing those guys. Um, We lost two draft picks. Um, we lost a special teamer tight end to attend special teams tackles for us last year on a block kick. Don't feel good about that. You know, we lost a young defensive back that we liked. And so that goes along with this. And so you can't sit here and feel tremendously good when you're losing players. We'll do our best to try to replenish that. Um, I told coach Clay I owed him one. So I'll I'll do my best to help him make up for it, but Um, yeah, certainly like to say wish those guys well, but but don't feel great about it. >> How were the conversations like with a guy like Damien Pierce to try to get him to come back on a practice squad? >> Yeah, sometimes you just run out of time. You know, you run out of time in terms of guys get nicked during camp. They miss some time. You want them part of the team. Um We're not We're not showing everything in the preseason, you know, that's that's not what anyone's doing. So, you get an opportunity uh the first four games of the season have always kind of been uh kind of another ramp-up period for for your football team. And so, you get an opportunity to evaluate uh the trade deadline's a long way away. Uh we have the resources to continue improving the team. Uh we'll continue to do that over the next couple of days as well. Um and at the same time um love what we have going in our tight end room, too. So, um I would say, you know, have talked to Zach um over a period of time, obviously rehabbing his ACL and the relationship. Um just like a lot of our former players who've been here. Um and then obviously um we talked a a little bit there um about Elijah. Uh >> How do you feel Quez has adjusted to the new offense? >> I think Quez has adjusted really well to the new offense. And Quez has embraced it. Um he's excited about it. I mean, really, really excited about those guys, about being able to have those guys, being able to develop those guys, but at the same time have confidence that if those guys need to play, that they're ready to play. How long before the youth talking point kind of becomes all right, let's let's get it into gear. >> Yeah, it it's in the gear now. Like there there is no there's no uh excuse making. There's no leash. Like the the we've got to get great very very fast. Um, but I I made the comment a couple of times with regards to this being our floor, like you give a young guy reps, they're going to get better. They have no choice but to get better. And when those the objective has always been forever, uh, forgive me, I'm going to be a little winded on this one. You know, like a coach always wants a veteran out there because they know what to do. Um, uh, they're where they're supposed to be, but they're not exactly running the 40 they used to run when they ran at the combine. A scout wants the young guy because they're as fast as explosive, but a coach is afraid of them because they're you have no idea what you're going to get play to play. So, the objective is how quickly can you get that young guy to play like that veteran while he's still running the 40 he ran at the combine, right? And uh the the best way to do that is give him reps. And uh we've got a young group, an explosive group. There's a mixture of some really cool veterans that are still in their prime um on this team. and uh and the hope is that the combination of veterans pulling the young guys with them uh we get to that that point of uh elite speed very quickly. >> Do you talk to the practice squad guys letting them know you're just as much a part of this team? >> Oh yeah. So we got I don't know if you noticed like a bunch of guys stay after. So we uh we have a a development period after practice where all the practice squad and the guys who either a didn't get enough reps or b are trying to work a different position where you know from a from a versatility standpoint uh you've got five minutes of individual to work through and then we run a seven on seven where they're the calls being made are the calls that are uh within the game plan. So, they've got to stay clued in. They've got to stay connected to their techniques. They've got to stay connected to their uh they're not just showing up to practice. Uh they understand that, you know, they're, you know, I I don't like calling it the practice squad. It's the next 16. You know, they're they're next up. You know, if there's an injury at running back, Michael Carter's coming up. Um and so [clears throat] it's a uh so that we do our best to try to keep them involved as best we can, and we do it with our postpractice period. Robert, bringing in five players uh off of waiverss, etc., uh what's the challenge with that getting them up to speed as opposed to some of the guys that are on the practice squad now who were here in camp and and how much of an indication of this being a changing team and and roster when you bring in that many guys at this point? Yeah, it's uh the challenge first off for those guys is to get acclimated to this uh to this son out here. But uh and then you mix in all the all the different techniques like we're different like you you talk about a guy like Sack House uh who we brought in from Green Bay. The techniques he's learning are completely different than what uh he had at Green Bay. Uh both fantastic techniques not but they're different. And uh then you mix in the uh just the the schedule, the routine, all the different things that they have to go through moving. There's a lot of moving parts for those young men who came in here and uh it's our job to try to make it as seamless as possible and get them up to speed as quickly as possible. >> Was a guy did get a lot of talk when he came in, but he really had some hand. >> Yeah, he's uh uh one one thing you're going to find out about us is we uh if you can rush the passer, you've got a home here. And uh Truman has gotten so much better in such a short amount of time. He's shown his ability to be dynamic in pass rush. Uh he's gotten a lot better against the run. Uh he's not where he needs to be to uh uh to be a staple on that third down crew that rushes the passer consistently, but he's but he's an ascending player for sure. >> What you said about the veterans versus the youth. Take uh Anthony Hill Jr., apply that to him. What does he have to do to get on the field more? And how has his process been just as far as learning that position, being the quarterback for the defense? >> Yeah, he's uh he's he's done a great job. You know, he's gotten a lot better. His communication's gotten a lot better. Um, knock on wood, we've got we've got a pretty cool linebacker room, and that I feel like all four of them are starting caliber between uh Cody said, Anthony, and uh James uh learning our the the the call him the new guy from Arizona. Uh but uh th those four that have been here, they're in my mind, they're all starter type players. Uh so we're we're fortunate in that regard and and Anthony has been able to learn at his pace and he's gotten a lot better. >> Last one talked about just Cam, his ascension over uh over training camp and what you've seen from him. Anything you have to say to him now is like the the switch gets flipped to it's it's regular season mode and it's go time. Have you seen that in him? >> Yeah. you know it uh all these guys should be at in my opinion there should be a full tilt whether it's OTAAS training camp walkthrough it doesn't matter uh my message to every player including Cam is to keep ascending uh you can't stay the same you've got to find a way to get better pick something anything to get better at that uh that helps you perform on Sunday and uh for him and again everyone on the roster is just because you made the team doesn't mean that parts can't move um you we we can't have complacency. We need to attack every moment and for Cam being the quarterback of this football team. He needs to continue ascending. And I'll say it again, he's nowhere near where I think he's going to be. Um he's a he's a young man. He's second year in the league. Um he's going to get a lot better as time goes. >> Jim, last one. >> Uh how did Fernando do during the start, you know, the start of camp up until now? Did he do enough to to earn the starting job? >> Yeah. Uh Fernando's going to start at right guard. Um I thought he's done an outstanding job. Uh you know, we gave him the opportunity to uh step in there and show what he can do and and when he when he got in that spot, he just wouldn't relent. And uh credit to him. He's a mer. He's a fighter. He's a strainer. He's got a lot of work to do. Um as you guys know, he's going to see some of the best uh dtackles in all of football. And um and but I do think he's up up for the challenge. >> Thanks, everyone.

title: Fernando Carmona & Truman Jones on Making the 53 | Press Conference
text: Playing in the NFL? >> Not once, man. Uh I always told myself I would never really play football at that time and it was funny cuz it was a tennis court right here and then the football court and every morning or every afternoon all the football players would yell at me across from the gate and like, "Come join us. Come join us." And I was like, "Nope, I'm fine playing tennis." And then sure enough, man, we're here. >> How good of a tennis player were you? >> Say that again? >> How big were you as a tennis >> I was about 6'4", 225, so played right up at the net. >> Did you guys ever play doubles or what was the size of your doubles court? >> Yeah, I was doubles and then he was about 6'2" and so we covered up a lot of ground. >> Wrestling tag team or a tennis tag team? >> Tennis. Tennis. >> Who ended up talking you into football? >> Uh so my my dad had played, my brother had played collegiately and my cousin's husband was actually the high school football coach, so I had a lot of people in my ear each and every day and then I think just sometime my junior during summer I was like, I looked at my brother, I was like, "Let's go to Burlington. Let's get me some cleats and I want to go play football." >> Every time your name is mentioned like somebody says nasty, where does that come from? That that style of play, that that mindset, that approach to the game? >> You know, something I had to learn in college. Off the field I'm a very friendly guy and it's something that you have to learn when you cross these lines. You know, all these guys can't be your buddies and you know, they're your teammates, you got to take care of them but at the end of the day you got to get your work and that took me a while in college to learn how to find that nastiness. My O-line coach Josh Oglesby at San Jose State and now at Arizona helped me a lot you know, overcome that mental barrier but it took some time. >> At what point did you say, "I can win this thing. I can start here." >> Uh I think that's just kind of been my mindset, you know, ever since I mean, leading into combine prep like I knew I could play in this league and I could be a starter and I've just kind of always had that belief in myself and I know my work will always lead me to that. >> What do you think helped us kind of accelerate your growth once you first got into camp up until this point. >> Uh really just just being consistent and that's just something that I've always I've really tried to home in on uh these past 2 years of my football journey is consistency cuz that's really what offense line's all about is uh just being consistent and you know not having your man tackle the guy with the ball. >> Was it important to you in your development to make that jump from San Jose to Arkansas so you weren't making a bigger leap to the NFL? >> 100% and that was a big part in the you know transferring. I love San Jose State. It always will have a a spot in my heart but I knew I had to face you know that that next level and I felt like the closest thing to that was the SEC and I got that week in and week out and uh I'm glad I made that move. >> How different is what you're being asked to do here from what you were expected to do at Arkansas? >> Uh you know it's not too much different. Uh I feel like Coach Carm lets us play really freely and uh you know I feel like that's helped me out a lot cuz I could just go out there not really think too much and just play fast. >> What's your relationship with Pat and what's it been like for you guys to kind of go through this thing together? >> Yeah me and me and PC are we're really good buds. Uh he's helped me out a lot. I mean we literally call him PC cuz he's just he's a genius. The way he retains everything uh he just is a true center and uh even a bet like a good friend of mine uh he helps me out a lot with just plays and uh he's going to be a great player and he's been a big help to my journey cuz I don't know he's just like we said he's just a PC. He knows everything. >> How has it been slotting in with him and then JC on the other side as well? That you've been talk talked about your communication skills being one of your strengths as well. Have you been talking to them or do you sit back and listen more when you're between them? >> I definitely listen. Uh you know they've been the ones in the battles. They've played numerous seasons in this league. They're veterans and so they know what it is and uh you know I'll put in my two cents when I need to but most of the time it's just sitting back listening to them cuz, you know, they know what it is. >> Thought much about what it would be like a week from Sunday and and how you kind of keep your emotions in check for first first game first start? >> yeah, I really haven't thought too much about it. Right now, I'm trying to really home in on my routine for this week and just really mentally prepare myself to get to, you know, this Sunday even though we're not playing. I'm trying to, you know, go through this game week acting as if we were playing Sunday. So, I haven't really crossed that barrier. I think I'll probably Friday I'll start, you know, visualizing and having those kind of mental reps. >> You have a position where you have to barter for extra tickets for family coming to the town or are you guys all covered there? >> Yeah, we're all covered. Uh mom and dad try to make it down as much as possible and then the lady and my brother, uh they try to make it down a lot. But, yeah, we're all handled. They'll be there. >> What have you What have you In your eyes, how much better do you think you have gotten since you first arrived here a couple years ago? And what what have you made your biggest improvement? >> I think for me it's hard to say, you know, I feel like I still have a lot of ways to go and I'm looking for improvements every day. I felt like, um just getting into a new defense and now playing with my hand in the ground, so more four down and getting off the ball. Like that's been a transition back to college days. Um so, just getting used to going forward and setting edge and being really physical there. I feel like that's been a big improvement. >> Did you Did you feel like making this team was uh a pleasant surprise or do you feel like you just kind of earned it and uh were kind of expecting that to happen? >> I felt like it was a surprise for sure. I mean, we had a great room with a lot of great veterans. I mean, it was very competitive and, you know, I caught myself just looking at the names and things and would think, "How am I going to make this?" But, just put your head down every day and kind of work and then end up here. >> How do they make you better this year? >> How has this coaching staff made you better this year? >> I think they've just uh the scheme just allows you to play fast and think less. Like I went to Harvard, so I obviously think a lot and used to analyzing and processing a lot. But, here it's like you put your hand in the ground and you just have to go, you know. Give you a few things to look at and then you can react fast off of that. >> Is that hard for you? >> A little bit sometimes, but it's it's a nice change. >> I know you didn't come here without a goal of making it to the roster but at some point when did it become a really tangible aim and like I got a legit shot and I'm going to make it? >> Yeah, it's hard for me to say, you know, when they brought me here last year and claimed me off the practice squad in New England I felt like that was a they were taking a chance on me and from there I had to earn and show that I wanted to be here every day. So, coming into this training camp I still have that mentality of, you know, last year is last year. I still have to earn it again just knowing how training camp goes and um I'll tell you there's never really a clear moment just always I felt like I was in contention. >> Understanding that the roster is still fluid how much do you have to kind of keep that mentality? >> Yeah, always. Always. You can never get too comfortable. I mean, I've seen people get cut week 16 or like week 13. So, I've I've moved late in my career and had to do that plenty of times so I know every week is a new week and so allows me to just take every day and not take it for granted, you know, be appreciative to be here and be on this team. >> Saleh said that they value guys who can rush the passer and you showed you could do that in the preseason but he also said there's still things you got to learn and grow with. Do you Do you find find yourself with a specific role right now or how do you grow into a bigger role this year? >> Yeah, it's hard to say right now. My role is whatever they need me to do. If they want me to rush the passer on third down and they want me to set the edge on first and second. They want me to play special teams. I'll do anything needed to to be on the field. Um just want to use my size and my strength and my speed and get out there and be able to showcase that. >> Did you do anything different this offseason from a size standpoint kind of adjusting to a new technique and what they were going to ask you to do? >> I think um I think earlier in my career I had I struggled to put on weight a lot so I feel like going into year four it's like the first time I feel like my weight is really settled down and I'm getting more comfortable with it. So, um just getting more comfortable feeling athletic and just feeling like, you know, my natural athlete self instead of trying to bulk on and put on weight all the time. >> Where do you think you were or where are you now compared to when you first maybe came in the league as far as the weight wise? >> I mean, when I first came in the league I was 250 but I was stretching to get to 250 whereas now I'm 255 and eating much cleaner to maintain that. >> Ryan Fitzpatrick, the other Harvard guy, yeah, famously got a perfect score on the Wonderlic. >> Yes. How'd you do? >> See, they didn't tell me, but only got a couple questions wrong, I believe. Not perfect, but it was close. Yes, sir. >> Talked about the the overthinking. We hear so much about how this defense is just go straight. Is that liberating to a degree that you get to play in a different way? >> It's absolutely liberating. You know, we're still it's such We're playing football at a professional level, so there's so much to look at and so many keys, and we watch so much tape, but still once you get between those lines, you're allowed to just play fast and play free. And so, any issues that I come across, they usually get solved by going fast and playing violent. >> What was kind of going through your mind when you first landed here and when you got signed off of New England's practice squad? What's that like? When you first got here, what was kind of going through your mind? New team, wondering how you were going to fit in. >> Yeah, I mean, it happened in the middle of the week. I think I got the call, or not middle of the week, early in the week. I got a call Sunday night and was here Monday morning, and so from there I just knew I was going to be drinking from a fire hose and had to do a lot to catch up. You know, I hadn't gone through an off season with this team and wanted to wanted to show up and be able to play that first week. And so, just really kind of locked myself in a room, got very serious, was in a hotel every night, and staying here late meeting with coaches, but knew that they they brought me here for a reason and wanted to see what I could do. >> What do you think about the new regime and just the culture that's in place now? >> Yeah, the culture's great, especially among the D-linemen we have. Like, a lot of guys we just love having fun together and love being in the room. It's been a really enjoyable process, and I mean, we work really hard as well. We go hard on the field, we will go hard in recovery. Um we do it together as a team.

title: GM Mike Borgonzi Breaks Down the Titans' Final Roster | Titans Press Conference
text: Um, I thought it was a productive camp we had. Um, I just want to thank, you know, the entire organization really. I mean, there's so much that goes into a training camp. Uh, it's, you know, the coaches, the players, of course, uh, but there's so much more, uh, support staff, our grounds crew, um, you know, business, marketing for, you know, the fans that we had here this year. Uh, ownership, you know, providing some of the upgrades here that we had here at camp. Um, so, you know, last couple days are always tough when [snorts] you're when you have to say goodbye to some players here that, um, that have worked really hard here in the off-season. Um, they're tough decisions, but, uh, you know, we we felt like this is the 53 that we're going to go with right now, but we're constantly going to be looking to upgrade and add here as we go. But, um, but right now we're set. It's opening up. >> Do you feel like the 53 you've got today will be your 53 on opening day? >> Yeah, you know, it it it changes all the time. You're always looking. There's always you look at the waiver wire. Now there's practice squads that are set. We're always evaluating our practices every day and how how guys are doing. so it it could be the same, it could change. >> We all wondered about Bryce because we knew he was a special teams player. Who fills that role that that he vacated for you? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I think it's the the gunner role that you're talking about. Um, you know, I think Michael Robinson's done a really good job there. Um, you know, we've also Alex done some of that. Uh, we acquired, uh, Melvin Smith uh, in one of our waiver claims has done some of that in the past. Um, so we feel good about the position. >> What's the front office's perspective on the leap that Alex has taken or what he seems to have taken from his first year? >> Yeah, you know, I think it's just confidence with Alex. Um, the guy is a a tireless worker. he puts in so much, you know, effort and time in the in the weight room and studying and so it's it's really a credit to him but I but I do think you've seen that jump and I think that's a lot to do with just just confidence working at it. >> Melvin can can you give a cliff notes take on maybe the other four guys that you claim? >> Yeah so we added a couple of guys that were veterans. James Hudson's a you know been a tackle in the league that that has experience is is been with Daves and Carm in New York. And then on that side of the ball you know we added four guys there. With with Burgess who you know has been a safety in the league for a while has been a couple different teams had had a good year and then and with the Saints last year you know contributes on special teams. Then Melvin Smith you know was a guy that we've looked at he went to the senior bowl and couple of you know past couple years just preseason tape but he's a young corner small school kid from Southern Arkansas that's still developing and we feel like you know can add a role in special teams right now. Um Oh and the linebacker that we claimed. He's he's he's a special teams you know he's had a lot of special teams production at Arizona last year. And then Stackhouse is just a you know big body in there is did a good job in Green Bay. And you know excited to have those guys. >> You said you could upgrade with with the five bottom spots on your on your 53. Why can't you upgrade on the practice squad? Why why the dedication to guys that were here? They're they're not better guys out there? >> There's a policy for a question because things have changed in the league where sometimes you you know there was a recruitment process sometimes to get guys from other from other teams and you know there was a pay scale that you could do. You could pay guys up an active roster spot. Um so, when you're looking at guys now that have gone through camp, a lot of them are going to stay with the team because they've been there and they're comfortable. Now, there's always decisions they make, well, maybe the team didn't want back. Um but there's also decisions that you know, is it is it best interest for them? Is there an opportunity here at that position that they might be elevated at some point? Um so, things have changed there in terms of I'd say the 53 cut and then and then organizing that practice squad. >> With the five guys that you swapped out, is that a sign that you're still trying to build depth on this roster even after going through all of camp and preseason? >> Yeah, I mean, I think we're we always are. Um I don't I think you're ever satisfied with, you know, we feel good about our guys, but you're always evaluating seeing where you can upgrade. And if there's a spot we can upgrade, whether it's offense, defense, special teams, I mean, we're going to take a look at it and and and do what's best for the team. >> What's your perception of your offensive line after the emergence of Fernando Carmona? Did you change it? >> With Fernando, you know, I think I think he's done a really good job, Carmona. You know, he's he's um he's everything we thought he'd be come, you know, he's he's tough, he's physical. Um but then he had an opportunity to run with the ones here a little bit in camp and and um you know, I think he's done a nice job with it. You know, there's always things with with every player, but especially rookies that they need to improve on. Um but he's done a nice job. >> Is it fair to say that he was a bit of a pleasant surprise or did you draft him thinking he could be the day one starter? >> Um you know, I I I I like this we all like the skill set coming out um in terms of his size, his strength. Um You know, he's smart, he's tough. You know, he brings a little bit of nastiness to to that group. Um So, you you you never know with those guys. I mean, that's such a um you know, characteristics position where and we've talked about this before with with some of these guys, especially the offensive line. Where there's certain character traits that sometimes make up for some other deficiencies. >> From your perspective, how is how is Cam grown into the role with the new offense? >> I think he's done a really good job and I I you know with with Dabs and and Shea, um you know, I think I think you know, from OTAs to now just in terms of just, you know, protections and and and knowing the scheme and and then just getting on the same page. A lot of new guys here. Um you got to you got a a lot of new players, new scheme. And I think as you see, it's get it'll get better and better here. I think as the season goes on. >> With Chuks Okorafor and Hudson, what what do you feel about OT depth? It's a tough spot to find people obviously, but >> It it is a tough spot. Um but I feel good. I think Chuks Okorafor, talking to him specific specifically, um has done a really good job just, you know, developing here in the past year. and then James, you know, has been a third tackle that that started games before in this league. So um we feel good about those guys right now, Paul. >> His low moment, Hudson, he's all over the place where he had four penalties in 5 minutes of real time. When you see something like that in a guy, uh I mean, what what Carm tell you about that? >> Yeah, I know they have a great relationship and sometimes the emotions get the best of you during the game and um you know, it's something that that he had improved on and and um you know, I had obviously had the conversations with Dabs and Carm on And um and we feel good about uh adding to the roster. >> When we asked you about Will back in July, you said that the best 53 were going to make the roster regardless of position. Is it fair to say you guys determined he wasn't one of the best 53 or was there something that >> that's that's the mindset when you're looking at it, you know, how can we keep the best 53? And you know, I credit to Will though. I mean, Will did a tremendous job for us. You know, throughout OTAs and camp here. You know, he handled himself like a professional. Was always good in the room. Came out every day he worked. You know, but at the end of the day, you know, I wish him the best and we had a great conversation when he left. And and I'll be rooting for him. >> Robert said a couple of times already that right now this is the floor for this team. Is that I mean the expectation for right now for this team is to just continue to get better as the year goes on? Is that how you approaching it? >> I think so. And I think that really has to be the mindset with every team that I've that I've really been a part of is that, you know, you go through camp, you're getting better and as the season goes on, you're getting better. But that's certainly our mindset right now. We we think you know, this this the young players on the team, right? There's a lot of new faces. New scheme. So, I think you've seen the improvements throughout camp and I think that will continue here during the season. >> How's like how Schofield settled in? And how would you assess how how Kugand's done since he's been here? >> Yeah, Schofield is everything that you know, Dave's and Carm said in terms of just, you know, being smart. Um and he brings leadership to the room. You know, he's able to because he's been in the offense before just, you know, articulate to those guys in the room. You know, some protection stuff and I think he's been a huge asset in that room and he's played well. and with Coogs, you know, he's he's done a really good job. You know, we've had him you know, really just at center here throughout camp. There was a you know, a few times here in practice we put him at guard. Um but he's one of those you know, he's a guy too that has played a ton of football in college. He's been versatile. He's played guard at Notre Dame, played center there at Indiana last year. Um but he's done a really nice job. >> Is there a position group that's ahead of where you thought it would be heading into camp? I don't know head is the right way you know I think some of the continuity with some of the players that we acquired from from Saleh's defense in New York. You know, I think they just have a better understanding of the scheme right away, right? So Um I don't know if they're ahead, but you know, they certainly had a better understanding at the beginning. Um so and that D-line group is is it's deep and you know, I think it's going to be the you know, really a strength really on that side of the ball for us. >> There were a couple spots where you ended up cutting a veteran depth piece to keep a younger depth piece. How do you go about developing somebody to be ready to play that haven't played yet and now they're one snap >> Yeah, that's a great question. You know, you have to have those are the tough decisions you have to make and you know, when you when you see a guy developing and you know, you don't want to lose them on your roster. but there there has to be a little bit of balance there, you know, and you know, I think we we brought James in and who's had some experience. You know, I I know Slater got in the game late last year in Jacksonville has had a little little bit of experience. Um but listen, we're going to do our best to to develop these guys and that's why you evaluate every practice, too. You know, you they're you know, some of these guys will throw in with the ones and see how they do versus our defense, too. Um so Um we feel good about those young guys developing and getting better and then if they have to get in the game, you know, to perform. >> When you took this job >> When you took this job in 2025, you said had embraced the idea that this was going to be a hard rebuild. And now less than 2 years later, I think there are 13 players on this roster that were either drafted, signed, or claimed by you. What does that kind of say for where this team was and where it is? >> You know, I don't know. We'll see when we start the season. Um but there there certainly are a a of new players here that we we've added. Um I think there was a you know a thoughtful strategy when you're going through that in terms of you know what you're looking for in the player and also you know you're trying to build a culture here too. So you want the right type players in here. So um so we're evaluating all those things and um you know our hope is it comes together. Um but you know I think we have the the right type of guys in here right now that um you know we're going to compete. >> Do you think the culture here is is in your image yet what what you want it to be when you walked in here? >> I I think yeah I know I I feel good where it's at you know I think it's it's getting there. You know it's that um talk about the standard of of doing things every day just you know the way you work the way you communicate the way you treat people uh you know the way you control your emotions you know all all those things come into play. So no matter what team you have and you you talk about culture it's it's really just how you know how you're going to handle adversity now. So um you know we haven't gone through it and that cuz the season really hasn't started yet. So um you know but that's that's why you build that culture to go through those tough times. >> What's what's the bar for being competitive this year in your mind? >> You know I you never want to you know say well I want to win all 17 games. Every every team does at the start of the season. So you know being competitive you know is just going out there and and and playing to your style. Um and and competing and and obviously you need the the physical talent to compete in this league right? You need the physical traits. Um and you know I I think we have the guys here to compete. And I think we'll get better throughout the season. That's probably a better question towards the end of the season of how we did. But you know it's um a little bit of an unexpected you don't know. We have confidence right now that these guys are going to go out there compete and perform and to win. >> Hadyn really took the snaps in your practice. Why was he the right choice to be the three? >> You know he he he did a really good job just in terms of you know, that quarterback and he's been great in the room. He's been great for the guys in the room.
