He's been doing great work to the side. Um Nick has always had a great sense and I I've always believed this really good players are very in tune with their body. Nick is certainly that he's come back from ACL's before. Um it's disappointing because he came back in camp and was all ready and then when he tried to get out there on the field uh it got stirred up a little and he got he got some tendon tendonitis that often happens in an ACL recovery. Um and so that was unfortunate. We pulled back. We got everything uh to where it was feeling better and then Nick u you know has uh you know kind of got behind this plan of really building them up and then putting them back on the field. So is it ideal? No. Um, but I I I do I I will tell you so long as he responds well, he's been tracking very well. Now, always ramping it up to actual football is a difference. And so, that's the next step. And and we're very hopeful. >> George KD, by the way, looked good on the 49ers practice field. Again, I do believe he will be making that trip to Australia. And it seems like it is trending toward George KD playing in week one. San Francisco finished their initial 70man roster. The final two practice squad spots filled by Kevin Given, veteran defensive tackle who's been a member of the 49ers since 2019. So, welcome back to Kevin Given and Vincent Anthony Jr. He is a rookie defensive end, an edge rusher with a very, very long wingspan of nearly 7 feet, 6'1 plus wingspan for Vincent Anthony Jr. recently waved by the Chiefs. So, the 49ers pick up Anthony to their practice squad that fills it up that they might still make a minor move or two, but as John Lynch said yesterday, they're about to fly to Australia. You've got to have the passport situation taken care of and you have to have the visa situation taken care of. And if you don't have those two things taken care of, then well, it it's hard for the 49ers to add you at this point. I'm sure they can expedite a process, but more or less the 49ers need to have that roster complete or the travel party complete, and they do. And they also have travel plans set. Listen to what Keon White plans to do on the 15 plus hour flight to Australia. >> I don't know if you can OD on melatonin, but I'mma try um take like five melatonin, go to sleep on the plane. As soon as I wake up, I'm taking five more and just keep rolling like that. >> So, the 49ers are flying Quantis. I think the NFL set that up. United's the official airline of the 49ers. I'm flying United. 49ers are flying Quantis. We take off at about the same time from SFO around 11:00 p.m. Wednesday night. The flight doesn't land in Australia until like 6 to 7 a.m. Friday morning. So, you lose all of Thursday flying to Australia because you crossed the date line. And then the challenge is that you got to stay up all day even though you've tried to sleep as much as possible on the flight. 49ers have put a lot of logistical work and thought into this whole process. The Rams are obviously going to try to just show up right before the game and play well, but it's going to be tough because as you can see, this can really mess you up. And I know that the Rams say that they saw success in London doing this last year, but this is a whole different animal. This is a different beast. Longer flight, crossing the date line. We'll see how it goes for the Rams. We'll see how it goes for the 49ers. But the talk in the locker room today was about uh making sure that that a sleep and a schedule is followed over the course of the flight so that the 49ers are in best possible position to recover and succeed once they do land in Australia. Now I was in the 49ers locker room today as I mentioned couple of shuffles there. We saw Debo Samuel has taken Brandon Aayuk's old locker. Now, today is September 1st. Today is the day that according to Brandon Iuk's contract, he was supposed to be due a massive option bonus of about 24 $25 million. But because Brandon Aayuk has not showed up to work, he hasn't even applied for reinstatement, he is not in line to make that money from the 49ers. He remains on the left squad list. Today in that locker room, I got to say hi to Mike Evans, talked to CJ West, and also briefly uh was able to talk to Alfred Collins, who very frankly said that his play right now is not up to the level that he needs to be as he still continues to recover from those offseason surgeries. >> Not where I want to be yet, but I'm strides ahead of where I was. So, you know, we'll keep on stacking days, you know, technique-wise, you know, conditioning wise. So, >> now I also saw Nick Bosa in that 49ers locker room. He did not speak to the media, but we did mention what John Lynch said about Bosa earlier today on KMBBR. Raheem Morris, the 49ers defensive coordinator, then talked about what he needs to see from Bosa for him to play in week one. Bosa's played a lot of football. For me to feel comfortable, it'd be different. It's more about Bosa, right? So, what what does Bosa need? What does he need to get out there and prepare himself to go be the very best version of himself? So, Bosa, you know, got a plan in place and I don't want to reveal it if Kyle hadn't done it. But, I let him do that stuff, break the news to you. What's going on with that? But, you know, obviously they got a real legit plan. We got Dustin Perry, we got Dustin Little, we got Kyle Shanahan, you know, John Lynch, all of his coaches, all hands- on deck type mentality to get him ready to go. Um, so whatever it takes for him to get out there, um, it's going to feel good when he gets a chance to get out there and be able to call those plays for him. >> Now, Raheem Morris is in a very interesting position to to be one of the coaches in this game because he used to be the defensive coordinator for the Rams under Shawn McVey. So, it's interesting to hear Raheem talk about his old boss, Shawn McVey, and his current boss, Kyle Shanahan. >> I mean, you're talking about two of the best minds in football, right? you're talking about, you know, Kyle's been doing such a long time at such a high level and really the Shanahan name, right? Talking about his dad, talking about the lineage of what's going on throughout that process. You know, Kyle, you know, really doesn't get enough credit. Um, you know, all those guys were together with him and then they've gone and kind of branched out and done some really good things, whether it's Matt Laflur, whether it's, you know, Mike Laflur, whether it's, you know, even Shawn McVey. Um, they've explored, they've done different things. they, you know, get a chance to get together and really um be a pain in the neck for us defensive guys throughout the course of of football. So, it's been fun. I've been able to join him and coaching the same sides of the ball, been on the opposite side of the ball. Um it's always going to be fun. It's always going to be good. It's just a matter of who execute that day. So, it's something that we all love to watch. >> Dan Graiano reports that Aaron Donald is unlikely to play here in week one, by the way, for the Rams, but it's still on the table. Week two or three is more likely for Aaron Donald's return. The Rams don't fly out, as I said, until much closer to game time. So, I guess there's a longer decision-making window there. Although, even if the Rams flew out early, you could always fly Aaron Donald out in first class commercial a little bit later if he didn't want to go to Australia. But the problem is that the 49ers have practiced with their football team over the course of this next week. So, they're going to want the entire travel party to be with them, including Nicabosa, including George KD, so they can get all of those practices in in the Australian time zone. One more nugget from the 49ers locker room, and I'm going to play the full interview from Keon White, but just wanted to provide a little bit of background context. Remember, he was shot in what was reported to be the ankle following the Super Bowl this past season in San Francisco. Turns out that he was actually shot in the foot, obviously fractured his foot. He talked about his recovery. He talked about the actual shooting. Just listen to Keon White discuss that incident publicly for the first time. And then you can listen to Keon White in his full interview. >> Oh man, I got shot. So yeah, it was gunshot to the foot. Uh broke my Taylor's bone. Um so I had to have surgery. Two screws in there. But yeah, brush it off. literally was making jokes as I was going to the hospital. So, I really don't be too serious. >> And then screws. Did they get removed or they >> No, they're still in there. So, two small screws like in my ankle. So, I got screws in each ankle now. So, I'm symmetrical. >> Were you fearful for your life in this incident? >> No. The funny part is I was actually the one calming everybody else down. I don't really take a lot of things seriously. So, like I didn't know I got shot till like 5 minutes after I was walking around. So, it was cool. At what point this off season were you fully back and and ready to go? >> Um to be honest, it's still an ongoing thing. Uh still dealing with my ankle and everything like that. Uh recovering, just have to take myself a day at a time, but I feel pretty good right now. It was like a touch and go situation right up to the beginning of training camp. For real. >> How do you feel about your position group right now? You guys going through some injuries? >> Um I think injuries is a part of the game. You just got to roll with the punches and whoever's up, we have confidence in in the guys to to go out there and do the job or else they wouldn't be on the team. >> What's your plan for the flight to to get rest and not feel crappy when you get to Australia? >> I'm about to take like I don't know if you can OD on melatonin, but I'm going to try um take like five melatonin, go to sleep on the plane. As soon as I wake up, I'm taking five more and just keep rolling like that. What was your first reaction when you heard you guys were going to Australia? Now that it's here, how do you kind of feel about it? [snorts] >> I'm excited. Uh, so this is my third uh international game. I've done Germany and I've done London. It's always cool to go out to another country, go experience those fans. Um, sometimes they don't really know about football too much, so they're just cheering for everybody, but like it's still cool to just interact with another culture. I love to travel and so you just take advantage of the opportunity. What what kind of message can [clears throat] you got from the coaches, training staff, things like that about you know hydration, just all the different things that you have to do when you are taking such a long flight and adjusting your >> DP gave a whole 30-minut seminar today about what to do. So about how you can sleep on the plane um either stagger it or try to stay up for a little bit then go to sleep. Um once once we get there um it'll be in the morning so try to stay up throughout the day. Like I said, I like to travel, so I'm familiar with like that first day is super crucial to really stay up that whole day and force and push through. And so just trying to do that season last year, your first time kind of actually being able to be here at the start and go through everything. How much different does it feel this season with the 49ers? >> Oh, shoot. I was off all I wasn't here all OTAAS cuz I was just trying to get the ankle right. So still coming kind of coming back and and working with the guys feels like in the middle. Um but it's been cool. So same system. This is actually the first time ever in my whole career playing football that I've had the same coach twice. And so, um, cool knowing what the guys want and kind of the expectation and already having that established. So, it's been cool. >> Getting through that first day. Uh, are you a coffee drinker or what's the plan going to be to try to stay awake? >> I'm an experienced guy. If I'm up uh walking around just going to go do stuff like I'll be up like just go explore like we'll have meetings and everything like that but once I do that I'm out exploring uh Melbourne and and getting around town. I think on the flight I'll just go like look up a bunch of Tik Toks for real. It'll tell me what to do. I'm a I'm a very impulsive guy. So like whatever calls to me I don't know. I might make ride public transportation and wherever I end up I end up seeing from Nick mostly behind the scenes. Um, Nick is just taking it dayto-day. So, um, I know he really wants to be out there. He's really, uh, working to get back and we'll just see where he, uh, lies. Can >> Can you describe the nature of the injury that you had to get through and just the surgery that that you required? >> Oh, man. I got shot. So, yeah, it was a gunshot to the foot. Uh, broke my Taylor's bone. Um, so I had to have surgery, two screws in there. But yeah, brush it off. Literally was making jokes really don't be too serious. And then screws. Did they get removed or they around. So, it was cool.

title: How will Packers handle Josh Jacobs' ongoing legal situation? | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: All right, the Green Bay Packers, they have an issue at running back Josh Jacobs on the commissionerexempt list. Brian Goodyunst, the general manager of the team, addressed reporters yesterday. And look, there's a lot of uncertainty and I've got a little something to add about what I've learned because we don't know whether or not Josh Jacobs will be reinstated before the criminal prosecution ends. It wouldn't be unprecedented if he was, but the general rule is you're out until the case is over. Here's Goodyakun from yesterday on if he thinks that Josh Jacobs will play for the Packers in 2026. >> I think that's to be seen, but like I I'm certainly hopeful that he will and certainly would expect that. Um but we're going to let this process play out and we'll be prepared either way. >> Is there any scenario in which you guys release him? Yeah, I mean I I think we'll let the process play out um you know before we make any kind of those decisions, but um you know um we'll see. >> Has part of that process been you seeing the video that >> we have not seen the video? Again, that's those are legal things going on right now. Um so we'll let those play out, you know, um that's really not, you know, for us. Um, but in the appropriate times if those if that those things u become available, we'll we'll figure that stuff out when that time comes. >> Now, this is one of the key differences between seeing quotes on social media and actually having a chance to digest the full clip. My read on this, they're bracing for the possibility of that video coming out and then having no choice but to cut it. That's my read on it. >> Yeah, I hear you >> hearing the whole thing. >> Y >> right. I locked on to a tweet that I saw and multiple people had tweeted this the answer about seeing the video. But when you put that with what he said when he was asked, "Will you cut him? Will he be on the team? You throw it all together, they know what happened with Ray Rice 12 years ago. >> Yeah. Right. >> They are keeping the possibility alive that they may have to once that video is out there, they may have to cut him. And that may explain why they haven't seen it. You know, my reaction when I saw the tweet that they haven't seen it, well, why the hell haven't you seen it? He's your employee. It's from his surveillance system at his house. He's turned it over to the authorities. It's part of his case file. The league and the Packers would have every right to say, "We need to see this. You're not playing again until we see this." And it reminds me of an argument I had with somebody from the league office over the Ray Rice tape. 12 years ago in August, I said, "How have you not seen the video?" "Well, we we don't have access to it. We can't make his lawyer." Yes, you can. You can make the lawyer give it to him. You say he's never playing again until we see the video. He owns that video. It's in his case file. It's part of the evidence in his case. He tells the lawyer, "I want to see the video." And they said, "No, we're not going to do that." I said, "Well, okay. If you don't get it, TMZ is going to get it." And they did. >> So, that video is going to get out there at some point. >> And I think the Packers kind of don't want to see it because they don't want to see it and think, >> "Yeah." >> Yeah. >> And and then have to sleep with one eye open worrying about the video coming out and then they're going to have to cut him once the video is out. What What a dilemma that would create. We see this video and we know I'm not I don't know what the video shows. I'm just reacting to the clip that we just saw. We see this video and we know, oh this gets out. Yeah, we we can't we can't. And then we're like, well, we're going to keep him until it gets out, but we're bracing for it to get out. And the moment it gets out, we're going to keep him and then we got to deal with the But you saw the video. Why'd you keep him? So, we're we don't want to see it. >> I think that that that may be the message from the Packers. Not we can't get access to it because bologoney you can. We don't really want to cuz we don't like what comes next depending upon what it shows. >> Yeah. No, I think there is a little bit of ignorance is bliss there. I mean, I'll be like, "Hey, hey, wait. No, I don't want I don't I didn't see it yet. I don't know where it is." No. Uh but but yeah, I'm sure they don't want to see it to this point. You're right. They're going to let it play out. We'll see where it goes. It's a big deal. It it is a big deal. We're talking about Green Bay. It's a damn good football team. And I think on top of that, you know, they're they're a team that yes, runs the ball. We know Laflur from the Shanahan McVey coaching coaching tree. So he believes in that and they don't have a running quarterback. So it's really about traditional running game. They can't like, oh, hey, our guy our quarterback will help out the running game a little bit because you got to account for him. Jordan Love's not that guy. He's pocket passer. That's who he is. So the traditional running back is very important to the Green Bay Packers. And then so you don't have Josh Jacobs and now they're having to put all their eggs in the Marshon Lloyd basket and he's really talented. They like him a lot. I know that. But damn, he hasn't been able to play or stay healthy. So that's going to be risky in itself. And we know it's a big year for Green Bay. Um so yeah, I'm interested to see where this goes. But Josh Jacobs is is certainly a big part of their success when he's out there. >> And let me just say this, too. I don't want us to lose sight of the fact that this all arises from an allegation of domestic violence. And if that occurred, it is reprehensible. If that occurred, there should be appropriate punishment. If that occurred, Josh Jacobs deserve every consequence that he gets. The problem is we have to talk about it in these terms because that's how the NFL handles it. That's how the teams handle it. They allow it to become part of a player's availability. We don't know how much time he's going to miss on the paid leave list. We don't know what the Packers are going to do. So, the whole thing gets jumbled together and it's easy to become desensitized to the reason why we're having the conversation. The reason we're having it is he possibly did something >> for which he should be punished. He possibly did something for which he should never play in the NFL again. If it is a privilege and not a right, then maybe he shouldn't. And he possibly did something that when we see it on video, we will say, "Holy shit." So, I don't want to lose sight of that. We're forced to have these conversations about when he's going to play. And I got all the fantasy football people saying, "Well, how long do you think Josh Jacobs is going to be out?" Hey, Josh Jacobs is on the board in round nine. How long do you think he's going to be out? I got a phone call. Somebody in the media called me up the other day. Hey, how long is Josh Jacobs going to be out? I mean, they force us to think that way. Let's not lose sight of the reason why we're having the conversation. >> Yeah. No, I hear you there. I I do. I do. It's it's certainly if if it's bad and whatever, we'll be here to tell you it's bad and get on them. It's just it's a tough thing and you don't want to rush your judgment as you've heard me say a million times before too. You know, it it's it's one of the scariest things about our job, this type of subject. And I've had experience through my playing days into my media days to go, this is one where, you know, you can't just believe everything you read or see sometimes, and you just got to wait for the facts to come out. And that's where, yeah, guys like you and me are in a little bit of a predicament talking about this stuff. >> And I know I got one more thing to say, Gary. I know that my viewpoint on what Goodikun said could be viewed as cynical. And people will say to me, "Why are you so damn cynical about the NFL and its teams?" And my response is, "I've been doing this for 25 years." That's why I've seen it all. And I've learned, as you're saying, there's a big difference between what we see, what they tell us, and what goes on behind the curtain. And we've we've we've seen it play out so many times. We all should be cynical. We all should understand. Totally. It's a magic trick. >> Totally. >> That they they present something to the world that is not the truth. It happens all the time at every team. So, we should all be cynical about it. >> No, we we we should and and we can't always take it for what it is because as I've told you in in in years past and everything there, even in my experience as players, right? You know, oh, player got arrested. Player got arrested. Oh, wait. He did do something bad. Okay. Yeah. Damn. Okay. Good thing he got arrested and he's off our team. wait player got arrested and then we find out and go oh he's just was arrested because he was a big you know big black strong guy or whatever else and he actually wasn't in fault at all. So that's where again it's dicey and I don't know what it is here but again we will give the appropriate reaction when we know exactly what the hell went on here. Hi it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. Hit subscribe for the latest news and analysis from Pro Football

title: Vikings add veteran presence to practice squad in LB Kyle Van Noy | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: Wednesday edition of PT Live. We're going to take a little tour of the NFC North. Some news that emerged late last night. Multiple reports. Kyle Vanoi expected to join the Vikings practice squad. He would be reunited in Minnesota with Brian Flores. Won a couple of Super Bowls with Flores in New England. Was with him in 2020 in Miami. Now for the third time, they'll be together. And when you consider that intricate, complicated defense, you bring in a guy that knows it well, a guy who still has some gas in the tank at 35. And you know, they're flirting with this idea still of bringing back Harrison Smith. And maybe maybe Vani arriving is the indication that Smith isn't going to come back, that they want like a veteran leader on that defense and maybe that becomes Vanoi. >> Yeah, I I I can see it. I mean certainly Vanoi is still a a good football player. He is. It's not like you watch Ravens last year and go, "Oh man, he's, you know, really at the end here. He's the weakly w weak link on the defense." He still can fit a role now. You know, whether he's a starter or not. Okay. Yeah. But for that defense, like you've talked about, it is complicated. And Flores values those pieces that you can move around. Vanoi can do everything. He's still got some value as a pass rusher. plays the run really well. You can stand them up at linebacker and trust them into pass coverage and do that. So, they're not overwhelmingly talented at that edge position. It sounds like Dallas Turner had a really good training camp and they're expecting something big from him. But, you know, as you know, you know, you look at them and go, "Oh, okay. He's on one edge. He's kind of unproven commodity still. We think he's a good player, but can he be a first round star like, you know, we thought or they thought he could be?" And then the other guy on the other side, Van Ginkle, there's not a lot of great depth and talent as far as pass rusher there. So, I can understand them, you know, having a need and wanting Kyle Manoi. >> And they thought they had something with Jamal Adams. He suffered that torn quad tendon against the Giants in the first preseason game. And that was that. >> Yeah. for unfortunately uh what would have been and was shaping up to be kind of a a a return a resurrection year for Jamal Adams. He's had several difficult years after suffering a torn quad tendon. He said it took him multiple years to come back from it. It's just a shame and the Vikings are kind of putting their arms around him and they're going to have him around the team all year long. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. title: CJ Stroud must prove he deserves a big-time contract from Texans | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: BFT Live Wednesday edition, September 2, one week away from the start of the regular season when we will see Sam Darnold and the Seahawks take on Drake May and the New England Patriots. Drake May, a guy from the class of 2024 who is destined to unlock a massive new contract after this season. There are three quarterbacks taken in the top five of the 2023 draft. Actually, the top four. Three out of four picks were quarterbacks that year. One, Anthony Richardson has been benched. Another was benched. Bryce Young, the first overall pick, he was benched and then he was unbenched and now he's the starter of a playoff team from last year, even though they weren't 500. And CJ Stout has been the best of all of them from a team standpoint, but there are real questions about what his ceiling is. And that has delayed >> Yeah. >> the the number the Texans want to keep him, but when you have a $45 million range now among veteran quarterback APY, where does he land? Well, right now, a hell of a lot lower than he'd like to. So, he's got to play well this year to try to push himself higher on that scale. And that's the reality for CJ Stout. And Bryce Young's kind of in that same spot. They seem like they want to keep him, but where does he fit and where they'd put him now? Well, after this year, maybe he earns a higher spot. So, I see the connection between the two of them. With Richardson, it's just finish this year in Indianapolis and go somewhere else. >> Yeah, that that's right. But yeah, it's odd in that you don't often talk about a guy who's going to year four and go, "Hey, the his rookie year was actually the best year of his career." And that's odd. And that's kind of where you are with CJ Strad. You know, I I look at CJ Strad and in this situation here with Houston and extension and all that, and I want to go, why why even want it right now? Go out and prove yourself. I mean, you go out and prove yourself and play good this year and you guys get deep into the playoffs that you have that kind of a quality of team there in Houston, you're you're going to be paid closer to the top of the market. And I think if you take something right now, I don't know, unless Houston, you know, just wants to save face and make it look like, oh yeah, we made the right pick and he's the franchise, you know, I wouldn't think he's going to be anywhere to near the top of the market. There's just too many questions. So, that's where it's different. You know, Bryce Young situations. Yeah. interesting in itself. I know. Listen, people down there before the year started last year. They were convinced he was not the guy. I don't think we got the guy. That's what they said. Then they go to the playoffs. Now they got to put their the old toothpaste back in the toothpaste holder as that that Aggie said. Only an Aggie could say something like that. And and and yeah, I mean only I mean a Longhorn is just too smart. We would never say that, but an Aggie would. But yeah, so now they're in a little predicament. But but either way with this Houston situation, you know, I I um I guess there's a part of me that's a little surprised that we're even here in this conversation. If I'm Houston, I do want to see him more. I like him a lot. He's got all the potential and the things we like to be the future of the franchise. And if I'm CJ Stra, I want to go out there and play good. So, I'm I'm making north of 50 million a year like the other good quarterbacks in football. And that to me is, you know, a little bit of the predicament they're both in right now. Let's hear a little bit from Nick Cacerio, GM of the Houston Texans, on where the contract negotiations currently stand with quarterback CJ Strad. >> You know, we've had productive discussions. I would say the reality is we'll get it figured out before the season starts and if we don't get it figured out before the season starts, then something we address in the offseason. So, you know, whenever it happens, it happens. Yeah, every situation is going to be different. So, um you know, we've done some deals during the season. I would say look once players get into the season sometimes they want to focus on football and don't want to worry about dealing with the contract and you maybe it's not as clean as some others. So again we've done it both ways. We've done deals before training camp, we've done deals during training camp, done deals during the season. So you know we'll see how this goes. I mean it's just my sense. I mean I could be wrong. I mean I'm wrong a lot. So kind of see how it goes. Um kind of keep working keep working through it. I think the most telling part of what he said is if we don't get it done before the season, we won't do it until after the season. That frames this exactly the way that I think you and I believe it will be framed. Hey, you want to take what we'd be willing to give you right now, we're happy to give it to you, but you probably don't want to take it, right? We're happy to give it to you, but it's it's a number that reflects where you are right now. you want to take this season and you want to try to push it higher, >> go for it. Yeah. >> Good problem to have. Yeah. >> If you play so well that we take whatever number, and I'm not even going to put a number out there because somebody's going to think that I'm suggesting that's the number. Whatever the number is right now, that surely isn't enough for CJ Strad to say yes or we'd already have a deal. Whatever the number is now, you can move it higher. And I saw that someone, and this is one of the realities of social media, and it can be someone who doesn't know Jack diddly squat, who throws a number out there. And this is why I'm being careful because number one, I don't know Jack diddly squat, and number two, I don't want to throw a number out there. But I did see that somehow this idea got traction that he wants 70 million a year. And my first reaction was no, he doesn't. There's no way that anyone with any ounce of sanity or intelligence would assess CJ Strad as a guy worthy of 70 million a year. I think some of it is based on experience, some of it is based on, you know, um what their track has been to that moment. You know, you know, some guys play a lot more in college than others. Some guys have a ton of experience in the NFL when they get here. I think every player is a little bit different. I think you know, as a as a organization, we have to look at that every organization really specifically and not just have a general, okay, he needs this many days to get ready, he needs this many practices. I think every player is a little bit different. So, I think you just take every situation and and assess it. >> Last one, you have a player like Nick Allegretti who has a lot of experience, but most of it is spent been spent at a position like guard. Um you know, I think you go you first of all you look at Do you think the guy can handle it mentally and do you think the guy can you know, can kind of be that you know, the what what all that center brings with it in terms of responsibility and duties and and Nick is absolutely that guy in terms of you know, intelligence and leadership and toughness and he's he's at what it's all about when you talk about an offensive lineman. Uh very excited about the athlete and the overall skill set. Um I I would say that he has um like a certain maturity to his game that a lot of rookies don't have and uh feel like he's very ready to contribute. >> Lance >> Hey, how you doing? >> Um kind of a I guess a procedural question that can be hard to answer generally when so specific, but when you kind of make a decision to release a vested veteran cuz you know, there's maybe an IR move coming later and you're going to bring him back. Every situation is a little bit different and every player is a little bit different how you um you know, assess how to how to handle that situation is different for every guy, honestly. Um it really it's it's it's not an easy conversation to have. It's not an easy decision to make and you try to you know, always think about what's best for the player and how to how to do what's best for him in every situation. So. >> And then of course, we always look at the the NFL calendar as like dates, right? Does it change those those the gauging of interest around the NFL after cutdowns happen or does that trade gauging I guess for to to repeat the term over and over again continue even though we've kind of entered a new phase of the of the calendar? >> Uh I guess it it probably um it there's I feel like that it really ramps up the conversation and the dialogue really ramps up as you get into those couple of days prior to cutdown. Um I guess it probably slows down to some degree, but I I think you're always you know, we we don't close up shop, you know. You uh you're always open and you're always, you know, dialogue's pretty constant. I would say that it does in those three or four days prior to cutdown really ramp up and, you know, we we had tremendous, you know, dialogue around the league and a lot of really um you know, substantive conversations and um yeah, but to to answer your question, it probably does uh taper off a little bit once that the dust settles on on cutdown, but you're always kind of you always have feelers out and you're always kind of having those conversations year-round, you know. Yep. >> Lance, with a guy like Tanoa Tongiai, obviously you sign an undrafted rookie cuz you think he can make an impact at some point. When over this summer and this spring did you realize he could make an impact this year on the 53-man roster? >> I guess it probably during over the course of August, you know. So, I would say over the course of August during the preseason he really started to um show us a lot of positives. >> For you all in the front office, how much does implementing David Blough scheme impact how you evaluate offensive lineman and their fit in the system? >> I think it's a you know, it's a it's a it's certainly a consideration always. I I do see guys develop and I do I think we do get a good sense of where they are in their kind of in their trajectory. >> You guys signed two tight ends today. Like, what do we have? What are our external options? Do they um make sense to to see if that can help us? and sometimes you feel like we're okay. And sometimes you feel like, "Hey, we we probably do need to go out and see if if this guy can make us better or if if let's let's bring this group in and see if we feel like um this group can help us. Um again, it's every situation, you know, some rooms are um really deep and some rooms you feel like you you you need to maybe see if there's more out there, but um every situation's a little bit different. And you just kind of take them day by day. >> And from a practice to joint practice to game perspective in in camp, how do how do you all do you weigh all of them, you know, kind of equally in terms of performance, you know, you know, practice performance, joint practice, game performance, or does one kind of weigh more than the other? >> I think it all it all is I wouldn't say it's like equally balanced, but I think every day, um depending on what you're doing, you know, there there are sometimes where we have a really um spirited practice, you know, where it's one versus ones and it's um some of those joint practices were really important to see, you know, new match-ups and um so I think, you know, it's hard to hard to be more important than a game, obviously, but I think every day um is really important in the in the big picture. I wouldn't say that um one is way different than another. I think they're all um really strongly considered and weighed. >> Thanks, I appreciate it. >> All right. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it. >> What time are the practices going to be tomorrow?
